chapters.html:
Chimera Park Grand Opening Dear Citizens of Okhema, We invite you, along with your friends and family, to join us for a day filled with games and fun. Come experience our themed attractions and meals, and even have a chance to play with the little Chimeras! Throughout the opening month, we’ll also be joined by some of the most beloved Chimeras from the hit show The Awoo Firm. We look forward to welcoming everyone with excitement! —The Awoo Team Mydei glances up from the pamphlet to the girl before him. “What am I supposed to do with this information?” he asks. Hyacine brings her hands together. “They are hiring part-timers to play as mascots in the park,” she replies. Mydei blinks at her, cocking his head to the side. “Yeah…?” Hyacine’s lips curve up in a grin. “Me, Rice, and Ciphy are going to apply for the position.” She pauses, shifting her weight from one foot to another as if she knew way too much. “We were wondering if you’d like to come with us?” Mydei frowns. Why would he? Sure, he loved the cartoon and its characters—the Fig Stew charm on his phone was just one of the many pieces of merch he owned. But working as a park mascot sounded like a hassle. “I’m not intere—…” “Employees get yearly VIP park passes and can interact with the Chimeras as much as they want. Plus… we’ll receive special merch autographed by The Awoo Firm writers,” Hyacine says smugly, as if she’s striking an irrefutable deal.

Damn. She’d make a fine businesswoman someday. Mydei stops in his tracks. It isn’t hard to see he’s clearly interested—he bites his lip. “… Fine,” he concedes, successfully lured in. Hyacine giggles as they discuss where to meet for the audition that weekend.

҉ ✼

The part-time job, Mydei finds out, is rather simple. Not many people were interested in working as mascots under the scorching sun of the Month of Freedom. So when a group of high schoolers shows up for an interview, the manager—who introduced himself as Mr. Reca —almost drops to his knees in relief. The mascot show only runs on Sundays for about thirty minutes. It involves some dancing and miming along to recorded music and the park’s fanfare. After the show, the performers can interact with visitors, take pictures, and even accompany guests to attractions if they wish. Each of the girls, along with Mydei, has their measurements taken. After a brief quiz, they are assigned their respective Chimeras. They also receive a digital manual on how to behave around children and what actions are forbidden. Hyacine is assigned Krenabis, Castorice gets Butterfly Cake, Cipher receives Master Cat-Thief, and Mydei lands Fig Stew. What a coincidence—the only Kremnoan employee gets to play the Kremnoan Chimera. On the first Sunday, Mydei arrives an hour early to pick up his costume. Castorice is already there, feeling a bit anxious since she’s not really used to interacting with crowds. Mydei isn’t exactly thrilled about the idea either, but his interest in the reward speaks louder. They both enter the changing rooms and stare in confusion at the Chimera standing in front of a mirror, taking a selfie with a phone. Mydei and Castorice exchange glances. “Um… Excuse us…?” Castorice asks tentatively, her hands clasped awkwardly in front of her. The black-and-red chimera turns toward them, placing a paw on its hip. “Oh. Hello.” Its voice is monotonous, almost uninterested. It puts the phone down on a table and extends a paw towards them. “I’m… what’s the name again?” “Gummy Roll,” Mydei observes, recalling all of the characters by heart. This seems to enlighten the memory of the person in the costume. Its large, round plush head nods. “Oh, that’s right. Nice to meet you.” Well, it seems their manager got another person hired at the last minute. As Castorice and Mydei greet the new mascot, Cipher and Hyacine arrive. They, too, look surprised by the extra worker but warm up to them rather quickly as everyone picks up their costumes and heads to the fitting rooms. Mydei can’t say it’s comfortable to wear a plush costume. The body feels like thick, heavy winter clothing, making moving a little difficult. The tail wagging is also a bit inconvenient, tugging at the fabric whenever it sways. The worst part, however, is definitely the head. It’s far too large and can get stuck in doorways if he isn’t careful. His field of vision is also greatly reduced, allowing him to see only what’s directly in front of him. The prizes are worth it, he insists to himself as he walks out of the dressing room in all his glory. “Aw, you look so cute, De!” Hyacine chirps. Her pink chimera costume is the smallest of the group, making her look almost like a cub next to the others. “Imagine if the kids knew what was inside there,” Cipher, now dressed as The Master Cat-Thief, mocks from her seat. Mydei rolls his eyes. It’s a running joke that some children are initially afraid of him at first glance. Once they are all ready, their manager comes to check on them. He seems satisfied with the results and urges the group to pick some accessories for the show and the guest reception afterwards. Mydei takes a pouch filled with candies and lollipops, perfect for handing out to children. There are also some Chimera-printed band-aids, since Mr. Reca guarantees that children always end up needing them in a park. They are then given plastic instruments: Hyacine gets a little drum, Castorice a harp, Cipher a viola, and Mydei a guitar. The mysterious person inside the Gummy Roll suit now holds a flute. The show starts at midday. A large crowd gathers around the main plaza of the park, many shouting and pointing at their favorite chimera as the group of mascots does their best to entertain them. Hyacine is a natural. She waves, throws kisses, and fakes the drum beats with ease. Cipher’s energetic movements attract the more hyperactive kids, while Castorice’s shyness is seen as adorable as she dances with careful, guarded steps. Mydei, taller than the others, makes an imposing figure—his Fig Stew costume and red guitar stand out even from the back of the crowd, turning him into the “cool” Chimera. As for Gummy Roll… well, she’s there, but it's almost as if she isn't, drawing mostly curious or puzzled glances from the audience. After thirty minutes, Mydei feels like he’s going to faint from dehydration. How do they expect mascots to keep interacting with guests all afternoon?

He retreats to a staff restroom, taking a few minutes’ break before he has to go back out. After removing the immense Fig Stew head and pulling the costume down to his waist, he bends over the sink and splashes water on his face, sighing in relief. “Uh… Hello?” Mydei freezes. This voice, though muffled by the door, is oddly familiar. He stays quiet, the water still running down the sink. “Is this really the restroom? Cyrene must have tricked me…” Every alarm goes off in Mydei’s head. The mention of Cyrene all but confirms that the person on the other side of the door is none other than Phainon Khaslana. Under normal circumstances, that wouldn’t pose a problem. Phainon is a classmate of his from high school—they interact ever so often, mostly picking on each other whenever they get the chance. This also means the guy would never leave him alone about the part-time job if he found out. “Hey… I know someone’s in there. Can you please redirect me back to the guests' area?” Phainon asks in that earnest tone of his. Mydei is still panicking silently as he thinks. He needs to conceal his identity; he can’t risk speaking and being recognized. Glancing at his sweaty reflection in the mirror, he gets an idea. Quickly donning the costume and Fig Stew’s head, he straightens up and unlocks the door. Phainon nearly jumps out of his flesh when a tall orange chimera greets him. “Titans!” He clutches his chest, taking an instinctive step back. “…” Mydei stares silently through Fig Stew’s unmoving, happy face—what else can he do? If he weren’t in the costume, he’d be laughing at the scare. “I’m sorry, I wasn’t expecting… a chimera,” Phainon says, now sounding a bit embarrassed. Mydei rolls his eyes, even though the guy can’t see it. He points a paw to his side. Phainon follows the gesture. “Are you… telling me where to go?” He tilts his head, uncertain. Mydei nods, and Phainon finally understands. “Oh! I see—thanks,” he scratches the back of his neck. “And… sorry for interrupting.”

Remaining silent, Mydei crosses his arms. Phainon takes the hint and heads back down the corridor toward the guest area. As soon as he’s out of sight, Mydei finally exhales. He leans back against the wall, fighting the urge to tear off the stupid costume. Of course Phainon Khaslana was at the park. Just his luck. To make it worse, he’s on a date with Cyrene. Even when Mydei tries to escape his one-sided crush, it finds a way to bite him in the ass. What a joyous day for a brokenhearted chimera.

҉ ✼

With the knowledge that Phainon is in the park, it feels like the guy pops up everywhere he goes. He takes pictures with families and children near the Dromases' ranch. A little farther ahead, two figures walk side by side as they watch the Dromas over the fence. One is clad in a white dress, with orchid eyes that twinkle like stars and long pink hair tied in a ponytail. She holds her date's arm, pulling him eagerly toward the animals. "Look at that one, Phai! It's pink—it's so cute!" she exclaims. Mydei hates that he can't focus on what the kids around him are saying. It's as if his hearing has a filter tuned only to their conversation. "I think the golden one is cuter," Phainon replies. Cyrene lets out a lighthearted laugh, as though he's just told the funniest joke in the world. "Oh, of course you do…" Cyrene releases his arm and winks at him. Phainon smiles back, a faint blush coloring his cheeks. Mydei’s heart aches at the sight. “Mr. Fig Stew, what’s your favorite food? When I grow up, I wanna be as tall as you!” A kid suddenly shakes him out of his trance. He turns his big plush head towards the child. While the mascots are allowed to talk to guests, he isn’t confident that the distance between him and the couple is enough to keep him from being heard. After all, he’s been eavesdropping on their conversation easily enough from where he stands. “Mr. Fig Stew?” The kid paws at his fluffy legs, and all he wants to do is run. Before he blows his cover, a paw lands on his shoulder. “Didn’t you know, little one? Fig Stew is under a spell… They lost their voice.” Startled, Mydei turns to Gummy Roll. When did it get so close? Some of the kids around them let out a collective wail. “Whaaat? Why?!” “Is Mr. Fig Stew going to be okay?” Gummy Roll removes its paw from his shoulder and crouches down to the children’s eye level.

“They’re going to be fine. A witch cast a spell on them… but it can be broken with a kiss.” What. Mydei scowls from inside his costume. A few of the kids let out an “Eww!” at the idea. “Ohhh, like in the Clockie movies!” a girl in the group chirps, and Gummy Roll nods. “Then why don’t you kiss them, Gummy Roll?” a boy asks. “It doesn’t work like that. The kiss has to come from someone Fig Stew likes,” Gummy Roll replies smoothly. Mydei is too afraid to look around and see if Phainon and Cyrene are listening to any of this madness. “And who’s that?” another child asks, much to Mydei’s dismay. “Who knows? Perhaps when they recover their voice… We’ll find out.” Gummy Roll pats some of the kids’ heads as it straightens up. “Until then, the curse only lets them say ‘Awoo.’” Mydei’s head snaps toward it so fast his neck nearly cracks. Somehow, he can sense the smile inside that black and red chimera head. The children keep questioning Gummy Roll about the curse, but the conversation soon shifts to another completely unrelated topic. Mydei tries to go along with it as best he can, handing out candies and taking more pictures. He’s almost too busy to remember his earlier worries when a familiar voice reaches his ears once more: “Aw, poor Fig Stew… Isn’t that sad, Phai?” Cyrene’s overly sweet voice makes him wince. “Yes… I hope this curse can be lifted soon,” Phainon agrees, and Mydei's stomach drops. If it depends on who he likes, his curse may as well last forever.

҉ ✼

“What the hell was that?” Mydei demands as soon as he and Gummy Roll are alone in the staff room. He immediately pulls off his headpiece, feeling suffocated after wearing it for too long. His hair is drenched with sweat, clinging to his forehead and neck.

“I was just entertaining them. It’s our job,” Gummy Roll replies, completely unfazed.

Mydei wants to believe this person. He really does. But almost everything they say feels painfully staged.

“Cut the crap. You made sure everyone around us heard it. Do I know you?” He crosses his arms, restraining himself from yanking the chimera's head off its shoulders.

Gummy Roll lets out a dry, humorless laugh.

“Not really. I just recognize a hopeless situation when I see one.” It brings its paws towards the headpiece and lifts it off its shoulders, revealing a mop of sweaty pink hair and a pair of blood-red irises. “After all, I’m pretty much in the same boat.”

She isn’t anyone Mydei recognizes. She simply sets the plush head on the table beside her and combs her damp pink strands away from her face.

“You keep glancing at that nerd even without realizing it. I do the same thing myself—with my dear sister, March,” she explains nonchalantly.

Mydei feels suddenly called out, a chill running down his spine. He didn’t know he was being that obvious. If she noticed, maybe Phainon saw it too? It should be hard to tell where a mascot is looking, but still… this girl nailed it. Mydei tries to play it off.

“What kind of look do you give your sister?”

The pink-haired girl offers him a faint smile in the mirror.

“A hopeless situation, indeed. I’m Evernight, by the way.”

҉ ✼

It’s the final minutes of their first day as mascots, and Mydei almost doesn’t want to come back for the remaining Sundays. After such an exhausting routine—even putting aside the whole ordeal with Phainon and Evernight—he just wants to collapse into bed and not get up for an entire day. The mere thought of having to go to school tomorrow is already draining.

The sun is setting on the horizon, painting the park in shades of orange. Most guests have already left; the few who remain are taking their last shots at the game booths or buying souvenirs on their way out. Sensing there’s not much else for Fig Stew to do, Mydei heads back toward the staff quarters to finally change out of the costume, which now clings to every inch of his sweaty skin.

As he passes the game booths, a sight catches his attention. On a bench near the plaza fountain, a familiar head of moonlight-colored hair is sitting alone. Mydei stops in his tracks. Cyrene is nowhere to be seen, and Phainon looks utterly dejected as he sighs at his phone screen, his shoulders slumped.

A knot tightens in Mydei’s stomach at the sight.

The look doesn’t suit his handsome features. It almost looks like he’s been dumped—which is inconceivable to Mydei. One part of his mind tells him to ignore it and keep walking toward the staff quarters. But the more insistent part—the part that still hopes—wants to approach Phainon and wipe that look off his face. Normally, he would shut down that train of thought as soon as it emerged. It’s not his place to meddle in the guy’s love life, even if he’s had a crush on him for two years. And yet… He isn’t really “Mydei” in Phainon’s eyes today, is he? Clad in plush armor, he’s seen only as Fig Stew. And as a mascot, it’s his job to make the guests happy. Before he knows it, Mydei is already heading toward Phainon. He has no idea what he’s supposed to do, but his feet are moving faster than his thoughts. When a shadow falls over him, Phainon notices a pair of fluffy paws standing before him. He lifts his gaze from his phone screen to the tall orange chimera. “Fig Stew?” he mutters, more to himself than anyone, clearly bewildered. “Is… everything okay?” That’s what I want to ask you, Mydei thinks. But he can’t say it—not without risking being recognized. So all he does is nod with the round chimera head, which only deepens Phainon’s confusion. Mydei can’t speak, so he has to communicate through actions. The only idea that comes to mind is inside his pouch. Phainon watches as he fumbles with the accessory, struggling visibly due to the costume's plush, chubby fingers. When Fig Stew presents him a single chimera-printed band-aid, his blue eyes widen. “Is this for me?” he asks. Again, Fig Stew nods. A little hesitantly, Phainon takes the item and examines it. “Do you… think I might be hurt?” It’s a rather strange experience, having to communicate without words, but so far it seems to be working. Phainon understands what he’s trying to say. Mydei nods once more in silence. Phainon’s bewildered expression softens into something more thoughtful as he studies the mascot. “I’m not hurt… at least, not physically. But I get the feeling you might already know that.” Mydei wants to roll his eyes, but of course, Phainon can’t see. “Why don’t you take a seat? It must be tiring, working in the park all day,” Phainon suggests, and part of Mydei wants to comply. He is tired, even though he knows he shouldn’t indulge in the guy’s company for too long and risk his disguise. Besides, listening in on someone’s private life in secret when you actually know them is, at best, unethical. If Phainon ever found out, it could end what little relationship they have as classmates. Well. It’s not like Phainon actually cared about what he thinks, anyway. The guy has been unreachable for Mydei ever since day one. He’s already stepped into this awkward situation—backing out now would probably seem even weirder. Mydei gathers the costume’s tail and holds it to the side as he takes a spot at a safe distance. Phainon offers a small smile; the earlier melancholy seems to have vanished. “Thanks for being so attentive. That’s the second time today you've helped me.” Oh, right. The bathroom thing. Mydei lets out a silent sigh and gives a small shrug. “Look, this might sound a little strange… but could you hear me out for a moment?” Phainon asks, his tone hopeful. Mydei supposes he signed himself to it. He gives a short nod. Phainon fidgets with the bandage between his fingers.

“I wanted today to be special.” He pauses, his shoulders dropping slightly. “There’s someone I’ve wanted to ask out for a long time.” Oh, by Nikador balls. Mydei was really going to have to sit here and listen to Phainon gush about his undying crush on Cyrene, wasn’t he? He clenches his fists inside the costume, a wave of discomfort washing over him. “…The thing is, I’m scared they might not be interested in me like that. So I always chicken out at the last second.” For fucks sake. They’re already together at school every single day—what more proof does he need? Does he want her to bring him a bouquet and a wedding ring? If his tail were real, he would be batting it in irritation. Mydei bites back a frustrated sound and lets the guy have his monologue. “Sorry, I must sound pretty pathetic, huh?” Phainon tries to shrug it off, though the earnestness from before still lingers in his voice. “Anyway, I thought inviting them to the park might be a good idea. They’re a huge fan of The Awoo Firm. Fig Stew is their favorite.” Huh. Mydei blinks as he absorbs the information. Not once had it crossed his mind that Cyrene’s favorite would be Fig Stew. She seemed more like the type to prefer Cyrup, the cutesy, romantic chimera. Besides, she hadn’t acted all that enthusiastic when she and Phainon were near him at the Dromases' ranch earlier. “So… I was wondering. Could I take a picture with you? Maybe I could use it as a way to… You know, build up the courage to confess.” What the hell. He didn’t need a prop to confess to her—was he an idiot? Mydei has the sudden urge to flick Phainon’s forehead, but not only is it against park rules, it’s also impossible to control his fingers that precisely inside the costume. The only thing he can do is nod again and hold his breath as Phainon pulls out his phone and comes closer, standing shoulder to shoulder with him on the bench. Even inside the thick fabric of the costume, Mydei catches a familiar hint of vanilla—a scent that brings back memories from two years ago. It makes him want to lean into it, but he refrains. He’s Fig Stew right now, and he’s taking a photo with a guest. An infuriatingly handsome guest. “Say cheese!” Phainon chirps, snapping a selfie with them both on the screen while flashing a peace sign. He angles the phone to show the picture to Mydei. “What do you think?” What Mydei thinks is that this might be the only photo they will ever take together, and the realization stings. Phainon may be oblivious to what is actually inside Fig Stew’s costume, but all Mydei sees is a bright-eyed teenager next to a park mascot. Though Phainon’s smile is radiant, Fig Stew’s stitched happy face only adds to its misery. Evernight’s words echo in the back of his mind. A hopeless situation, indeed.

“I know you can’t talk, so I’ll take that as an approval.” Phainon straightens up. He tucks his phone in his back pocket, and as he does, he realizes something is there. “Oh, right. Did I tell you? I won a game at one of the park’s booths. They gave me a monthly pass as a prize. I didn’t even know those existed,” he says. Mydei frowns, lost on why he was being told that. “I’ll do my best to ask this person out. And I’ll bring them over to meet you properly. It’s a promise, friend!” Nikador, have mercy on me.

҉ ✼

When Mydei arrives home, it’s already evening. After greeting his mother, he heads straight to his room and drops his bag at the foot of the bed. The park had employee showers where they could wash up after getting out of costume. His suit would be cleaned and stored there for the week. Before going downstairs to join his mother for dinner, he reaches for his phone, which had stayed securely tucked away in his bag the entire day. The last time Mydei checked it was a few minutes before arriving at the park in the morning.

As he unlocks the screen, a series of notifications catches him by surprise.

Phainon: Hey, Mydei! How are you doing?

The first message was sent at ten in the morning. Mydei frowns. It is rare for Phainon to message him, unless it’s something regarding school. His eyes drift down the chat. —this message has been deleted—

At least three messages have been deleted within the span of an hour Maybe Phainon was reaching out about something and got it solved before Mydei could reply? That seems the most likely explanation. He met the guy after lunch in the park, so perhaps Phainon was busy with something else in the morning. Still, curiosity gnaws at his core. He wants to ask what that was about, but then he would probably need an excuse for why he wasn’t available earlier. Gripping his phone a little tighter, he scrolls down. The next message is from 5:43 p.m.

Phainon: I’ve made a new friend today. Aren’t they cute?

[photo attachment]

It is the same photo Mydei took with him as Fig Stew. Why the hell was he sending it to him instead of Cyrene? Mydei wants to delete the photo—it wasn’t meant for him. Yet the longer he stares at Phainon’s cheerful expression towards the camera, the more a wave of butterflies swirls in his stomach.

No one needs to know he has it saved, right?

After downloading it, he pauses. What can he even say when he’s the one in the costume? So he defaults to their usual dynamic.

Mydei: Are you a baby? Taking photos with a children’s mascot like that.

Mydei almost startles at how quickly he receives a reply.

Phainon: No need to be mean. Just thought they reminded me of you.

Mydei freezes. He can’t be suggesting that he knew who Fig Stew was, right? With trembling fingers, he reaches for the keyboard.

Mydei: What do you mean?

This time, Phainon takes a little longer to respond.

Phainon: Aren’t you both Kremnoan?

“HKS,” Mydei curses, though it carries a veil of relief within. There isn’t much else to worry about when the guy is this dense.

Mydei: Cool.

Phainon: Wow, such a reaction. Careful not to fall asleep.

Mydei: It’s hard to stay awake when you’re the one talking.

Phainon: Oh, really? That explains what happened during our math lessons…

Fuck, won’t he ever forget that? Heat crawls to his face as he recalls those from two years ago. Mydei is too damn tired to think of a way to change the topic, so he texts saying that he needs to go have dinner and leaves the phone on his bed for his own sanity’s sake.

When he comes back, only a single message waits for him: “See you tomorrow :)”

Chapter Summary

Chapter Notes

No warnings for this chapter.

First chapter was a really short introduction, so I bring this as a treat. Enjoy!

Month of Cultivation, 2 years ago When Mydei moved to Okhema with his mother, he didn’t expect a warm welcome at all. Okhemans and Kremnoans were always treated like wine and water—two things that don’t mix well together. What consoled him at the time was knowing it was only temporary, until he finished high school and returned to Kremnos. So he spends the first days of school ignoring the pointed looks he gets wherever he goes. Okhemans may as well believe that Kremnoans eat their own children, and honestly, it’s not his place to change that. After all, Mydei is rather used to being alone, and he can still message his friends at Kremnos if he feels lonely. That’s why he finds himself annoyed when someone approaches him out of obligation. It’s lunch break, and as he gathers his belongings, a silver-haired student wearing glasses and a sympathetic grin stops at his desk. “Hello. You must be Mydeimos, right? I’m Phainon Khaslana. Nice to meet you.” The boy extends a hand toward him, and Mydei scoffs. Such a practiced act. As expected from the class rep. He waves the gesture off dismissively. “No need to force yourself. Talking to me won’t earn you any Good Samaritan points.” Mydei knows he’s being a bit harsh, but he can’t bring himself to care.

Phainon Khaslana is practically worshipped at the school. Everyone looks up to him like he’s some kind of saint, and it’s so fucking weird to Mydei. On top of his good looks, the boy is always in pristine condition—uniform without a single wrinkle and smiles carefully measured. He’s the top student in their class, and all the teachers adore him. In other words, a total nerd. A picture too perfect to be real. The most authentic detail about Phainon, at least to Mydei, is the out-of-place sun tattoo on his neck, usually hidden partially beneath the neat uniform. It can be seen better in PE class, which has Mydei wondering why a boy so worried about appearances would get ink on such a place. “I was just being polite. You’ll scare everyone off with that attitude.” Phainon’s tone is patient yet hollow, though his eyelids narrow slightly. Mydei rolls his eyes. “Everyone is already scared of me. I’d prefer you to join them.” He walks past the stiff boy without even glancing back, already heading toward the hallway. Mydei is not wasting his break with someone who’s just talking to him for appearances’ sake. If he had looked back, though, he would have seen the moonlight-haired student crouched beside his desk, picking up a small item Mydei had dropped in his hurry. Phainon holds it curiously, turning it over in his palm. He can’t help but wonder why someone so intimidating would carry around a cute orange chimera phone charm.

҉ ✼

It only takes the first math exam since arriving in Okhema for Mydei to be summoned to the teacher’s office.

The words “disappointing” and “pitiable” are thrown around repeatedly by Mr. Ratio as Mydei silently listens to the man dissecting every single mistake on his exam. And boy, there are plenty.

The truth is, math has been a lost cause for Mydei ever since they started mixing letters with numbers. He barely scraped through elementary school, and now it comes to bite his ass again without mercy.

“I will assign you tutoring classes,” comes the verdict, and Mydei wants to roll his eyes. He refrains, knowing Mr. Ratio would not hesitate to give him an earful for it.

But which student would be willing to teach him math? Most are either intimidated by him or simply don’t wanna mingle with a Kremnoan more than necessary.

The answer shouldn’t surprise him, yet it does.

As if Mr. Ratio has calculated the timing perfectly, a knock sounds at the door. The teacher calls for them to enter.

“Excuse me… You wanted to see me, Mr. Ratio?” Phainon Khaslana opens the office door, poking his head inside. His blue eyes widen as they land on Mydei, standing cross-armed beside the teacher’s desk.

“Yes. Khaslana, you will be tutoring Mydeimos in math this semester. He desperately needs it.”

What a jab. Well, it isn’t a lie—but did it have to be Phainon? Mydei grits his teeth but remains silent.

Phainon takes the cue step fully into the room, scratching the back of his head. His gaze flickers between Mydei and the teacher.

“Oh… sure,” is all he says.

Mr. Ratio assigns them a study room in the library twice a week, until the next exam period where they will evaluate Mydei’s progress.

The first tutoring session takes place that very same day, after classes.

Mydei has already taken a seat and is fiddling with his phone when Phainon arrives a few minutes later.

“Hey.” Phainon greets, and Mydei only nods without giving him a second glance. He just wants to get it over with and head home.

To his surprise, Phainon doesn’t sit across from him. Instead, he takes the seat right beside him and drops his bag on the table.

“Mr. Ratio showed me your test,” Phainon says. “Didn’t know someone could do that badly at once.”

“Math sucks,” Mydei snarls. Out of respect, he puts his phone away as Phainon takes out his notebook and pen.

“It sounds more like you suck at math.” Phainon points out.

“Whatever. It’s not like those calcs are gonna be useful outside school.” Mydei shrugs.

Phainon’s lips curve upward slightly.

“No way. Tell me anything you like, and I’ll prove math has some use in it.” Phainon challenges, sounding confident.

Mydei eyes him skeptically.

“Cooking.”

The look on Phainon’s face is almost comical.

“You like to cook?”

“Is that a problem?” Mydei crosses his arms, waiting for any snarky comment.

Phainon opens his mouth but hesitates. At the last moment, he seems to change his mind, adjusting his glasses.

“No. But cooking and math are closely linked. Any recipe has measures and portions you must follow. There are also timers, temperatures, and scales.”

“None of those use awkward formulas, though,” Mydei counters, unimpressed.

“Maybe not, but that was not the point. Math is present in every aspect of our lives, whether you like it or not.” Phainon concludes.

“Sounds like you enjoy way too much,” Mydei shoots back.

Phainon scratches the back of his head, a nervous habit by now.

“Well, my goal is to become an engineer, so… maybe you’re right.”

Huh. So nerd boy does have his own personal dreams. Mydei shifts in his seat.

“Are you used to tutoring, then? Spreading the gospel of math and all that.” Mydei asks, propping his chin on his hand.

Phainon chuckles at the remark.

“Not really. It’s the first time Mr. Ratio has asked me. Guess he’s really worried about you.” He replies.

Mydei isn’t ashamed of being bad at the subject, but the thought of Mr. Ratio worrying about it is kind of amusing. The man is known for being rather stoic, after all.

“I doubt you can make me learn anything, though,” Mydei scoffs. He’s already bored out of his mind.

Phainon studies him for a brief moment, twisting a pen between his fingers.

“If you’re so sure, why don’t we make a bet?”

Now that gets Mydei’s attention. He perks up.

“What are the terms?”

“I bet that by the end of our tutoring sessions, you’ll score above 80% on Mr. Ratio’s next exam.”

That’s a wildly optimistic take when Mydei barely managed 20%. Nerd boy must be really confident in his teaching skills. It sounds almost too easy a win for Mydei.

“And what do you offer if I win?” Mydei asks, a skeptical edge to his voice.

Phainon thinks for a moment.

“I’ll do your math homework for a month. And if I win…” He smiles brightly. “I want you to cook lunch for me for a week.”

Given that they have math homework twice a week, and there are five school days for lunch, the deal seems fair enough.

“Deal.”

“I trust you will not sabotage your own test. Right?” Phainon asks, scratching his chin.

“I honor my word. If I actually learn how to solve it, I’ll solve it,” Mydei says, a smirk playing on his lips. “That makes the responsibility all yours, Mr. Tutor.”

Phainon averts his gaze, looking slightly flustered as he turns his attention to organizing his notes.

“Okay… let’s start, then.”

As Phainon begins reviewing the topics from Mr. Ratio's class, Mydei has to admit—the guy is good. His explanations are clear and concise, and whenever Mydei makes a mistake, he patiently walks him through the correct steps until he’s sure Mydei understands.

Maybe it’s Phainon’s genuine enthusiasm for the subject, but soon enough, Mydei finds himself settling into a comfortable rhythm. He doesn’t say it out loud, of course, but every time Phainon leans in a little closer to check his exercises, a fluttery feeling stirs in his stomach.

There’s no way he’s losing that bet.

… Right?

҉ ✼

As the weeks go by, the next exam period draws nearer. Mydei continues to be tutored by Phainon, and the model student never hides his pride in their progress. Each word of praise for a correct answer makes Mydei a little self-conscious, leaving him worried about whether he will truly remember everything when the exam day arrives. Lately, however, Mydei has found himself focusing more on the tutor than the subject. Phainon still sits unnecessarily close, leaning over his shoulder and letting their hands almost brush whenever he points out a mistake. Phainon’s scent lingers in the small room—a soft, vanilla trace that Mydei still catches on his own clothes long after they’ve parted. He may have grown attached to it, as the memory of its owner keeps drawing him back to their private hours in the library. Phainon has also started bringing snacks, insisting it’s no good to study on an empty stomach. He has tried nearly every flavor in the vending machine until finally discovering Mydei’s favorite—the pomegranate one. From then on, he pampers the Kremnoan with it whenever Mydei scores at least 60% on their mock exams. It’s the bare minimum to avoid failing, and still a long way from the 80% Phainon’s bet on, but already a significant improvement. “You did well today, Mydei! Here,” Phainon says, handing him the flavored candy. Mydei accepts it proudly and takes a bite. Phainon watches him with a soft, unreadable smile. “What?” Mydei asks, pausing mid-chew. Phainon tilts his head slightly, his tone gentle. “Next tutoring will be our last.” A muted emotion flickers in the depths of his blue eyes, leaving Mydei searching for its meaning. “I’m sure you’ll do great on the exam.” Somehow, it almost sounds like a farewell. After all, they would have no reason to meet here anymore if Mydei truly overcame his struggles with math. He should feel relieved, but a sense of dread quickly floods his thoughts. If he does well, there will be no more tutoring sessions. The small, cozy moments he’s been sharing with Phainon would be gone. Whoever wins the bet claims their prize, and then… they’ll return to being the model student and the intimidating outsider—two opposites in everyone’s eyes. Before he knows it, he’s grimacing. “Mydei?” Phainon calls, and he nods absentmindedly. “Yeah,” Mydei replies to the earlier statement.

There’s a beat of silence, each of them lost in their own thoughts. Phainon moves first, rustling through his bag. Mydei’s gaze shifts curiously toward it. His eyes widen when a familiar item is pulled out. “The day we met, you dropped this after brushing me off,” Phainon says, holding up the small Fig Stew charm Mydei had been certain he had lost weeks ago. “I wanted to give it back, but you’re not easy to approach outside class.” Mydei accepts the charm in awe. It’s a limited-time exclusive merch—he had stood in line for hours just to buy it. He had spent the last few weeks mourning its loss, convinced he’d dropped it on the way home. It’s still in pristine condition, a sign that Phainon had kept it safe with care. “Why only give it back now? We’ve been having lessons for quite a while,” Mydei asks, bewildered. Phainon’s smile carries a trace of guilt. “I… wanted to keep an excuse to talk to you even after the tutoring ended,” he admits. “It’s silly, I know. I was being selfish.” Warmth blooms in Mydei’s chest, spreading quickly. It is a silly excuse, indeed, but knowing Phainon has been thinking about what would become of them after the tutoring leaves him feeling giddy. It’s true that, in the beginning, he wanted nothing to do with the boy. However, after spending this much time with him, something has changed. Mydei hasn’t stopped to think about what, exactly, has changed. All he knows is that the more time he spends around Phainon, the less he wants to go home. A lump forms in his throat as the realization hits. He has a crush on Phainon, doesn’t he? “T…Thanks,” Mydei replies awkwardly, clutching the charm in his closed palm with a little too much force. “Is this character from a cartoon? It’s pretty cute,” Phainon asks. If he notices Mydei’s sudden out-of-orbit state, he doesn’t comment on it. “It’s Fig Stew from The Awoo Firm,” Mydei says. Phainon seems intrigued. “Oh, I’ve heard about that one. Some of my friends love it. Must be really good if even you like it.” There’s a tentative hint of teasing in his tone, but Mydei simply shrugs it off.

“It is. You should watch it.” “Only if you watch it with me.” Mydei hopes he isn’t blushing. His face feels way too hot. That invitation is… not doing him any good. Phainon’s eyes look like little stars twinkling in the room’s light as the boy stares expectantly at him. By Nikador, he’s lost it. Averting his gaze, he clears his throat. “Yeah, sure.” Mydei will worry about the details later. Right now, all he can think about is going home with Phainon and spending the evening watching his favorite cartoon with him. Whatever might happen beyond that, he slams a stop sign in the back of his mind to keep his dignity intact. “It’s settled, then! Give me your number so we can arrange a day for it,” Phainon chirps enthusiastically. They exchange numbers, and Mydei feels his heart leaping against his ribcage. He’s painfully aware of his own feelings, and although Phainon does seem to enjoy his company, it’s by no means a green light for anything more. As they part, Mydei fastens the charm back onto his phone, brushing it lightly with his fingers. Fig Stew has been lucky, spending all those days at Phainon’s side. Mydei almost wishes the charm could speak, to reveal what it had witnessed. What does Phainon truly think of him? Could he ever let these feelings be known? Mydei wishes he could.

҉ ✼

It’s the day before their final lesson when everything comes crashing down. Mydei and Phainon have been exchanging messages—idle talk about their routines and hobbies, mostly. Then Phainon invites him to have lunch with his friends. Mydei doesn’t know any of them, but he supposes it will not be that bad if they’re not afraid of Kremnos' reputation like Phainon. Phainon has left class early, summoned by one of the teachers. Mydei makes his way to the school gardens, where Phainon said everyone usually gathers. Surprisingly, the group consists only of girls. He recognizes Castorice from their class —a shy girl who usually sits in the back. Spotting him, a pink-haired girl with ponytails waves enthusiastically. “Oh, hello! You must be Mydeimos,” she chirps. “I’m Hyacine. Nice to meet you!” “Just Mydei is fine,” he says, greeting the group. “Name’s Cipher. And you must know Cas, right?” A gray-haired girl says, nudging Castorice playfully. Castorice blushes and partially hides behind her notebook. “U-uh, hi, Mydei…” she murmurs. Mydei almost feels bad for her. He settles onto the grass, the group forming a circle as they resume their lunch. “Phai told us a lot about you! We’re glad to hear he made a new friend,” Hyacine says cheerfully. “Sure, friend…” Cipher snorts, and Castorice immediately brings a hand to her mouth. Mydei arches an eyebrow, uncertain of what that means. “We heard you like The Awoo Firm! Cas and I love the cartoon too,” Hyacine continues. She pulls out her phone, showing off a Krenabis charm—the same edition as Mydei’s own Fig Stew. That sparks a lively banter about their favorite episodes and chimeras. The only one without a charm is Cipher, who chose to sell her Master Cat-Thief. The price had skyrocketed after it sold out, and she preferred the profit over keeping it. “It paid for my driver’s license. No regrets,” she sneers. “Poor Master Cat-Thief…” Castorice laments, clutching her Butterfly Cake charm.

Mydei finds the group pleasant to be around. He was initially worried about being out of place, but all the girls warmed up to him rather quickly as if he belonged there. “Where’s our golden boy, by the way? Kind of surprising for him to be this late,” Cipher asks between bites of her tuna sandwich. “Phai said Rene is coming back today. They’re probably dealing with transfer papers in the principal’s office.” Hyacine explains. “Oh, really? Thought she would be spending more time at Charmony’s High.” Cipher muses. “It’s way too expensive—even with a scholarship,” Castorice replies. Mydei doesn’t know who they’re talking about, so he remains silent as he eats. “Oh, they’re here,” Cipher announces, glancing past Mydei’s shoulder. The Kremnoan turns his head toward the direction of a very familiar mop of moonlight-colored hair. And suddenly, something in his stomach drops. Beside Phainon walks a pink-haired girl with small elf ears. She’s the very picture of feminine grace and delicacy—manicured nails, a ribbon tying her ponytail, and light makeup that makes her orchid-colored eyes glimmer like stars. Normally, her appearance wouldn’t have caught Mydei’s attention—if not for the way her hand rests around Phainon’s arm, as though it were the most natural thing in the world. They walk together, radiating happiness. When the girl's eyes find the group, a smile graces her lips, and she rises on the tip of her toes to whisper a secret into Phainon’s ear. Mydei is almost certain she glances at him in particular, but it’s the faint blush blooming on Phainon’s cheeks that makes his heart clench painfully in his chest. From every angle, they look like one of those perfect couples straight out of a TV drama. “Hi guys! Missed me?” The girl sings as they approach the group. She untangles herself from Phainon, bowing down to give Hyacine, Castorice, and Cipher a hug. “Took you long enough, Peach. Golden boy was miserable without his childhood friend around,” Cipher teases. “I was not,” Phainon protests, settling down beside Mydei on the grass. Even though he’s physically close, Mydei feels there’s now an immense gap between them. “Don’t I know it. Phai still has a phone, and my ears haven’t been spared,” the girl sighs dramatically, earning a pout from Phainon. She then turns to Mydei. “Hey! You must be Mydeimos. I’m Cyrene—it’s a pleasure!” Mydei takes her hand. It’s so small compared to his, a delicate and soft thing he can easily imagine fitting perfectly in Phainon’s. Up close, he catches her peachy scent—syrupy and cloying enough to make his stomach churn. “Hi.” he says, a little out of it. Cyrene doesn’t seem bothered as she continues talking about her time as a temporary student at Charmony High. It was a famous and notoriously strict school. At some point, Mydei tunes out, no longer interested. He’s lost his appetite and just wants to get back to class. “Are you alright?” Phainon asks eventually in a volume only they both can hear, and Mydei has to fight the urge to grit his teeth. “I’m fine.” It may have come out a little too harsh, because it’s the last thing Phainon says to him before they part ways. Well, just his luck. His crush has a beautiful, perfect childhood friend who clings to him as if she owns him —and perhaps she does, judging by how freely Phainon lets her do as she pleases, holding on to her like she’s something precious. The only thing consoling him is that at least he discovered it before making a fool out of himself in front of Phainon. So all he needs to do is swallow those feelings, right? Eventually, the jealousy will fade, and he’ll move on soon enough. To help with that, he’ll put some much-needed distance between himself and Phainon once the tutoring ends.

҉ ✼

Mydei can’t say he slept well that night. He keeps replaying the lunch scene in his head, leaving him feeling bitter and cold. As a nail in the coffin, Cyrene has been transferred to their classroom. From now on, he’s doomed to watch her and Phainon grow all touchy with each other every damned day. It’s not difficult to picture, really: two very good-looking childhood friends, growing together and eventually falling in love. A perfect, cliché romantic story. The final day of tutoring with Phainon arrives. It’s spring, and the cherry trees in full bloom only sour Mydei’s mood further. The color alone is enough to remind him of a certain pink-haired girl. Mydei lets out a heavy sigh. He’s too exhausted for tutoring. He spent most of the night tossing and turning, replaying the previous day over and over in his mind. He hadn’t even replied to any of Phainon’s texts. That must be why Phainon seems hesitant when he arrives—like he’s dealing with a large, dangerous feline. “So… last day, huh?” Phainon says, trying to lighten the mood as he takes out his notes. Mydei is still staring out of the window, his face resting in his hand. “Mm,” he grunts. “You look tired… Do you want to call it off?” Phainon asks, uncertain. “Let’s just get it over with,” Mydei says, stifling a yawn. He leans back against the chair and turns to face Phainon. Somehow, the model student looks stupidly good today. “Okay… then, about that last formula…” Phainon begins, picking up where they left off and explaining how to solve the exercises. Mydei tries to pay attention, but his eyelids betray him. Phainon’s voice is soothing, and his warm, familiar scent only loosens the tension in Mydei’s muscles until he can no longer stay awake. His eyes drift shut, and at last, the tormenting thoughts of jealousy fade into silence.

҉ ✼

Phainon’s accelerated pulse rings in his ears. He had noticed the dark circles under Mydei’s eyes, but since the Kremnoan insisted, he thought it might be better to comply.

He knows Mydei isn’t paying attention—the blond keeps leaning forward the longer Phainon talks, his head drooping. Phainon considers shaking him awake, but stops when Mydei’s head finally comes to rest on his shoulder.

Kephale above.

Mydei is sleeping on him.

Mydei is sleeping on him.

The sight is so adorable, Phainon feels he might burst. Mydei’s long eyelashes flutter as small cherry petals, carried by the wind, settle on his face.

Phainon’s fingers twitch. He wants desperately to brush the petals away and smooth the strands of wild golden hair from Mydei’s face. But what if it wakes him?

Mydei’s breathing remains slow and steady, and against his better judgment, Phainon lifts his thumb to the boy’s cheek, dislodging the petal. He stiffens as Mydei shifts slightly, nuzzling closer against his collarbone.

Phainon’s heart races so fast he fears it might stop altogether.

He has done his best not to reveal his feelings until now. After all the subtle things he’s been doing—learning about Mydei’s favorite show and snacks, insisting on staying in touch outside of tutoring, using that stupid bet as an excuse to taste his cooking, standing far closer than necessary— he was sure that sooner or later Mydei would notice.

The past few weeks have been all about Phainon doing late-night calls to Cyrene, talking about his crush on Mydei and taking her advice. It has become a joke between his friends the way Phainon stares at Mydei with heart-shaped eyes.

Ever since the day they met, Phainon was drawn to the gorgeous Kremnoan boy. Most of the students were intimidated by his appearance—blond hair tipped with crimson, ear piercings, silver chains draped over his pants, tattoos along his body and even on his face—combined with his outsider status and the fear that he might be a delinquent. Phainon, however, thought he was so unbearably hot it made him feel feverish.

The initial dismissal back then had stung a little. Still, Phainon’s gaze kept searching for Mydei at school—always alone, always looking like he didn’t want to be there. Phainon found himself wanting to change that, even if it was difficult given the close-mindedness of Okhema’s people. That was why he waited until he could have a better opportunity to approach Mydei without inviting piercing stares.

He would be forever grateful for Mr. Ratio’s idea of tutoring.

The more time he spent with Mydei, the more drawn he felt to him. He had been afraid Mydei wouldn’t welcome the tutoring, but the boy had been surprisingly laid-back about it after their bet. It gave Phainon the space to get to know him better, all while a quiet longing bloomed in his chest.

Still, Mydei seemed indifferent to everything Phainon did. The only thing that had truly cracked his stoic demeanor was returning the Fig Stew charm.

So Phainon had thought that maybe—just maybe—things were finally starting to shift in a better direction.

And now, with the boy’s warm weight resting against his shoulder, Phainon feels both panicked and elated. He knows it may have been accidental, but still—he wants to indulge in it, if only for a moment.

Leaning back against the cushioned chair, he carefully slips an arm around Mydei’s waist and adjusts his posture so the boy can rest more comfortably against his side. Mydei exhales softly, yet remains fast asleep.

Phainon holds him gently, wishing the moment could last forever. He rests his cheek atop Mydei’s soft hair, inhaling its faint cinnamon scent, realizing how perfectly they fit together —like matching pieces of a puzzle. It feels right.

Maybe Cyrene was right—he should confess soon. He’s been so afraid of driving Mydei away that he’s kept silent. Yet now, finally able to be this close to him… Phainon can’t help but want more.

He promises himself he will confess during their date to see The Awoo Firm. Because, really, isn’t that exactly what this feels like?

Smiling, Phainon has another idea. He wants to commit this moment to memory, and maybe someday, he can show it to Mydei, too. He pulls out his phone and frames them in a selfie, snapping the picture and nearly giggling at how cute Mydei looks, tucked into his embrace like that.

Phainon saves the photo, hoping it will be the first of many.

Around twenty minutes pass before Phainon finally senses Mydei stirring awake. He blinks sluggishly, yawning, still unaware of their current position. Phainon can’t resist a quiet chuckle.

“Morning’, sleepyhead,” he says softly.

Mydei’s gaze slowly lifts to meet Phainon’s. A few beats of silence pass, and then—

Mydei’s eyes widen, and in the span of a second, he’s out of Phainon’s reach. The color drains from his face, his chest heaving like a deer caught in headlights.

…Isn’t that a bit of an overreaction?

“HKS, sorry. I…” Mydei mutters flatly, sounding like he’s done something wrong.

Confused, Phainon tries to swallow the upsetting feeling that Mydei might be disgusted by the situation. Coldness seeps into the spot where Mydei had been pressed against him only moments ago.

“It’s alright. You didn’t sleep for too long.” Phainon says with a smile, hoping to calm him down.

It doesn’t work. Mydei averts his gaze, his voice trembling slightly.

“No, it’s not…” He bites his lower lip, frustration edging his tone. “I should get going.”

Phainon blinks.

“Huh? But we still have time…” He doesn’t mean time for tutoring—just time to talk, if Mydei wants to.

Mydei shakes his head, running a hand back through his bangs.

“I don’t feel well. Sorry.” Mydei stands and hurriedly gathers his belongings.

“I can accompany you—”

“Phainon.” The tone makes Phainon stiffen. It almost sounds like a plea—but a plea for what? “I’ll be fine. Don’t worry about me.”

Phainon does worry, though. He grimaces, watching the Kremnoan already making way to the door.

“At least text me when you get home. Please?”

Mydei doesn’t look back as he grips the doorknob.

“… Sure.”

҉ ✼

After that day, their relationship became only a shadow of what had once been flourishing between them. Mydei knows Phainon is out of reach—he belongs to Cyrene. And he can’t trust his own heart when close to the boy, not after even falling asleep to the soothing sound of his voice. He can’t imagine what he would do if they actually ended up watching cartoons together at his home. So he comes up with an excuse, then another… until eventually, Phainon stops asking. Their messages grow sparse, dwindling down to little more than homework reminders. They still have lunch together sometimes with the girls. With others around, Mydei feels more grounded. If anyone notices the growing distance between the two of them, no one says a word about it. He tries to ignore the hurt in Phainon’s expression. Sadly, he can’t be the friend the model student wants—not when he’s hurting too, stuck on the thought of Phainon’s crush on his childhood friend. When Mydei receives his math exam results, Mr. Ratio wears a satisfied look. He had managed to score above 85%. That means Phainon won the bet, and Mydei owes him a week of home-cooked meals. He wants to follow through. He gave his word. But wouldn’t it be strange to do it in front of the girls… especially Cyrene? It’s not like they talk the way they used to anyway, so maybe Phainon has already forgotten about the bet now that his childhood friend is back to keep him company. And yet, part of Mydei wants to show the results to him. Phainon would surely praise him, and Mydei misses the bright smile that always comes with it. His fingers hover over his phone at the last second before he can send a text, and he curses his own selfishness. He deletes the message. The Fig Stew charm seems to stare back at him in silent judgment, and his heart aches. Mydei tells himself it will get better someday. But as weeks turn into months, and months bleed into years, he still finds himself longing for the days when Phainon’s gaze was only his —even if the boy never felt the same. Graduation couldn’t come soon enough.

Chapter End Notes

Well, so that's what happened two years ago. Don't you love some teenager drama? :´)

Next chapter we'll go back to the present; I'll do my best to get it out until next weekend.

Thank you for every kudo and comment. I read every single one of them and get all fuzzy inside <3

See you!

Chapter Summary

The rumor about Fig Stew's curse blows out of hand. Meanwhile, Mydei discovers that Phainon relationship with Cyrene is in a rough spot.

Chapter Notes

Every misunderstanding is crucial to this fic.

:´)

Phainon doesn’t deserve to suffer like that. The bright, cheerful smiles he used to wear suited him so much better. They were what made Mydei’s chest flutter whenever they were directed at him.

Mydei doesn’t know if he can help mend his heart, but he can at least try to be a better friend during such a fragile moment.

Sighing in his sheets, he wonders. How could he possibly begin to make up for years of stubbornness and cold dismissals?

He turns onto his back, pulling out his phone. Instinctively, he opens the only photo he has with Phainon and stares intently at it like it will give him an answer. To no one’s surprise, it only makes him feel even more guilty over everything.

When he’s about to give up, the Fig Stew charm hovers into view when he shifts the phone slightly, the tiny character staring back at him as if it knew too much.

A very specific memory resurfaces alongside it—and with it, an idea.

It could be a starting point. After all…

He still had a bet to honor.

Chapter End Notes

Everyone saw that coming, right? I swear I did not write an entire fic just to have Mydei say awoo. Blame hoyo and the "Mydei turns into Fig Stew" brainworms.

Thank you very much for reading! Your kudos and comments make my day and keeps me motivated <3

Next chapter we'll take a peak at how Phainon is keeping up in all this mess. See you soon ~
