Chapter Summary

While Mydei is set on amending their strained friendship, Phainon's inner turmoils spiral out of control.

Chapter Notes

We're finally here with some Phainon POV. He overthinks a lot, so be prepared.

“Phainon. Are you paying attention?” It is so rare to hear Principal Tribios use a stern tone that it makes him wince. He finally gazes at her, adjusting his glasses in shame. “I’m sorry, Ms. Tribios.” Ms. Tribios wears an empathetic expression as she looks at him. She leans back in her chair, gesturing toward her desk—and the reason he’s here: his exams from last week. “It’s such a huge drop in your recent grades.” She shakes her head, grimacing. “Tell me, is everything alright? You know you can confide in me.” Is everything alright? Well, that depends. His life has mostly been the same as always. However… The mere thought of Mydei and that mysterious pink-haired girl being together makes his blood boil. Jealousy was, until now, something Phainon had only seen from afar in the romcoms Cyrene invited him over to watch. It had always seemed like a silly notion—that someone could be so deeply affected by seeing their love interest close to another person. That’s why it caught him by surprise how dark the feeling actually was. In two years, he had been keeping his distance from Mydei. There had been no other choice, since the Kremnoan seemed to have started hating being around him ever since their final tutoring session. It squished his heart the way Mydei chose to shut him out without ever telling Phainon what he had done to deserve it. This made him feel guilty over something he had no understanding of. Still, it was Mydei’s right—he had no obligation to explain himself. They were just classmates at best. Even if Phainon wanted more, there was nothing he could do about it. Eventually, he was able to smile again around his friends. The scar was still there, and Phainon thought it might close with time if he focused on other things. So he doubled down on his studies and even started to hit the gym. It helped to some extent. He spent less time moping over what he might have done wrong, and convinced himself he was satisfied enough just to maintain some kind of contact with the Kremnoan at school. It had never bothered him to see Mydei interacting with the girls before, Castorice being the one he talked to the most nowadays. They both were introverts, so it only felt natural. All of the girls knew about Phainon’s crush on Mydei, and they supported him whenever he thought about giving up. “Give him some time,” Castorice suggested. “I’m sure everything will sort itself out eventually,” Hyacine reassured him. “Have you tried getting on your knees and begging for forgiveness, golden boy?” Cipher joked. In truth, he had tried to reach out and ask for forgiveness. But every single time he did, Mydei vanished from his field of vision in mere seconds. After two years, no one comments on it anymore. It is almost an unspoken agreement that the situation will never change, no matter what they say. Two years flew by in that state. Until one day, with only about six months until graduation, Cyrene invades his room in the middle of the weekend. “Phai, hear me out!” she chirps, hopping happily. “Mhm?” Phainon doesn’t lift his gaze from his notebook. The exam period is approaching, and he has been studying like there’s no tomorrow. “Look at me, you dummy!” Cyrene spins his chair forcefully, and he tries to hide his annoyance at the enormous pen stroke he ends up dragging across his notes. “What?”

“Look!” Cyrene practically shoves the pamphlet into his face. He takes it from her, frowning. “Chimera Park Grand Opening?” he reads aloud. Why, in Kephale’s name, is she showing this to him? “Yup!” she puts her hands behind her back cheerfully. “You know who loves The Awoo Firm, right?” Oh. Of course is about that. “I’m not inviting him, Rene.” “Phai…” She wilts a little. Of all his friends, Cyrene has been the only one who consistently insisted that he try to confess to Mydei all this time, without success. “I already told you he doesn’t like me. There’s no way he’s going to accept.” “Phai… you’ve been assuming that without any proof for years!” she whines. “I do have proof, Rene.” The way Mydei looked at him that day at the library still hurts. It was easier to assume he simply wasn’t into guys, and that the situation had thrown any chance of friendship right out the window. Cyrene puffs out her cheeks, annoyed by his endless stubbornness. “No, you don’t! Phai… are you really going to let this drag out until graduation?” “Mydei will probably be glad to never see me again.” Phainon shrugs. “But what about you? Are you really okay with never seeing him again?” This has Phainon thinking. Would he? Until now, he has managed to endure being nothing more than Mydei’s classmate. Somehow, stealing glances at him has become routine. It is almost a vice by now, and seeing the ultra-rare smiles Mydei shows around the girls still has his chest squeezing with affection. On weekends, when he cannot see his face, he always ends up opening that photo Phainon took of them together at the library. And then he spends the day imagining how things might have been if Mydei had ever returned his feelings. “I… don’t know,” Phainon admits, nervously adjusting his glasses. “I think you know very well, sir!” Cyrene says. Her voice softens. “Instead of locking yourself in your bedroom the rest of the summer like the sad puppy you are… why don’t you give yourself a chance to be happy, Phai? Who knows? It could turn into a very romantic story.” “It could also end in irreparable heartbreak,” he points out. Cyrene stomps her foot. “We are already there! Soon there won’t be a heart left to feel anything,” That earns a small laugh from him. Cyrene has always worried far too much about him. Regardless, she is right. What is there to lose if Mydei already despises him? Perhaps he has simply been too afraid of being officially rejected while still having to attend the same school for years. With graduation so close, even if Mydei ends up shredding his heart to pieces, at least he can recover far away from the places that hold their few shared memories. Then, maybe, he will finally gather the courage to delete the photo. “Alright… I’ll think about it,” he concedes. “Promise me, Phai. Promise that you will invite him out.” The girl holds out her pinky. Even after all these years, she still does these childish things. That is only one of the reasons she is such a dear friend to Phainon. “It’s a promise, Rene.” They link pinkies, and Cyrene seems finally satisfied. She winks at him. “Don’t forget to invite me to the wedding!” Though he doubts it, Phainon laughs along with her. Turns out it was hopeless all along. Mydei is not only totally uninterested in him—he is already dating someone else. How could Phainon not have noticed it before? Over the past few weeks, he had been so caught up trying to invite him out that he never even considered the possibility that Mydei might already be in a relationship. Whatever chance he had has been smashed altogether. He feels so hollow that he couldn’t even bring it up with Cyrene yet. His childhood friend is having a wonderful time with her first girlfriend She had already gone out of her way to keep him company for a while on the park’s inauguration day, especially since Mydei never saw any of his messages about it. Phainon knows she would move sky and earth to hear him out, but this time, he cannot bring himself to reach out to her. Funnily enough, the only one he feels he can confide in lately is the park’s mascot—Fig Stew. What a strange coincidence it is for Phainon to befriend Mydei’s favorite chimera from The Awoo Firm. Maybe that’s the reason he feels such a strange connection to the mascot— he recalls holding onto Mydei’s little phone charm for a while two years ago, poking its head sometimes during late-night study sessions in his bedroom. It was the first time he had actually talked to an object. “Did you see how gorgeous he looked today?” Phainon asks the charm as if it could reply. The fact that it cannot is what keeps him going. “I almost forgot what we were supposed to be studying during the tutoring.” Phainon laughs, twirling the small charm between his fingers. “I envy you, little one… I’m sure your owner cherishes you a lot.” He props his chin on his hand, a dreamy look overtaking his features. “I wish he would let me cherish him, too.” The poor charm is forced to listen to every affectionate thought of this hopelessly smitten teenager. Even now, Fig Stew cannot say anything back to him because of its curse. It’s almost as if the small charm has truly turned into a living being—if Phainon did not know there was someone inside the costume. Naturally, the identity of whoever that might be makes him curious. Fig Stew is being played by a real person this time, and the chimera can now comfort him through his frustrated attempts with Mydei. For that, Phainon is deeply grateful. He swears that once things settle down—for better or worse—he will properly thank the kind person behind Fig Stew someday. That small, shy ‘Awoo’ brought much-needed comfort to his scarred heart, even if he is not sure what it truly means. It is Sunday night, the same day he poured his heart out to the poor mascot. Their small adventure in the park earlier almost made him forget the dread that seeps into his mind every time he is left alone these days.

Because every time he’s alone, he thinks about it—and it consumes him. He thinks about the mysterious pink-haired girl. About Mydei. About how close they were that day at school. Phainon thinks he must be going crazy when it almost feels staged—like the girl knew he was watching and chose that exact moment to stake her claim on Mydei. From his angle on the second floor, when she brought her face that close to Mydei’s, it looked almost like a kiss. A destructive feeling nests at his core, threatening to burst out. Why? Why does she get to have him? Who is she? She had never been anywhere near Mydei in all these years. Is that really the kind of girl he likes? Blood-red eyes, black fingernails, and a large black flower clip in her hair. Did Mydei always like gothic girls? How far have they gone already? And that is when things get ugly. Barely seeing them kissing already made him nauseous. If they did more than that— His hands clench into fists, his heart plummeting as a lump forms in his throat while his imagination runs wild. Mydei’s body looming over hers, her arms wrapped around him intimately. Her blood-red irises glow in the dark, mocking him. “A loser like you never had a chance,” the illusion taunts, wearing a victorious grin. It is the first time he ever punches something out of sheer emotion, trying to make the image disappear. His fist slams into his study desk—fortunately—but the same cannot be said for his desk lamp. It flies off and shatters on the floor with a crash. Darkness seeps into the room, along his heart. Fuck. So this is jealousy. Phainon entertains the idea of finally deleting the photo of himself with Mydei. What use does it have, if not to upset him over something that never happened? He tries once, then twice. Part of him wants to hate Mydei—that way, maybe it would be easier to get over the Kremnoan. But as his thumb hovers over the “delete” button, his breath catches. He could not hate Mydei even if the guy stomped all over his already broken heart. One single look into those deep, golden irises is enough for Phainon to forget every cold thing Mydei has ever said to him. It is almost as if Mydei owns a part of him that Phainon can never get back, no matter what. All of this happens during exam season, and it reflects in his grades. Unable to concentrate on his studies or on the questions themselves, combined with a string of sleepless nights, he ends up performing terribly for the first time. “If your grades don’t improve by the last exam period this year, it may be very difficult to secure you a recommendation letter to the Belobog Institute, Phainon.” Ms. Tribios's tone is clearly worried. Oh, right… That had been his goal. Belobog is the dream of every aspiring engineer—they build literal mechas there. Maintaining excellent grades would ensure a full scholarship to college, a necessity since his parents cannot afford college tuition. But even that thought has grown dull lately. “It won’t happen again,” Phainon assures, his voice devoid of emotion. “You don’t look well, Phainon. You should go home and rest. I’ll let the teachers know.” “There’s no need, Ms. Tribios. I’m fine—just a little tired,” he lies, hoping to win her over with a half-smile. Going back to the quiet of his own room would not do any good for his spiraling thoughts. Ms. Tribios still wears a worried expression as she dismisses him reluctantly. His feet carry him back to the classroom. It is Monday morning, just before classes begin. His head throbs, and his body feels heavy as he walks. He feels sluggish and overheated—it is normal, it is summer, or so he forces himself to believe as sweat gathers on his palms and forehead. His vision starts to blur, making it hard to focus, so at first he does not pay much attention to his surroundings. That’s until he hears a strangely familiar voice around the corner. “You’re giving me that funny look again, Dan Heng.” Monotonous, almost bored. Where has Phainon heard it before? Something compels him to stop. Phainon peeks into the corridor and realizes he is in the first-floor hallway, where the second-year classrooms are located. A jolt runs through his spine when he sees her. The mysterious pink-haired girl.

She has her back turned to him, speaking with a tall, dark-haired student. They have not noticed him yet. “They’re still really curious about your relationship with that third-year.” Dan Heng says. Third-year? Are they talking about Mydei? Phainon’s pulse quickens. What is this about? The girl lets out an almost inaudible chuckle. “It has to do with our little secret.” It does not make sense to Phainon. Are they keeping their relationship a secret for some reason? Dan Heng scoffs, shaking his head. “… I assume you’re going there this Sunday too?” “Yes. All my weekends this month have been consumed by it.” She sighs dramatically. Oh… So that’s how it is. Mydei’s weekend plans for the entire month involve going out with her. It should not surprise Phainon—yet it still leaves a bitter taste in his mouth. Dan Heng sounds exhausted as he sneers. “Must you be so secretive about it, even with March?” “No need to give March something to stress her pretty little head over.” The girl shrugs. “I’m sure she’d be thrilled about it, though…” “Some things are better left unsaid, Dan Heng. This thing will only last two more weeks, anyway.” Huh? Did Phainon hear it right? Why does it sound like she’s talking as if her relationship has an expiration date? “… I never would imagine you doing something like that, Evernight.” Dan Heng sighs. Phainon can hear the amused tone in the girl’s voice. “It’s been entertaining, at least.” Entertaining. Going out with Mydei has been entertaining. While Phainon spent two whole years trying to come to terms with being hated by his crush, this girl gets to treat it as something as trivial as entertainment. Phainon turns around so quickly he fears he might have revealed himself to the duo. A few students in the hallway stare at him in confusion as he rushes past them. It does not matter. Even if they noticed him, he is already out of reach as he hurries up the stairs. That girl—Evernight? Is she toying with Mydei? The way she spoke made it sound as if she were planning to end whatever they had in two weeks, laughing about it all the while. If Mydei is serious about her and she ends up breaking his heart… Phainon knows he would never harm another human being, but the thought is disturbingly tempting right now. His dizziness worsens with every step, and he is so lost in his inner turmoil that he can no longer tell where he is. His head feels on the verge of exploding, and if he does not lie down and rest for a while, he might collapse onto the floor at any moment. Phainon finds the first place he can to set his bag down and closes his eyes, hoping the pain in his head will be enough to drown out those horrific thoughts.

҉ ✼

Mydei’s plan begins before the sun rises. He is out of bed at the first alarm, making his way to the kitchen with renewed vigor.

It has been a long time since he last cooked for someone other than his mother. Back in Kremnos, he used to gather his group of friends and make meals for all of them, but there has been no similar opportunity since. He also never mentioned this hobby to any of the girls at school.

Mydei does not know Phainon’s favorite dishes, so he plays it safe with grilled fish, rice, and vegetables for a starter. He also hopes Phainon is not allergic to anything in the dish. Maybe he can learn more about Phainon’s tastes as the week goes by.

When Mydei arrives in the classroom, he is surprised to see Phainon is not there yet. Usually, as class rep, he arrives much earlier to assist the teachers. Well, maybe he is dealing with that right now.

So, without giving it too much thought, Mydei takes his seat by the window and greets Castorice.

“Hi, Mydei.” She replies, but there is something off about her tone. It makes Mydei frown.

“Did something happen?”

Castorice averts her gaze, as if unsure whether she should be talking about it. She shifts uncomfortably.

“Haven’t you heard?” Her voice drops. “Phainon bombed almost every exam last week. Principal Tribios summoned him to her office a few minutes ago.”

What?

“How?” Mydei echoes more to himself than to her. Phainon has been top of the class for years. To do that badly out of nowhere—

Well, maybe entirely out of nowhere.

He is heartbroken because of Cyrene.

“I don’t know either… but he looked really worn out earlier.” Castorice presses a hand to her chest, her brows knitting together. “I was afraid he might faint at any moment.”

Mydei would not have believed it if Castorice were not so earnest. Her concern seems genuine enough to make him shift uneasily in his seat.

Yesterday, Phainon had seemed perfectly functional—or at least as much as his sadness over Cyrene allowed. But he didn’t look that bad. Had anything else happened in the meantime?

As the minutes pass, Mydei grows increasingly uneasy. When Cyrene enters the classroom, she is wearing a grim expression. Her orchid-colored eyes sweep across the room before finally landing on him.

If looks could kill.

Why is she angry at me? Mydei wonders, narrowing his eyes, completely taken aback.

Cyrene shakes her head, though her expression remains stiff. She takes her seat and starts fiddling with her phone until class begins.

Even after the bell rings, Phainon still does not show up. Some of their classmates begin murmuring about what might have happened.

“Isn’t this the first day Khaslana has missed a class in literal years?”

“I’ve known him since elementary school, and this has never happened before.”

“Yeah, dude shows up even during snowstorms. Total freak.”

“He had a bandaged arm too. Did someone finally grow the balls to punch the perfect boy?”

Mydei’s fists clench on top of his desk. Before he can do something he might regret, the teacher for their philosophy class—Anaxagoras—arrives.

The man unceremoniously drops his thick books onto the desk with a loud thud.

“I hope all of you can redirect that enormous interest in Khaslana’s private life toward our upcoming lecture on nousporism.”

The students shut their mouths almost instantly.

It is still not enough to ease the growing worry in Mydei’s gut about Phainon’s—and Cyrene’s—unusual behavior. He can feel a few sidelong glances from Castorice as well, but he does not try to search for its meaning yet. There is too much going on in his head already.

When lunchtime arrives, the pink-haired girl nearly jumps out of her seat and heads straight toward him.

“Mydei.”

Somehow, her stern tone makes him nervous. He looks up at her.

“What?”

“Do you have anything to do with this?”

“Anything to do with what?” Mydei tilts his head, completely lost.

Cyrene’s frown deepens. She opens her mouth, closes it once, then twice, before finally pressing her lips into a firm line and rubbing her forehead.

“Never mind.” She seems less angry now. “Have you seen Phainon?”

“… No?”

It almost feels like the wrong answer, even though he has no idea why. Why on earth should he know where Phainon is when Cyrene is his closest friend? Surely they must be in a rough spot in their relationship, but assuming that Mydei, of all people, would know anything is almost insane. Even Castorice sounds like a better option.

“He’s not answering my calls or texts,” she says.

Well—did she ever consider the possibility that it might have something to do with Phainon being heartbroken over her new girlfriend?

“Stelle said some second-year students saw him on their floor a while before classes,” Cyrene continues. “Then he ran off somewhere else.”

“So he’s still at school, then?” Castorice asks, unable to hide her concern as she speaks from her desk.

Cyrene nods. “I assume so. No one saw him leave through the school gates.”

“Have you tried the infirmary?”

“I did.” Cyrene sighs. “Can you contact Cipher as well? If any of you see him…”

She trails off, placing her hands on her waist, suddenly looking exhausted.

“Just let me know if he’s alright, okay?”

“Of course, Cyrene…” Castorice agrees.

Before turning to leave, Cyrene throws one last pointed look at Mydei.

“You two are going to be responsible for my newest white hairs. I swear to Mnestia.”

What the hell does that mean? Mydei arches an eyebrow as she walks away. He glances sideways, where Castorice already has her phone in hand.

“Cipher said she and Hyacine will be looking for him as well.” Castorice turns to face Mydei. “Are you coming too?”

What a mess.

It’s not that Mydei isn’t worried—he is—but he is fairly certain he is not the person Phainon needs most right now. If Phainon is really hiding, or if something has happened, the best he can do is report it to his friends or the teachers.

“If I see him, I’ll let you all know,” Mydei assures her.

Castorice nods and leaves the now-empty classroom. Mydei exhales heavily, pinching the bridge of his nose.

Where are you? he wonders silently, a dull ache settling in his chest.

It seems his plan to honor their bet will have to be postponed again.

Maybe he underestimated how deeply Phainon was suffering over Cyrene’s new relationship. He gathers his belongings and heads out.

Mydei tries to convince himself that he is not going out of his way to look out for him. It is obviously a lie—he spends every minute of lunchtime wandering through places where he remembers seeing the moonlight-haired student pass by.

When he is certain he has run out of options beneath the courtyard staircase, a familiar voice calls out to him from above.

“Did you lose something today, big boy?”

Evernight. Mydei is not in the mood to deal with her riddles right now.

“None of your business,” he snarls.

Evernight grins as she leans against the stairway handrail.

“Really? I thought I had seen it earlier… your precious dawn.”

Mydei is on the verge of walking away when it finally clicks.

Dawn?

Phainon’s sun tattoo flashes through his mind. All this time—was Evernight talking about him?

“Oh. Something in that oblivious head finally clicked, didn’t it?” she teases, and Mydei is one step away from climbing the stairs and shaking her for a straight answer.

“Where is he?”

“Wouldn’t you love to know…”

“Evernight.” Mydei knows Evernight wouldn’t ever feel threatened, but he is out of patience. The corners of her blood-red irises crinkle with amusement as she looks down at him.

“Sorry. That intense display of emotions is always very entertaining,” she chuckles. “The last time I saw him, he was heading toward the fourth floor.”

The fourth floor? There is nothing up there except the rooftop. Most of the floor is occupied by storerooms and—

The library.

Evernight seems delighted by the shocked expression on Mydei’s face. She lets out a dramatic sigh.

“He looked very sluggish. I hope he’s still in one piece by the time you find him.” She pauses pointedly as Mydei gathers his thoughts. “What are you waiting for, big boy?”

That’s the million credits question. After all, Mydei has just learned where Phainon might be. Wouldn’t the logical thing be to report it to Castorice and Cyrene? They would take care of him regardless of his condition. That had been the plan, after all.

But a small part of him—the selfish part, the one still clinging to a few sweet memories from years ago—slowly begins to override his rational judgment.

Why the library?

He wonders.

Could he be… waiting for me to find him?

He hopes.

A foolish train of thought. The library had never been exclusive to the two of them; it could mean absolutely nothing.

Still, as long as that possibility exists… Mydei decides to see it for himself.

He hurries up the stairs. Evernight waves at him as he passes by, and he makes a mental note to ask about the other things she implied in earlier conversations once everything is solved.

By the time he reaches the fourth floor, the bell is already ringing. Well—he will not be going back to class anytime soon. Mr. Ratio can throw a piece of chalk at his forehead later.

Stopping in front of the library’s large wooden double doors, he pushes them open with a creak.

The place seems empty; it must be the librarian’s break time. Mydei scans the room, confirming there is no one inside.

Is he somewhere else on the fourth floor, then? he wonders, frowning. As he turns to leave, a slight glimpse of an ajar door in the corner catches his attention.

It leads to one of the library’s lecture rooms—one he remembers all too well.

His breath hitches.

Why?

Mydei steps toward the lecture room slowly. He pushes the door open just enough to peek inside.

Indeed—Phainon is there. He is slumped over the desk, lying atop his bag, apparently asleep. His glasses rest folded at his side. He does not stir as Mydei fully enters the room, trying to get a clearer sense of his condition.

Phainon’s face is deeply flushed, his skin slick with sweat, his bangs plastered to his forehead. His brows are drawn together, and his breathing is heavy. Castorice and Evernight were right—Phainon is clearly not in good shape. He must have felt far too unwell to return to the classroom earlier.

Of all the places… he chose to faint right in their old lecture room?

While Mydei desperately wants to know why, there is a more pressing concern. Phainon needs to go home and rest properly instead of worrying all of his friends—and Mydei himself.

He steps closer, placing a hand on Phainon’s shoulder and giving it a very gentle shake.

“Hey. Phainon,” Mydei calls hesitantly, but the student does not budge in the slightest. Phainon remains trapped in a restless sleep, his pained expression a clear sign of distress.

Mydei’s chest tightens at the sight. Is he having a nightmare?

“Phainon, wake up,” he tries again, putting more pressure into his touch.

It gets some response at least.

“…n’t go…” Phainon murmurs through his unconscious state.

Unable to make out his words clearly, Mydei leans closer, worry etched into his features. He is almost certain Phainon cannot hear him, but he keeps trying.

“What are you babbling about? Hey—”

“D… Don’t go. Please…”

Mydei’s heart catches in his throat as a tear slips down Phainon’s cheek, his shoulders trembling. He knows it is about Cyrene. He also knows Phainon has no idea who is in the room with him right now.

If you believe I’m her, will you stop crying?

Maybe Cyrene from the reality can’t return Phainon’s feelings. But if Mydei’s affection can reach him—even for just an instant…

“I’m here. I’m not going anywhere,” Mydei murmurs, lifting a hand to gently brush the tears away. Only then does he realize how close he is—close enough that his lips nearly graze Phainon’s ear.

Phainon sniffles, and it’s a pitiful thing. His skin is feverishly hot beneath Mydei’s fingertips.

“…Mi… missed y-you…”

It’s not meant for me, Mydei reminds himself. It isn’t.

Still, the words that leave his own mouth could belong to no one else. A pained smile curves his lips.

“Missed you too,” Mydei whispers, pressing a kiss to a freshly fallen tear, the salty taste lingering on his lips.

Phainon inhales shakily, and finally—finally—he seems to break free from the nightmare. Slowly, a pair of moist cerulean eyes opens, unfocused at first, then settling on the figure hovering above him through a haze.

Mydei freezes, keeping perfectly still, afraid that any sudden movement might startle him as Phainon tentatively tries to make sense of what’s happening. His eyes blink sluggishly, still heavy with exhaustion, and his rough voice barely rises above a whisper.

“Am I… dreaming?”

Mydei can’t help but wonder who Phainon is seeing through that feverish haze. Judging by the fond look that softens his features, it certainly isn’t him.

If only…

“Think again. Welcome back from the dead,” Mydei scoffs, now certain the other is awake enough to register his surroundings. He takes the chance to straighten up, earning a cute, confused frown from Phainon and silently hoping he hasn’t thought too much about how close they were just moments ago.

The distance gives Mydei room to breathe, to steady the frantic pounding of his own heart.

“Mydei…”

Oh. So he does recognize him. Phainon lifts a hand to his forehead, using his uninjured elbow to prop himself up slightly. Slowly, he reaches for his glasses and settles them back onto the bridge of his nose. “Why are you here…?”

“You gave everyone a scare. Cyrene and the others are looking for you,” Mydei explains softly.

It’s almost as if Phainon’s headache worsens. He casts a sideways glance at Mydei.

“You were looking for me?”

Mydei swallows. There isn’t really a way to deny it, is there?

“Like I said, everyone’s worried,” he replies, hoping it’s clarification enough.

Phainon narrows his eyes toward him. Mydei is starting to miss his slumbering self.

“Right. And you suddenly care about me?” Though it sounds more tired than angry, the bitterness is unmistakable.

Well. Mydei supposes he deserves the suspicion.

He crosses his arms defensively over his chest. He isn’t about to argue with someone who’s clearly unwell. Maybe it’s better to give in this time.

“… Yeah.”

Phainon nearly loses his balance, barely stopping himself from face-planting into the desk.

“H-huh?”

Mydei shifts his weight, feeling out of place.

“Look, that’s not important right now.” He tries to steer the conversation away. It’s not like he’s about to admit that meeting Phainon as Fig Stew shed some light on just how awful he’s been treating him. “You look like shit. You need to go home and rest.”

It takes Phainon a few moments to let the subject drop. He closes his eyes and pinches the bridge of his nose.

“I feel like shit. I think I’ll faint if I get up.”

Mydei shuts down the idea of offering to carry him to the infirmary as soon as it crosses his mind. Not going there now.

Still, Phainon looks pale as a ghost despite his burning-hot skin.

“Have you eaten?”

Phainon shoots him a surprised glance. He seems on the verge of agreeing, but stops at the last moment.

“…I had dinner yesterday.”

Under normal circumstances, Mydei would flick his forehead.

“Dumbass. No wonder your body’s so weak.”

As he says this, Mydei sets his bag down on the desk. Turns out his plan wasn’t completely in vain. Phainon watches in silence as he pulls out a Tupperware and a pair of plastic utensils. Mydei is glad he chose something easy on the stomach, considering how long Phainon has gone without food.

“Eat first. Then we’ll get you on your way home.”

Phainon’s gaze flickers between him and the accusing meal.

“Mydei, that’s your lunch… I can’t take it,”

“I already ate. I made this one for you,” Mydei replies without missing a beat. He’s not accepting any excuses.

Phainon’s jaw drops.

“You… Made this for me?” he repeats dumbly.

“Yeah.” Mydei tries to shrug it off, pushing aside the upsetting thought that Phainon might refuse anything that comes from him. “It’s not poisoned or anything.”

“That’s not—” Phainon frowns and shakes his head slightly, but the motion only seems to worsen his dizziness. He groans, forcing himself to focus. “It’s just… why?”

Mydei figures they won’t be leaving anytime soon. With a sigh, he takes a seat across from Phainon, crossing his arms.

“I told you before: I honor my word.” Albeit really late. He swallows as Phainon blinks at him in confusion. “That bet from two years ago… You won.”

Phainon’s wide cerulean eyes stare at him as if Mydei has grown a second head. The silence grows so awkward that Mydei ends up clearing his throat.

“I get that it’s weird after so much time, but if you can just ignore that detail—”

His words are cut short when Phainon suddenly picks up the cutlery, opens the plastic container, and takes a generous bite. Mydei almost worries he might choke on such a big mouthful.

When Phainon finally gulps down, Mydei’s heart does a little leap around his ribcage. There it is—albeit exhausted and dulled by sickness. Phainon’s radiant smile pierces through for the first time in what feels like ages—and it’s directed at him.

“I wish I could taste it properly without being sick,” Phainon says, chuckling weakly but earnestly. “It still tastes amazing, though, Mydei. Better than I have ever imagined.”

You imagined it?

What a silly coincidence. Mydei has imagined it too, more than once, during better days— what Phainon would think of his cooking, what expression he’d make. He’s used to being praised for it; it’s the skill he takes the most pride in, and the career he wants to follow when back in Kremnos.

But having his crush taste it—seeing him so genuinely happy because of it—makes his chest feel light, giddy in a way he’s not quite prepared for.

He hopes it doesn’t show in his face, even though he can feel a smirk tugging at his lips.

“Then get better and taste it again tomorrow,” he says.

Mydei knows Phainon is flushed because of the fever—but he’s almost certain the moonlight-haired student’s cheeks deepen into an even stronger shade of red at the comment.

He’s so cute.

“O… Okay…” Phainon mutters, turning his full attention back to the meal and eating in flustered silence.

As Mydei watches him, he remembers he’s supposed to let Cyrene and the girls know that Phainon is alright. Well, mostly alright. He nearly reaches for his phone to message her, but hesitates at the last moment.

Would Phainon be upset if Cyrene learned about his condition? If he’s been hiding his sickness from her, there has to be a reason.

It obviously has nothing to do with Mydei wanting to keep him to himself.

“What are you thinking about?” Phainon asks quietly. That’s when Mydei notices he’s finished eating—and that he looks a little more lively now.

Mydei remembers how sad Phainon had looked yesterday at the park. He doesn’t want to bring Cyrene up now, and he certainly doesn’t want to see Phainon upset again. Maybe… he could help distract him from it.

“That Chimera Park pass of yours…” Mydei starts, trying to sound as nonchalant as possible, but Phainon is already squinching his eyes at him. He swallows. “Do you… still want to go?”

Phainon’s shocked expression isn’t unexpected.

“I… I thought you already had plans?”

Well, fuck.

Looks like he’s calling in sick this Sunday.

“They got cancelled.”

“Oh,” Phainon says. He seems troubled as he scratches his chin, and Mydei wonders if he’s already given up on the idea of inviting him. After a long, stretched moment of silence, Phainon nods curtly. “Sure, I would love to.”

Mydei tries not to make too much of it. After all, he’s just comforting a friend after his latest romantic frustration.

They agree to discuss the details later in the week, since Phainon isn’t really in good shape right now. Mydei walks him to the school gate, where Phainon says his father will be there to pick him up in a few minutes. He explains that Principal Tribios already suggested he leave early and authorized his exit beforehand.

“You can go back to the classroom. I’m not going to faint again,” Phainon teases lightly, well aware that Mydei has already missed an entire class by now.

Even though Mydei believes him, he’s still bothered by the idea of leaving him alone. Or rather… he doesn’t want to part ways just yet, not when they’re finally able to talk normally again after so much time. There’s no way to say that without sounding weird, though, so all he can do is sigh.

“You better not,” Mydei mutters. “You don’t get to invite me somewhere and bail on me— not even if you’re almost dead.”

The corners of Phainon’s eyes crinkle as he laughs wholeheartedly, a sound Mydei is never tired of hearing.

“I wouldn’t miss this for anything, Mydei. It’s a promise.”

The butterflies in his stomach flutter at those words. Mydei needs to leave before he does something he might regret, so he finally turns to go.

Still, that insistent, hopeful part of his mind is far too happy to be contained.

Because if he ignores the small detail that Phainon doesn’t reciprocate his feelings, it almost feels like it could be called a date.

As the thought sinks in, he feels the urge to look over his shoulder. It’s the first time he actually does so before leaving Phainon behind.

To his surprise, the moonlight-haired student is already watching him. When Phainon notices Mydei’s stare, a beautiful smile graces his features as he lifts a hand and waves goodbye.

Mydei turns away, red-faced and with his pulse racing, quickening his pace back toward the classroom.

Can Sunday come sooner?

Chapter End Notes

I like to think Phainon's jealousy tends to be way more destructive (ahem) than Mydei's, who prefers to avoid thinking about it.

I had so many power shortages while writing this chapter. I now click the save button every time I write a new sentence.

Thank you so much for sticking with me. I hope you enjoyed it! Knowing you had fun pays out all of the suffering I went through <3

See you soon ~

Chapter Summary

Phainon's name is now being associated with the Fig Stew curse. Surely that won't affect their trip to the Chimera Park...

Chapter Notes

The only warning I have for this chapter is that it's huge. Enjoy!

On Tuesday morning, Mydei is out of bed again as soon as the alarm rings. Before heading to the kitchen, however, he realizes he isn’t sure whether Phainon is feeling well enough to show up at school. Against his better judgment, he opens the messenger app. The last time they exchanged messages was two weeks ago. Mydei quickly types, hoping he’s not disturbing Phainon if he’s still feeling sick.

Mydei: Hey. How are you feeling today?

He taps his finger against the back of his phone as he waits. The message soon changes to read, and then a reply comes through:

Phainon: I feel better. Good morning to you too :)

Mydei rolls his eyes.

Mydei: Are you coming to school today?

Phainon: I’m already on my way. It’s a bit of a long trip by bus.

Mydei can imagine him sitting with his notebook in hand as the track goes on. It would be nice to watch.

Mydei: What do you want for lunch?

Phainon: I get to choose? :0

Mydei: You won the bet. Seems fair to me.

Phainon: Hm…

Phainon: I want something spicy.

Mydei snorts. Could it be any more vague?

Mydei: How spicy?

Phainon: As much as the chef ;)

Mydei stares at the message for a full minute. He’s almost sure Phainon is just teasing him, but he can’t help feeling his face grow hot as he rereads it a couple of times.

Calm down. He’s not flirting with me, Mydei thinks. He’s just being a prick.

Mydei types the only thing that comes to mind as he pulls his phone away and starts thinking of a recipe for the day.

Mydei: HKS.

҉ ✼

When Mydei arrives at the third-year hallway, he’s surprised to see that the way to his classroom is crowded with students from all years.

What the fuck? he thinks as he tries to get a look inside the room. Luckily, he’s much taller than most of the students, so he manages to catch a glimpse of what’s happening all the way at the front.

“Oh my Phagousa! Khaslana, are you really connected to the Chimera Park easter egg?!” a first-year girl exclaims, circling the class rep along with several others.

“Are you appearing on the special? I want an autograph!” another nearly shouts.

Phainon is at the eye of the storm, trying to get everyone to calm down with his palms raised.

“It’s just a coincidence—I have nothing to do with Fig Stew’s crush!”

Oh, shit.

Panicked, Mydei pulls out his phone and checks his social media, searching for the “Chimera Park” tag.

What he sees there makes his mind stall.

Lilgui: A very trusted font of mine shared this photo yesterday!

[totallytrustworthyproof4.jpg]

notrashnogain12: by Aklivii, isn’t that Fig Stew??

d4zzlingninj4: it’s not very ninja to be seen hugging someone so intimately!! (Ծ_Ծ

RedHerring: forget that… isn’t that guy’s color scheme suspiciously similar to Vigethos?

cutestofall✿: what are you even talking about? since when do humans have a color scheme???

Cloudsknightbeauty: Oh no… That’s not Butterfly Cake D:

notrashnogain21: the hell. I know him, he’s from my school. think his name is Kevin or something

cutestofall✿: omg! Stelle, you can’t dox anyone online like that!

notrashnogain12: you just did that though March lol and his name is Khaslana Lilgui: *ahem* guys! Remember to be civil—don’t go and importune the poor soul. Or if you do, at least don’t mention my name; I don’t want to lose my account!

Lilgui: Either way, it seems like we saw a glimpse of Fig Stew’s possible crush. Let’s stay tuned to see if we get new details this weekend!

Mydei stops scrolling, feeling faint.

Can Nikador’s big fucking sword hit me already?

It takes Principal Tribios’s presence to settle things down. When she appears in the hallway, the crowd slowly falls silent.

“Dear students, our school is in no way linked to any show or studio. Please refrain from disrupting school activities during class hours. Additionally, it is expressly prohibited to use personal information to expose any of our students’ private lives.”

Though her tone is patient, the fiery-haired woman carries an imposing posture as she waits for the students to return to their classrooms. She then approaches the classroom door and signals for Phainon to step outside, asking him to accompany her to her office.

Mydei watches as the student is already apologizing for the turmoil, and he can’t help but feel guilty.

He hadn’t thought about the consequences of letting his emotions show so openly as Fig Stew.

When Mydei is finally able to reach his seat, he notices Castorice staring at him.

“Morning,” he says, sounding more tired than he expected.

“Good morning, Mydei…” She seems on the verge of saying something, but then changes her mind. “I assume you know about Fig Stew’s new rumor?”

Mydei never wanted to hit his head on the desk that much before.

“Yeah.”

Castorice glances around, making sure nobody is paying attention to them—most of their classmates are yapping about Phainon’s involvement with The Awoo Firm.

“Shouldn’t we tell him about the mascots?” When Mydei squints at her, she continues. “I-I mean, he got involved accidentally… I think he at least deserves to know by whom…”

Though Castorice's suggestion makes perfect sense, there’s no way Mydei is accepting it. He’s not going to admit to being Fig Stew and literally awooing to Phainon.

“Over my dead body,” he says, more to himself—though it makes Castorice recoil a little. Poor girl.

A few minutes before class starts, Phainon returns to the classroom. Though everyone is looking at him funnily, he doesn’t seem to take notice, glancing toward the back and offering Mydei a brief smile before taking his seat.

What are you so happy about? Mydei can’t help but wonder.

Just after the bell rings, Cyrene arrives in a rush. Mydei hasn’t really spoken to her since yesterday—he’d notified Castorice about Phainon being on his way home, and she must have passed the information along to the other girls. Cyrene’s behavior toward him had been odd, but honestly, he couldn’t bring himself to care what she thought of him.

She and Phainon seem to have started talking again. Mydei doesn’t know to what extent, but he supposes Phainon is handling his childhood friend—and eternal crush—dating someone else a little better now.

Mydei only hopes he won’t eventually spiral into another breakdown.

When Ms. Aglaea’s English class ends, most of the students are already leaving for lunchtime. Mydei only has the time to stand up when Phainon approaches him.

“Hey, Mydei. Care to accompany me for lunch?” he asks expectantly.

Though Mydei has been preparing his meals for the week, he hadn’t been sure Phainon would want to spend lunchtime with him. He had thought that maybe Phainon wouldn’t want to be seen eating something the Kremnoan made— even though Cyrene is likely nowhere around for the time being, having already dashed out the door. He side-glances at Castorice, who’s been flickering her eyes between the two of them with widened eyes and one hand covering her mouth.

Well, he can understand the shock to some extent.

As Mydei takes too long to answer, Phainon’s expression wilts a little.

“Unless you already planned to go with someone else—”

What is he even talking about? Mydei always ate alone if not with the girls.

“Sure,” he cuts in, hanging his bag over his shoulder. Phainon’s features brighten as he leads the way. Mydei notices that as soon as they start moving, Castorice immediately pulls out her phone and starts furiously typing.

Seems like the girls will have a lot to gossip about.

҉ ✼

Surprisingly, Phainon leads them to the fourth floor. They stop in front of a locked door as Phainon fidgets with his back pocket, pulling out a key.

“Where did you get that?” Mydei asks curiously, unable to picture the student snagging a key to some prohibited school place.

“Ms. Tribios said it would be a good place to hide from the other students until things settle down,” Phainon chuckles. “I guess she’s confident that I wouldn’t jump off the building.”

Wait. Principal Tribios let him have a private place during lunch, and Phainon chose to bring Mydei of all people with him?

It must be because of the meal, Mydei thinks, not wanting to let his mind read too much into the situation. It’s perfectly normal behavior to invite a friend over. If Phainon were on better terms with Cyrene, she would probably be here instead.

The rooftop is, as expected, very plain, but as they enter Mydei can’t help but find the view of the city pretty amazing.

It’s the first time he realizes he’s never gone out of his way to actually learn anything about Okhema; the return date to Kremnos was always a certainty to him. It’s by no means as big and glorious as everything Kremnoans like to express—even in their architecture—however, Okhema has a more classical, eye-catching charm of its own.

“Breathtaking, isn’t it?” Phainon’s voice carries over a soothing tone.

“Mhm.” Mydei grunts.

They sit down near the rooftop entrance, where the wall casts a stretch of shade. Mydei busies himself with taking out today’s meal as Phainon watches, arms tucked behind his head.

“What’s on the menu today, chef?” he teases.

Mydei rolls his eyes as he slides the container toward him. He then takes his own portion, toned down in spiciness—he doesn’t want to end up with an upset stomach so early in the day.

“Potato and carrot cooked in curry broth,” he replies monotonously. “With extra spice, just for you.”

Phainon is already taking his first bite as Mydei speaks.

“It tastes divine, as expected from you,” he praises earnestly. “Thanks for the meal!”

Mydei scoffs, feeling giddy from the praise.

They spend lunchtime in comfortable silence, until Phainon speaks up again.

“Aren’t you curious about this Fig Stew thing?” Phainon asks once they finish eating.

Mydei stiffens as he replies, “Why would I be? Sounds like a baseless rumor over a single photo.”

Phainon studies him in silence, resting a hand on his chin.

“I thought you’d be interested in your favorite chimera having a love interest,” he points out. “From what I hear, it’s something never seen in the cartoon.”

Well, shit.

Under normal circumstances, he would be very interested—but when he’s the one playing Fig Stew in that story, he can’t help feeling awkward. Mydei shrugs, trying to sound nonchalant.

“I’ll only believe it if it actually becomes a special,” he says. “Unless you know something about that?”

He hopes playing dumb is enough to keep Phainon from growing suspicious about his lack of interest in the topic.

“Not really,” Phainon shakes his head. “I just happened to befriend Fig Stew during a rough time. They’ve been really kind to me, although…”

As Phainon trails off, Mydei arches an eyebrow.

“What?”

“It’s kind of funny, actually,” he says as he brushes his fingers over the bandage around his elbow. It’s probably almost entirely healed by now, and this certainly isn’t the same Fig Stew wrapped on Sunday. “You two have a very similar way of showing kindness. A very imposing one.”

Mydei blinks. He should be more worried about the comparison, but he’s more baffled than anything else.

“The heck is that supposed to mean?”

Phainon laughs quietly.

“Fig Stew wouldn’t let me go until it treated my injury.” he says, cerulean-blue eyes settling on Mydei’s, the color incredibly bright under the open sky. “And you made sure I ate yesterday when I was feeling unwell. It leaves no room to complain.”

Mydei crosses his arms defensively over his chest.

“Maybe they’ve also identified your lack of self-preservation,” he shoots back. Mydei is used to looking after his friends, and it was not different even if Phainon happened to be his crush.

“Mhm, maybe…” Phainon hums, a bit too casually for a comment about his lack of self-care. “I’m glad you will finally be able to meet them, though.”

Damn it.

Guilt gnaws at him. Phainon truly thinks Fig Stew will be present there this Sunday. It brings another point of attention to their scheduled trip to the park.

“About that… are you sure it’s a good idea to go there when you’re caught up in this Easter egg mess?” Mydei asks, recalling how exhausting dealing with the fans can be. “There’s a high chance people will bother you about it.”

“No way—as I said before, I’m not missing it, not even over being harassed by Fig Stew’s fans,” Phainon replies decisively.

Though Mydei feels giddy over Phainon’s being so set on keeping his promise with him, he wouldn’t be opposed to going somewhere else instead of the park. Still, it feels too awkward to suggest that when Phainon is being so laid-back about it.

“Unless… you don’t want to go anymore because of it?” Phainon’s tone shifts into a dejected one.

“No—that’s not it, I still want to,” Mydei replies honestly with a sigh. “I’m just worried those people might ruin the trip.”

“Ah… that’s fair,” Phainon concedes, falling into thoughtful silence. “Then… if I come up with a plan to clean my name off Fig Stew’s rumor, it should be all right, no?”

Mydei squints at him, suddenly uneasy.

“What kind of plan?”

The half-smile Phainon gives him doesn’t do any good to his heart.

“One that would ensure we aren’t bothered.”

҉ ✼

The week goes by rather quickly. Phainon keeps dragging Mydei up to the rooftop and refuses to share any details about his so-called foolproof plan to stop being associated with Fig Stew’s crush. Though some students still insist on questioning him about it, he patiently reiterates that he has nothing to do with the Awoo Studio.

Mydei keeps honoring his bet. He asks Phainon what kind of food he wants first thing in the morning, and each day is more random than the last—from desserts to Kremnoan cuisine.

On Friday, Phainon tells Mydei to choose something he thinks he’ll like, based on his reactions over the week.

It’s really hard to do when Phainon devours everything like a starving man and praises Mydei’s cooking skills every time.

Mydei is almost sure that if he feeds him a piece of burnt meat, Phainon would still eat it with a smile on his face. But he would never do that—not without a good reason, at least.

So, Mydei ends up baking golden honeycakes, one of his own favorite dishes.

When Phainon takes the first bite, it’s almost as if he melts.

“Titans, Mydei… this tastes so good,” he whines in awe, licking the remaining syrup off his fingers—a gesture Mydei pays more attention to than he’d like to admit. “I don’t think I can live without your cooking anymore.”

Mydei’s chest tightens at the comment. If it means getting such earnest reactions from Phainon, he finds the idea appealing. He can’t say that out loud, though, so he averts his gaze for the sake of his own sanity.

“Too bad. My debt is already paid off,” he says.

“Can’t we make another bet then? Please?” Phainon bats his eyelashes at him, all the while devouring the dish.

Mydei scoffs, casting him a sideways glance. “You would have to win again.”

“A feat I can absolutely repeat!” Phainon chirps.

“Fuck off,” Mydei elbows his side, though a smirk tugs at his lips as Phainon lets out a lighthearted laugh.

It’s nice to finally be able to interact with Phainon so casually after so long. If Mydei ignores the part of him that yearns for something more, he can almost convince himself that Phainon could fit among his best friends if circumstances were different. He can picture it vividly— introducing him to Hephaestion, Leonnius, Perdikkas, Ptolemy, and Peucesta. They’d surely start by picking on him, but once they warmed up, Phainon would be treated like a member of the group in no time.

A dull ache settles in at the thought. Sadly, that reality is nothing but a dream.

He would consider himself lucky if he ever saw Phainon again after graduation.

҉ ✼

It’s Saturday night. Mydei and his friends have just finished their last session of Chrysos Wars 2, a common activity for them and the usual way he keeps in touch with them while in Okhema.

After Leonnius, Peucesta, Ptolemy, and Perdikkas leave the call for the night, it’s just him and Hephaestion.

“So, tomorrow you’re going on that super-ultra-secret part-time job again?” Hephaestion asks over the mic. His friends have been pretty insistent on knowing what he’s doing every Sunday instead of showing up to play with them.

“Actually, I’m not going tomorrow,” Mydei replies, staring at his screen absent-mindedly.

“Oh? You’re finally gracing us with your royal presence, then?” Hephaestion teases.

“Like I was not present the entire year before,” Mydei scoffs.

“Everyone’s just curious. Leonnius is certain I know what this is about and won’t stop pestering me.”

Mydei rolls his eyes. Theoretically, hiding the park mascot thing from his friends shouldn’t be an issue—but he can already imagine the endless comments about “that part-time job when you were a furry” being used endlessly on repeat.

“It’s no big deal. In two weeks, I’ll be free again,” he assures.

Hephaestion hums.

“So what’s got you so busy tomorrow, then?”

Mydei shifts in his seat. He would be lying if he said he wasn’t at least a bit anxious about it.

“I’m going out with a friend.”

Obviously, Hephaestion wouldn’t be satisfied with just that.

“What? Who is this warrior who got you out of your house and part-time job?” his friend presses.

I asked for it, haven’t I?

Mydei tries to sound as nonchalant as possible, though the mention of the name already has his stomach fluttering.

“It’s Phainon, from my class,” he replies.

The shock is clear in Hephaestion’s voice.

“Huh? Phainon? That Phainon? The one you used to blabber about on every call two years ago?” He rattles on, recalling more details as he goes. “The same one you said had the fluffiest snowy-white hair ever, a smile as radiant as the morning sun, and the pool of bluest eyes you ever gazed upon?”

Holy shit. Why does everyone around me have such a good memory?

“I did not say all that,” Mydei protests with a frown—he most certainly did not use those exact words—but Hephaestion isn’t having any of it.

“Yeah, no shit. You’re lucky I’m the only one here right now—I’m only bringing up the cute things you said,” Hephaestion replies. His smirk can almost be felt through the mic.

Mydei’s cheeks flush red. Can he go back in time and slap his younger self?

“But… didn’t you give up on him because he already had a girlfriend?” Hephaestion continues. “You never brought him up again after you found out.”

Indeed, Mydei shut down every mention of Phainon his friends made until, eventually, they accepted that he’d moved on.

It had been easier to fool them while living in another city.

“She dumped him last week,” Mydei says. “Phainon needed some distraction from it, so he invited me out.”

He doesn’t go into detail about how he found out—or about the way Phainon had nearly collapsed over it.

Hephaestion snorts.

“Oh, you sneaky bastard. The guy’s been single for a week, and you’re already back on the dating market?”

“What—It’s not a date,” Mydei says, trying to shrug it off after spending far too much time convincing himself of that. “It’s just two friends hanging out, dumbass.”

He’s been trying to associate Phainon with the word friend more lately. Their relationship has regained some of its foundation, and he’d rather not strain it again over his own feelings.

“Mydei, my dear, you’re many things—but a distraction isn’t one of them.” Hephaestion’s voice softens. “If he’s single, what’s stopping you?”

“Well, for one, he already said he can’t stop liking her,” Mydei says, remembering the breakdown Phainon had at the park. There’s also another issue that’s been etched into the back of his mind lately. “Besides, there’s no point in investing in something here when I’ll be going back to Kremnos in a few months.”

Hephaestion sighs.

“You realize you’re coming up with excuses that will only leave you miserable, right?” he says, voice dropping. “If that’s really how you feel, why not give it a shot? Even short relationships can create lifelong memories. I’m sure Phainon has eyes—as you very lovingly described—and he’d be crazy not to find you attractive, at the very least.”

His friend’s words make that giddy feeling bubble up in his stomach again.

“Well, he wears glasses, so that might not be the case…”

“Mydeimos, for fucks sake.” Hephaestion groans. “When you’re back, I’m going to hammer some sense into that thick head of yours. Mark my words.”

Mydei lets out a soft chuckle over the mic. He isn’t doubting Hephaestion on that one.

Though Mydei tries to avoid thinking about the possibility of actually dating Phainon, he can’t say he isn’t fond of the idea. After all, Phainon seems to be warming up to him far more quickly than he expected after two years of Mydei giving him the cold shoulder.

But what if Cyrene breaks up again and decides to go back to him? Mydei is fairly sure Phainon wouldn’t hesitate to return to the girl’s embrace. The thought of being reduced to a band-aid on Phainon’s heart makes him hesitate.

So he decides to at least enjoy Phainon’s company while he can—even if it means staying just a friend.

It's what he forces himself to believe when Sunday arrives, and Mydei definitely didn’t spend almost an entire hour wondering what to wear.

Knowing that some of the park’s attractions involve getting guests wet, he opts for his combat boots to avoid spending the entire day walking around in soaked sneakers.

Concluding he looks decent enough—to hang out with a friend, obviously—he grabs his phone and heads toward the subway station.

Phainon lives on the other side of the city, so they plan to meet at the park’s entrance. When Mydei arrives at the station around ten in the morning, he’s immediately greeted by endless waves of guests and the screams coming from the attractions inside.

Giant chimera sculptures stand alongside other secondary characters, like small, fluffy fairies and colorful dromases. Hints of silver accent his belt and choker—the latter leaving a clear view of the sun tattoo on his neck. Phainon looks like he’s stumbled into Evernight’s wardrobe. And really, Evernight’s wardrobe shouldn’t suit him this well. It leaves Mydei’s throat suddenly dry.

It only takes Phainon a few seconds of scanning the entrance area to spot Mydei frozen on the bench and walk over to him with an unfairly handsome smile.

“Hey. Did you wait long?” Phainon Mydei snaps himself out of his dumbfounded state and stands up, taking out his earbuds and slipping them alongside his phone into his back pocket. The very obvious once-over Phainon gives him does nothing good for his heart.

“Does that mean I exaggerated?” he asks, scratching the back of his neck.

“It means you look like a lost member of My Chimerical Romance.”

Phainon tilts his head almost cutely—a sharp contrast to his current look.

“Should I take that as a compliment?”

Mydei bites the inside of his cheek. Of course the nerd has no idea what he’s referring to. Sure, he’d thought their style was cool a few years ago, but he’d stopped caring once he got older.

Still, seeing his crush dressed like that definitely awakens some long-forgotten corner of his brain. He fidgets slightly.

“… It looks fine.” Mydei manages to mutter.

Phainon lets out a lighthearted laugh.

“Thank you. You look good, too,” he shoots back, and Mydei has to avert his gaze to keep his cool.

This is way worse than interacting with him as a chimera.

It’s just a totally normal compliment, Mydei reassures himself. A very normal thing for friends to do.

“Are we going in or not?” Mydei crosses his arms, jerking his chin toward the park gates. He hopes they can move on and stop exchanging flattery already.

“As you wish,” Phainon chuckles.

The same can’t be said for Phainon.

As soon as they reach the main plaza, a few eyes are already drawn to him.

Wow. So he really plans on reaffirming what he already told the fans at school? That clearly didn’t work last time.

Mydei certainly chose a good day to call in sick.

Everyone around them falls silent, waiting expectantly.

What?

It has to be a lie.

The crowd erupts in murmurs.

“I don’t believe it!”

“It’s clearly a distraction…”

What? Mydei repeats mentally as he looks around—because surely Phainon can’t be gesturing toward him. Surely there must be someone beside him, or behind him…

By Nikador’s immortal corpse.

Phainon has just declared to everyone—including Lilgui’s thousand viewers—that they’re dating.

“Who is this guy?”

If only they knew Fig Stew would be partially absent today.

“So there’s still hope for my Butterfly Cake ship to sail…” the brunette girl sighs in relief.

“It would be weird for Fig Stew to be interested in a human, anyway,” someone shrugs.

“It’s fine. How is he even supposed to react to that?

He’s right. Mydei would never have agreed—because the last thing he wants is to pretend to be on a date with his own crush.

I’m dealing with some divine punishment here.

“What—” Mydei tries to look over his shoulder, but Phainon stops it with a hand to his chin.

No, Mydei thinks. Because I wouldn’t be lying.

“I can’t,” Mydei says firmly, turning his gaze away from those impossibly blue irises.

Phainon wordlessly retracts his hand from Mydei’s chin, the motion on his back stopping altogether.

“Is the idea really that disgusting to you?” he asks, his voice unable to fully hide the dejection beneath it.

No. The problem is the exact opposite.

It’s everything I want.

“You’re worried about being found out by—”

“Never mind.” Though his lips curve into something resembling a smile, it carries none of its usual cheerfulness. “I understand. But look—I’m not asking us to do anything intimate. If we at least look like we’re having fun together, I’m sure we can pass as discreet in front of those fans.”

It’s a strange choice of words.

So why does Mydei want to cling to those words so badly?

Until now, he had never thought he would have the chance to be close to Phainon like this— like he belonged there, even if it was just a lie on Phainon’s side.

Because Mydei could never pretend his feelings weren’t real.

Even short relationships can create lifelong memories.

Is it so wrong to want to accept it?

“O… okay,” Mydei says so quietly he’s almost unsure if his voice actually went through.

“… Really?” The storm clouding Phainon’s expression slowly drifts away, as if Mydei's acceptance brought the sunlight back with it.

Mydei closes his eyes and creases his brows. He can’t look at him right now—not when his heart is plummeting this hard.

“Already backing down on your own proposal?”

“No—!” Phainon nearly shouts, catching Mydei off guard. He quickly lowers his voice, a faint flush creeping up his cheeks. “I mean— I’m glad. Thank you, Mydei.”

“You owe me one,” Mydei can’t help but scoff.

“Sure, I’ll do anything you want!” Phainon replies eagerly, and the urge to ruffle his hair hits Mydei all at once.

Wait a minute.

If this is a date now…

Doesn’t that mean he has the right to do it?

Phainon freezes when Mydei slowly and gently lifts his hand and places it on top of his head. The strands are smooth and silky beneath his fingers, even styled like this—just as Mydei had imagined after all this time. He threads his fingers through the wild bangs, combing them back slightly.

“Good,” Mydei says, voice low but steady. “Now let’s get going, mhm?”

The dumbfounded look Phainon gives him makes Mydei huff out a chuckle. He lowers his arm and slips his hands into his pockets, resuming his walk at a pace slow enough to give Phainon time to recover and catch up with hurried steps, whining about the “surprise attack.”

Well. Mydei, at least, would try to enjoy it while he could.

The first thing they do is queue for the Dragon’s Lair—a rollercoaster themed around Toasty’s Dragon home, a large cave beneath a sleeping volcano that sprouted an enormous tree with golden leaves in its slumber. “Isn’t this a bit too much on an empty stomach?” Phainon asks as they watch the colorful carts run along the track, the guests’ screams echoing as background noise. He looks a little paler than usual.

“Getting scared already?” Mydei teases, leaning on the metal fence with a smirk.

“I’ve never been more than two meters off the ground…” Phainon replies, sounding a bit anxious.

Mydei tilts his head, arching an eyebrow at him.

“I thought you had already been to the park.”

“Well, I didn’t go on any extreme rides. I mostly visited the animal’s area and played at the game booths…”

“Oh, really…?” Mydei can already feel a grin forming on his lips.

“I’m not sure I like your tone, Mydei…” Phainon fidgets, flicking his gaze between him and the coaster.

To his misfortune, Mydei is very fond of extreme rides. Kremnos has some large parks, and he used to visit them quite often with his friends.

“Don’t worry—you’ll survive,” Mydei assures him, though he’s very interested in seeing how Phainon will react to the ride.

The queue moves forward a little more, and as Mydei steps ahead, he nearly trips when Phainon puts both hands around him on the fence he was leaning onto.

“What’s that about?” Mydei asks confusedly as Phainon pouts at him.

“I don’t like the way some people are staring at you.”

“They’re staring at your thighs, Mydei,” Phainon clarifies with a grimace.

Ah.

“…Do you mind if I hug you?”

And a little touching should be fine in those circumstances, right?

Mydei gives a small nod, trying to sound unwavering. “Watch your hands.”

Phainon’s grim expression softens, an amused hum escaping him.

“Yes, sir.”

He has to stop himself from leaning into the touch, suddenly unsure of what to do with his free arms. There’s a growing urge to place his palms over Phainon’s, but he shuts it down by burying his hands in his pockets.

Phainon’s heartbeat against his back is fast in a way that almost mirrors his own.

“Mhm,” Mydei grunts, not trusting his voice right now. He also hopes that, from this angle, Phainon can’t see the rosy tint on his cheeks.

Phainon lets out a shaky breath, something filled with relief. Mydei can’t bring himself to read too much into it, too caught in his own thoughts.

Couple.

I’m here. Don’t be afraid.

Is it his own desire for it to be real, making him imagine things that aren’t there?

“I’m taking pictures of you—for free,” Phainon says with a grin, clearly amused by Mydei’s bewildered expression.

“… Why?”

“Because I’m tired of seeing my date being extorted by those booths,” Phainon says, lowering his voice just a little. “And I want some for me, too.”

Though Mydei’s insides flutter, he somehow manages to keep his composure.

“You could’ve asked for it. I can share the ones I bought,” he says.

Phainon hums, staring fondly at something on his phone screen. Mydei’s curiosity spikes, but Phainon pockets the device before he can get a peek.

“Why not both? We can go through all of them after.” Phainon suggests. Mydei thinks it’s a good idea. Phainon might be oblivious to why he’s keeping the photos in the first place, but he doesn’t see a reason to deny the offer.

As the day goes on, Phainon keeps finding excuses to steal touches here and there, supposedly because “someone could still be watching.” Except for his possessiveness over Mydei’s rather eye-catching choice of pants, it’s all bullshit. Mydei knows it by now, but he doesn’t have the heart to call it out when he’s enjoying the attention.

When they visit The Master Cat-Thief Ghost Tower, the track consists of a walk around the building filled with jump scares and even some employees dressed as monsters and ghosts.

“Those are from the Halloween special years ago,” Mydei explains as they wait for their turn in line. The entrance is a large reception room in the tower’s lounge. “Master Cat-Thief heard there was an immensurable treasure hidden in the depths of the tower and sneaked in to steal it. Turns out the tower was haunted, and the treasure was nothing more than a lure for her to play with ghost chimeras.”

“That sounds adorable.” Phainon chuckles beside him, their shoulders touching. He has a fond smile gracing his features as he looks at Mydei. “You sound so happy when you talk about the show. I love hearing about it.”

It’s becoming increasingly hard to ignore the way Phainon makes Mydei forget how to breathe. The more time passes, the more he wants this to be real.

They enter the tower, the path poorly illuminated as the ambience tries to recreate a full moon night. Through monsters creeping from open holes, mice screeching, and projections of ghosts, Mydei isn’t afraid—he’s more interested in how faithful the recreation is to the show. Phainon, however, clings to his arm, swearing that those things are too scary for him to let go.

Mydei saw how Phainon is when really scared—The Dragon’s Lair is a perfect example.

“Dumbass,” Mydei eventually says, motioning for Phainon to come closer as he puts an arm around his shoulder.

“My hero.” Phainon bats his eyelashes at him in a dreamy tone.

Mydei tsks, resuming their walk along the dark path. The only thing haunting him is when this dream will end.

It has Mydei wondering why Phainon is being so insistent in treating it as a date when everyone has already been fooled—including his own heart. Maybe he’s just being too stubborn after saying they should do it for the entire day around the park.

As sunset approaches, the weather changes drastically. It’s summer, so it isn’t rare for the sky to cloud over the span of a few minutes before heavy rain. They are on their way to the game booths—set on competing over it—when Phainon notices a loud thunder.

“Seems like it will rain soon. Do you want to go back, Mydei?” Phainon asks softly.

Mydei glances at one of the clocks around the park, and a feeling of dread crawls over his stomach. There isn’t much time before it closes, even if they choose to wait for the rain to pass somewhere.

It means that their day together is coming to an end.

So that’s it, huh?

Tomorrow things will go back to normal. They will be back into the world where Mydei and Phainon are just friends, and the person whom Phainon likes isn’t him anymore.

Well, it never was actually. From the very start, Phainon made it clear how it was just a pretend act—even if he got a little too invested along the way.

The truth is that there was never a future beyond this date for them.

All that will be left are the memories of a sweet lie.

Before Mydei can think of an answer, the first droplets start to fall. It takes only a few seconds for the rain to turn into a downpour.

“Shit,” Mydei curses.

They quickly take cover under the closest shelter, a closed-off cotton candy stall. It’s small and doesn’t offer much protection once the rain reaches full force.

How ironic that Mydei avoided religiously every single attraction that could get them wet only to end the day like this.

“Damn… That’s summer rain to you.” Phainon chuckles beside him.

“Mhm,” Mydei grunts, crossing his arms and leaning against the stall. They managed to avoid getting drenched just in time.

The rain turns the park into a wasteland. Most of the guests gather in the indoor food court while it pours heavily, since most of the attractions have had to pause their operation for safety reasons. Only the restaurants and a few booths remain open.

“Do you think it will stop soon?” Phainon eventually asks, having pulled his phone out. It’s as if he’s worried about the time.

“In a hurry?” Mydei teases, though his heart feels heavy. To think their date—fake, he reminds himself—would end like this.

“No,” Phainon shakes his head. “I just wanted to beat your ass at the shooting stall before we leave.”

“Like hell you would.” Mydei scoffs, rolling his eyes.

“Well, at least I’m not like a cat afraid of the rain. You ran here in record time.”

“I’m not afraid of the rain.” Mydei frowns, baffled at the accusation. He just doesn’t like walking in wet clothes.

“Sure, sure…” Phainon grins.

A funny feeling begins bubbling in Mydei’s guts.

He hums thoughtfully. “What about you? Are you fine with walking under a storm?”

Phainon tilts his head at him. “Of course. I’m not made of sugar.”

Mydei’s plan is set. Without warning, he grabs Phainon’s hand and pulls him outside the stall —into the heavy rain.

“Hey—!” Phainon yelps, almost tripping as he hurriedly pockets his phone before it gets wet.

When Mydei steps out, the rain almost instantly soaks his clothes.

“If the rain isn’t a bother, let’s get going then,” Mydei says with a smirk, pleased at the shocked expression on his date’s face.

“You’re enjoying this way too much, aren’t you?” he mutters weakly, stunned.

“Maybe a little,” Mydei admits teasingly.

Phainon’s hand is still linked in his as they fall into step toward anywhere—it doesn’t really matter right now. The park’s lights flicker to life, signaling that the day is winding down— and with it, their pretend date.

Mydei had more fun than he expected. Even if they’d stopped being followed way earlier, the experience was too nice for him to put a stop to. So he decided to let it drag on until Phainon called it quits.

But it never came.

Now, having spent such a joyous day with the person he’s longed for after all this time, it’s only natural that he doesn’t want it to end.

He eventually stops, and with him so does Phainon. The summer rain keeps pouring over them, sticking his hair onto his eyes and nose. It surprises him how warm it is, and how it doesn’t bother him in the slightest getting wet from head to toes for once.

“Mydei…” Phainon calls quietly, and even though the rain makes it hard to hear, Mydei turns to him almost instantly.

He can’t contain a smile at the sight of the eyeliner stain coming down Phainon’s cheeks. His hair finally lost its carefully styled shape, now falling closer to its usual form. Mydei lifts a hand to his face, gently rubbing away the smudge from his face with his thumb.

Even under the rain, Phainon’s skin is so tender. He already misses the closeness they shared, something he’ll never be able to taste again.

It hurts, thinking it’s coming to an end. But at the same time, he’s happy to have Phainon for himself—even if for only a day.

Phainon’s palm comes up and rests over his cheek in a featherlight touch, just above the diamond tattoo beneath his eye. Mydei instinctively leans onto it. Is he pretending still? He’s too good at it, really. If Mydei didn’t know it was all a lie, he would have fallen for it completely—just as his heart has already done.

“Mydei, I…” Phainon’s voice trembles, faltering as he continues, but an alarm rings sharply in the back of Mydei’s mind.

Don’t fall for it. Whatever you think is happening, it’s not real.

Phainon is too gentle to end it now. And Mydei is too selfish to stop himself. Yet he can’t bear to hear words meant for someone else—words he knows are never truly his. Outside this park, Phainon doesn’t belong to him.

Do you see me?

I’m not her. I’ll never be.

But here, now, Phainon is with him. For him. Just for today. And if he can grant himself one last selfish wish…

Mydei leans in before Phainon can speak, before hesitation can take hold. The rain lashes over them, warm droplets dripping down their faces and blurring the world around them. He doesn’t think about the consequences—only about the way his chest is so full of emotions he can’t begin to put into words. His eyes flutter shut. His lips press gently as he kisses Phainon —tenderly, lovingly.

Mydei doesn’t know what he expects—maybe to be pushed away, maybe a shocked expression. Perhaps even a final sentence to their healing friendship. This crosses a line, and they both know it.

He’s braced for anything, really—but definitely not for Phainon pressing his lips back against his, their hands finding anchor in one another’s waists like they’ve been afloat the sea, lost for too long and finally finding their way back home.

Because it’s what it feels like to kiss Phainon—home. A place he wants to return to every day, not just once in a fleeting moment.

Their drenched bodies press together, and for a moment, it’s as if the rain itself melts away. Phainon’s hands trace up Mydei’s back, sliding to the nape of his neck with a touch so full of charge it has Mydei inhaling softly, tilting his head to deepen the kiss, desperate to absorb everything being given to him.

Phainon is warmer than the rain. Warmer than the sun. Evernight was right—he’s the dawn itself.

Maybe Mydei should have declined the offer to turn this into a date from the beginning.

Because after a day so perfect, after feeling Phainon’s tender touches, hearing his sweet words, and tasting those impossibly soft lips, he’s almost certain he can’t call it a simple crush anymore.

Thankfully, the rain hides his thundering heartbeat and washes away any trace of tears. In these last moments, all he can do is hope for a miracle only a Titan could grant.

If Oronyx hears prayers…

Please, let this moment stretch into eternity.
