chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

After their kiss, Phainon is left do deal with the confused mix of emotions that settles over his friendship with Mydei.

One day. One day would be everything he had to date Mydei—even if it was a pretend one. Phainon figured that, since Mydei was already in a relationship, he would never agree to something like that unless Phainon pushed a few buttons. If Phainon could guarantee that it would be harmless and entirely born out of his need to put an end to the Fig Stew rumor, then maybe he could finally have Mydei to himself for an entire day. And if, by any chance, what Evernight implied turned out to be true—that she planned on ending their relationship in a few weeks—then perhaps Phainon could use this date as a trial, a chance to prove himself as a worthy boyfriend candidate to Mydei, if he even managed to get the Kremnoan to entertain the idea. It had still been a hard task to keep his jealousy in check. Phainon made sure to insist that Mydei have lunch with him alone on the rooftop—bless Ms. Tribios—all week long, solely for the sake of keeping him away from the pale pink-haired girl. Thankfully, Mydei didn’t question anything, too focused on paying his debt off. Which was honestly kind of weird. Of course, Phainon knew he had won it two years ago. Mr. Ratio himself had proudly shown Mydei’s exam scores and congratulated them on the success of the tutoring. Phainon was glad he had been able to help, but even more so that he would get to taste the Kremnoan’s cooking. However, since that incident, he has chosen not to mention it again, burying that bet in the depths of his mind. One could imagine his surprise when Mydei decided, completely out of the blue, that he should pay his debt. And, coincidentally, it happened just when Phainon needed it the most.

Talk about fate. Needless to say, Phainon felt like he was in heaven during that particular week they were able to spend together. They went back to talking casually and even shared some friendly banter. It rekindled Phainon’s hope, flickering back to life after so long. Although he forced it down and told himself to be satisfied with Mydei’s friendship, there was still that egregious voice in the back of his head, stirring up that ugly feeling every time Phainon remembered Evernight’s existence. He wasn’t sure why they were keeping their relationship a secret, but he knew Mydei was a very private person when it came to his personal life. Even learning about his hobbies beyond cooking had been a tiring quest two years ago. As such, Phainon chose not to question it. The less they mentioned Evernight, the better for his own sanity. Mydei was finally back in his life—as a friend—and Phainon couldn’t risk losing that over a feeling like jealousy, something that could never change the fact that Mydei already had a girlfriend. However, that didn’t mean Phainon refrained from trying to cater to the Kremnoan’s tastes, if only to make it seem more authentic. Researching “emo” and gothic fashion was an… experience in itself. Evernight was always dressed in edgy clothes, black accessories all over her uniform, and even carried a large black umbrella on sunny days, as if she were allergic to sunlight. While it was a bit weird, it wasn’t like he could judge her fashion sense—his friends often said he dressed like an uncle in his forties, all plaid shirts and button-downs. Either that, or the usual secondhand embarrassment whenever he wore his favorite yellow T-shirt with Droma’s purple pants—an outfit Cyrene had made him promise never to show Mydei, if Phainon didn’t want to traumatize him. So if Evernight’s style was what caught Mydei’s attention, Phainon was determined to dive right into it. He picked up the only black clothes he owned—remnants from one of Cyrene’s shopping sprees she loved dragging him into—along with a black choker Cipher had given him as a joke during an uneventful Secret Santa. He styled his hair to a more edgy shape, letting it look spikier than usual. If his research was anything to go by, makeup would also be required. Phainon wasn’t fond of the idea of painting his nails black, so he asked his mother to lend him her eyeliner. She kindly offered not only the eyeliner but also to apply it herself, lest he end up looking like a panda.

There’s a mischievous hint to her expression as she applies it, as if she knows far too much about what this is really about, even though Phainon only said he was going out with a friend. “Will they be coming for dinner, sweetheart?” she asks midway through it. Phainon does his best not to blink, the sensation around his eyes feeling a bit off. It almost feels like a thin layer of clay has been applied. “I don’t think so, Mom,” he replies. There are no plans to keep the pretend date going outside the park, so he hadn’t even considered the possibility. Audata hums, unconvinced. “If they change their mind, dinner’s at seven. If your charm doesn’t win them over, my cooking surely will.” She winks at him, and Phainon can’t help but feel flustered. If only his mom knew how good a cook Mydei is, she would most likely fall for him just as easily as he did. He hadn’t told anyone about his intent to turn this hangout into a date—not even Cyrene. Somehow, he had the feeling she would give him an earful the moment she found out, but what else could he do? It was almost a desperate measure, and the Fig Stew excuse fit like a glove. He would apologize to the poor mascot for using them like that when the time came. Any explanations he might owe could wait until tomorrow. With his mind set, Phainon walked to the bus stop, joy and anxiousness tangled in his gut. If everything goes wrong, Mydei could very well punch him and snap the fragile strings their friendship was balanced on. Yet the moment Phainon’s eyes found Mydei’s figure at the park entrance… he knew he would give anything to be on an actual date with him. So he pressed forward with his plan, forcing himself to swallow the bitterness tied to Mydei’s obvious hesitation about Evernight finding out. She wasn’t even that serious about their relationship, so why did Mydei care so much? Still, it wasn’t his place to question it—partly because he feared the answer. Phainon was relieved that Mydei didn’t show the same disgust he had two years ago at the mere suggestion of pretending to date him—perhaps because the terms made it clear this was just a fake scenario meant to help a friend. Yet there was still that flicker of hope, burning a little brighter. Although a few suspicious fans followed them for a while, they grew bored within minutes after the pair joined their first queue, which meant Phainon could have put an end to it at any moment. As if he would ever do that. Phainon had spent years daydreaming about going out with his crush, and the only thing that could put an end to the experience was Mydei himself, if he eventually grew annoyed by it. So long as Mydei kept playing along and seemed to be enjoying himself, Phainon would indulge in it completely. Some things were kind of hard to ignore, though. Mainly those pants. Phainon didn’t think it was possible to feel both gratitude and anger toward a piece of clothing at the same time. Because holy fuck, did Mydei actually look in a mirror before going out? He had never taken the Kremnoan for a show-off, but now he had doubts about the rest of Mydei’s wardrobe. The small thorns would have been harmless on anyone else’s legs. But on him, Phainon could catch tiny glimpses of red beneath the fabric—the same shade as Mydei’s tattoos—and it sent his mind on a completely different trip than the park. His tattoos go all the way down there. And boy, didn’t this realization make his thoughts run wild. Phainon’s saving grace was that they were in a public place, which allowed him to keep his arousal in check by channeling his frustration toward the not-so-subtle onlookers whose curiosity had also been piqued by that incriminating piece of clothing. Who would have guessed that his first move would be driven by possessiveness over his pretend date? If Phainon couldn’t hide Mydei from those thirsty gazes, then at the very least, he would make it clear that this beautiful young man was his—even if only for a day. That thought alone gave him enough courage to engage in a more intimate setting, ignoring even the fear of the upcoming rollercoaster ride. And to say he was surprised at how receptive Mydei had been was an understatement. At some point, everything began to flow so naturally that Phainon himself started to get carried away. Mydei not only looked like he was having fun—he looked truly happy, perhaps for the first time since they had known each other. Every time they held hands sent a jolt of electricity through Phainon’s body. Mydei kept allowing Phainon’s touches to the point that he grew greedy. Letting go was becoming harder and harder, each touch lingering a little longer than it should. And when Phainon hugs him, he’s carried back to those peaceful days of their tutoring two years ago.

After all this time, they still fit perfectly together. It’s enough to make him forget about the world outside the park—about Evernight, graduation, and even the fact that he still hadn’t managed to introduce Mydei to his favorite mascot chimera. The only thing that really matters is at this exact moment in his arms, as they queue for an attraction Phainon hasn’t even been paying attention to. When it starts to rain, that’s when the realization that their date is coming to an end finally sinks in. Needless to say, Phainon wishes it could last longer. But how could it? Mydei is already taken—he can’t just steal him away, even if he wants to. He starts to worry about the time. His phone reads almost six p.m. If they leave soon enough, maybe they could make it to the dinner his mom had suggested earlier. Would it be too weird to invite Mydei after everything they had done in the park? Nothing so far suggested their friendship would be damaged by it, so perhaps it could be understood simply as a way of thanking the Kremnoan for playing along. Phainon doesn’t get much time to dwell on the thought because soon after, Mydei’s hand finds his, dragging him into the heavy rain. Though baffled by the audacity, Phainon can’t help but find the smugness in Mydei’s features utterly adorable. And so he lets him have his way, each step a ripple across the few remaining minutes they still have together. What would Mydei say if he knew Phainon hadn’t been pretending at all during their date? If he discovered that Phainon had set this up out of jealousy—resenting his girlfriend, wishing he were the one in her place, and hoping that if they ever broke up, Mydei would turn to him simply because he was happy beside him, even for a fleeting moment. It sounds so stupid, yet it gnaws at him from the inside out. But… what if it wasn’t only a single moment? What if he could stretch it, just a little longer? Whatever might happen, Phainon doesn’t want to part ways just yet. Here, with Mydei’s hand in his, only one thought repeats itself in his mind: Mydei, I don’t want this to end. As he squeezes his palm, Mydei comes to a stop. The words tighten in Phainon’s throat the more he tries to force them out. I wasn’t pretending. All he can feel are the droplets of water against his skin and the frantic rhythm of his heart when Mydei’s fingers brush his face. Phainon doesn’t even remember he’s wearing makeup until Mydei gently rubs away some smudges. He doesn’t even care if he looks like a panda, just as his mother warned him that morning. His focus is entirely on those shining golden irises—a beacon of light beneath the summer rain. Phainon doesn’t understand the melancholy etched into Mydei’s features, even as he smiles at him. How could he make it go away? Mydei’s smile softens as he leans into Phainon’s palm, as if using it as an anchor to this moment where only the two of them exist. I like you. Phainon’s words are cut short when Mydei kisses him. The world comes to a halt as the realization sinks in: Mydei is kissing him. And suddenly, there are no more thoughts in his head, not when Mydei’s lips fit perfectly against his, warm and soft enough to push all confusion aside. Phainon can’t dwell on why his friend, who never showed any romantic interest and agreed only to a fake date, would kiss him. All he knows is that this is something he has yearned for so long that there’s no way he’s going to just stand still. So he returns the kiss with fervor, as if it were the first and the last—Titans forbid it should be the last, but what if it is?—and when Mydei melts into his embrace, when their lips move together with so much heat, Phainon realizes there’s something slipping through the cracks of this situation. How can they still call themselves friends after such a mind-blowing experience? Phainon doesn’t know how long it lasts—though he wishes it were forever—but eventually they part, the rain still tickling their faces. Mydei’s eyes are half-lidded, clouded with an underlying emotion Phainon’s dazed mind almost wants to label as affection, while his gaze remains fixed on Phainon’s lips as if he hasn’t had enough yet. Titans, how Phainon wants more too. But something holds them both back, even as they cling to each other as though they would fall if they let go. Under the rain, with his hair damp and his slightly parted lips rosy and swollen from their kiss, Mydei is breathtaking. It isn’t fair. How could Phainon ever think of giving up on this crush? If Mydei harbors even the slightest feelings for him, Phainon wouldn’t hesitate to steal him away from Evernight. The moment slowly begins to crumble when he notices Mydei trembling slightly in his hold.

“Mydei… you’re shivering,” Phainon isn’t sure how his voice sounds—probably too strained —but he hopes the rain masks it to some extent. He caresses Mydei’s cheek, and Mydei shuts his eyes tightly at the touch, his brows creasing. His feverish skin is starting to cool, and Phainon’s stomach twists wildly. Please don’t say you’re sorry. If Mydei admits the kiss was a mistake, that he somehow got carried away during their fake date, Phainon doesn’t know if he’ll survive. Don’t give me hope and then take it away. “Mydei—” “We… should go.” Mydei says, his small voice nearly lost to the sound of the rain. His eyes open again, and the moisture there is impossible to read under the storm. Why do you look like you’re about to cry? Seeing Phainon frozen in place, he adds softly, “I’m getting cold.” Even if the rain had been warm at first, the constant exposure to it, paired with the fierce wind, was bound to lower their body temperature. “R—right…” Phainon stutters, slowly stepping back to give him space. Mydei wraps his arms around himself, averting his gaze in an almost guarded way. Phainon knows it might not help much in this situation, but his jacket shields against the rain better than a soaked T-shirt. He swiftly takes it off and drapes it over Mydei’s shoulders before the other can react or find an excuse. “What—” “Don’t worry about me,” Phainon assures with a smile. “I don’t get cold easily.” On the contrary, Phainon still feels like a burning sun after everything that just happened. His heart continues to plummet wildly, his emotions scattered as though he might burst at any moment. Mydei studies him for a second before giving a small nod, as though he doesn’t have it in him to argue. He buries himself in the jacket, and Phainon nearly breaks down over how cute it looks—a funny thing, because although they’re about the same size, the clothing around his shoulders somehow makes him seem smaller.

“… Thanks.” They walk back to the park’s entrance in silence, each lost in their own thoughts. Phainon keeps stealing glances at Mydei the entire way, desperate to grasp anything that might reveal the meaning behind that kiss. How he wishes he could read minds, just this once. He’s dying to ask about it, yet equally terrified of what Mydei might say. What if he feels guilty about betraying his girlfriend during a fake date? Or worse—what if he didn’t enjoy it at all? Is Phainon a bad kisser? It was his first time, and he only did what felt natural—or… Does Mydei really feel anything for him? “I had fun today,” Mydei says, his voice pulling Phainon back to reality. Phainon blinks, realizing they’ve already reached the park’s station. Mydei will be taking the subway home, while Phainon will have to wait for the next bus, since his neighborhood lies on the outskirts of Okhema. At least the station has a wide roof they can use as shelter from the rain. Phainon avoids thinking about how Mydei is still holding onto his jacket tightly, even now that they’re out of the downpour. “Oh—uh, yeah. Me too,” Phainon stammers, cringing at how awkward he sounds. It’s almost annoying how composed Mydei looks while he’s very clearly having a mental breakdown. Mydei gives a small hum, his lips faintly curving upward. “You should look into a mirror when you get the chance,” he says softly. Phainon can only imagine the disaster around his eyes if the kids at the station, gaping at him, are any indication of how bad it is. At least the adults pretend not to notice before turning away to giggle. And you kissed me when I looked like that, Phainon thinks, biting the inside of his cheek to keep himself from saying it out loud. This elephant in the room needs some time to cool down before he can talk about it without having a heart attack. Mydei’s subway arrives soon after. He’s already moving to return the jacket when Phainon holds it firmly over his shoulders. “Keep it,” he says. “It will help warm you up until you get home.”

Mydei stares at him with widened eyes, his arms slowly slipping out of the jacket. There’s a hint of frustration as he fidgets slightly. “… I’ll give it back tomorrow.” For all Phainon cares, he can keep it forever if he wants. Knowing Mydei is taking something from him home makes Phainon’s insides flutter. “Mhm.” Phainon nods with a half-smile. “Get home safely, Mydei.” Mydei hesitates for a second before boarding, lips parted as if he still has something to say. When the subway’s departure chime rings, he snaps out of it. “You too,” he says, stepping into the subway car. Phainon waves as the subway propels forward on the rails, receiving a contained wave back before the vehicle disappears from his field of vision. The way to his own home is a blur. He somehow manages to get on the right bus and step off at his neighborhood stop in full automatic mode. Phainon still can’t believe everything that happened today.

When he opens the front door, the smell of something delicious makes his stomach growl almost instantly. His parents are watching TV in the living room, and his mother is the first to greet him. “Welcome, sweetheart,” she chirps, but her smile quickly fades when she takes in his state. “Oh dear, what happened to you?” She’s off the sofa and reaching for him in an instant. “And what kind of witchcraft is that on your face?” his father asks. Audata immediately slaps his arm, earning a mumble of “kids these days” as he turns his attention back to his favorite show. Phainon can’t help but chuckle at the scene. “I got caught in the storm,” he explains. The rain has stopped now, and though his hair and skin are nearly dry, his clothes remain drenched, clinging uncomfortably to him. Audata cradles his cheeks with her palms. “And what about your friend? Didn’t they come to dinner?” Oh, that. Phainon had wanted to invite Mydei, but he ended up far too confused about their actual relationship to ever remember. “Not today, Mom,” he says, trying to sound composed, though he’s still too shaken to really keep his tone steady. “But I’ll invite them next time.” Audata frowns, but she knows her son too well to press him about it right now. She lets him off the hook with an exasperated, “You better,” and tells him to take a bath and eat before going to bed. That’s exactly what Phainon does. And oh boy, he looks like he’s wearing that cartoon superhero mask—what was its name again? Batcake? It’s something to laugh about, and certainly not a face anyone would normally consider attractive enough to kiss. What did Mydei even see in me? The memory of their kiss makes his body heat up, and he quickly hops into the shower before he gets too excited about it. Washing the eyeliner away is a battle in itself, but he emerges victorious after twenty minutes and with slightly swollen cheeks. Back in his bedroom after dinner, he sits on the bed and picks up his phone. Luckily, the case kept most of the wetness away, and the device seems to be working properly now that he’s finished drying it. Finally, alone in the quiet of his room, Phainon has time to think as he opens the messenger app to a very familiar chat. His thumb hovers over the keyboard, but he’s out of words as he glares at the screen. There’s a growing restlessness at his core as he replays their date over and over in his mind. What if Mydei uses this day as an excuse to distance himself from me again? Honestly, Phainon had thought their friendship was untouched—at least until the kiss. They’d both had fun at the park, even if things had been more intimate than strictly necessary, and Mydei hadn’t seemed bothered by it the way he had two years ago. What changed? Phainon has no idea. But hey, he’s not complaining. Not when Mydei is more at ease in his presence, to the point of actually enjoying it. Everything had been fine. He’d gotten close to his crush again and managed to earn his friendship back—and then Mydei kissed him. Titans above, he still can’t believe it. Even after dinner, after washing away the rain, it lingers. His mouth tingles at the mere memory of Mydei’s lips against his. An electric sensation floods his entire body with ecstasy as he recalls the touch. Phainon’s fingers hover just above his bottom lip. It felt real. As if Mydei truly wanted this.

Still, Phainon can’t be entirely sure. And he doesn’t know how he could confirm it without asking Mydei directly—and the thought terrifies him. He might finally face rejection, whether because Mydei already has a girlfriend or because Phainon is hallucinating some hidden meaning that isn’t there. He runs a hand through his hair in frustration, letting out a loud groan. For Titans' sake, friends don’t kiss each other! What even are they now? How can he swallow it all down and greet Mydei tomorrow without combusting on the spot? There’s no way Phainon trusts himself to act normally around him anymore. Above all else, he can’t bear the thought of Mydei already being taken. No matter how he looks at it, it means Mydei cheated on Evernight. Honestly, Phainon doesn’t care what the girl thinks—but how does it weigh on Mydei? Will he tell her? Is he regretful? Was that the reason he looked on the verge of crying? Phainon squeezes his phone tightly as that bitter feeling threatens to consume him. What if they’re texting each other right now, trying to make amends? What if Mydei was simply too determined to help his pathetic friend and took a step farther than he should have? Is Phainon at fault for suggesting something that might have blurred their judgment? Only when his phone vibrates does he realize he’s on the verge of snapping it in two from the force of his grip. Phainon turns his attention to the screen, his breath catching.

Mydei: Still awake?

The surprise nearly makes him drop the device. Phainon blinks, as if the message were some divine signal from the Titans themselves. It’s past ten p.m. He replies instantly.

Phainon: Yep. Fell out of bed?

Mydei: I was having tea. My throat feels raspy.

Phainon’s heartbeat races so fast it feels like it might burst from his chest. Mydei is talking to him casually, as though they hadn’t shared a kiss under the rain just hours ago.

Phainon: Oh? Getting sick?

Mydei: As if. There’s no word for “sick” in the Kremnoan dictionary.

Phainon groans, pressing his phone against his forehead. Even in the midst of panic, how can he still find this guy so unbearably adorable?

Phainon: Hm…

Phainon: Does that mean Kremnoans have an amazing constitution, or is that just you?

Stop it, you idiot. Stop flirting with him—he’s your friend, your former pretend date, and he already has a girlfriend. And he kissed you, but we’re still not talking about that.

Mydei: HKS. I should known better than to text you.

Phainon can’t hold back his smile.

Phainon: But you still did.

He chews on his bottom lip, taking a leap of faith with the next message.

Phainon: Missed me already? :^)

Mydei’s reply takes so long that Phainon is perched at the edge of his bed, anxious, watching the three dots appear and vanish on the screen.

What finally comes through makes his mind stall.

Mydei: Your jacket will have to suffice.

He rereads it so many times his glasses nearly slide all the way down his nose.

Phainon: What do you mean?

No reply comes, even after several minutes.

Phainon: Mydei????

Phainon: Mydeiiii? Answer me pleaseee (T⌓T)

Phainon: …good night, then. :((

Kephale spare him. How could Mydei drop this and go to sleep peacefully afterward? Now Phainon can’t shake the image of him cuddling his jacket to sleep. He never imagined he would feel so much jealousy over his own piece of clothing.

Do friends sleep with each other’s clothes?

The answer is rather obvious, but Phainon’s brain is too fried to think rationally at the moment. It was just something Mydei implied—it’s not as if he’s actually hugging the as he dozes off this very moment. It shouldn’t even be dry yet!

…Right?

Someone please slap him already.

Though this conversation erased any chance of Phainon getting sleep tonight, at the very least it reassured him that Mydei wasn’t planning to shut him out of his life again. That alone feels like a victory. Still, there are so many things they need to talk about. Phainon needs to understand what really happened today—and what these flirty interactions are doing to their friendship, if it can even still be called that.

Rolling onto his bed, he sighs. Is it too much to dream that Mydei is doing all this because he actually likes him too?

Despite having a girlfriend, despite ignoring him for two whole years… none of it really matters if that’s true.

So late into this starless night, Phainon’s hope, for once, burns as bright as the sun.

҉ ✼

On Monday morning, Phainon discovers he’s still been left on read, with no reply in sight.

That’s fine. He’ll meet Mydei at school and ask about it.

He totally can do it without fumbling anything. The trembling in his hands and his left leg twitching the entire way to school are clear signs that he’s not nervous at all.

Titans help him.

He needs to talk to Mydei about their date. He can’t keep bottling everything up and pretending they’re just friends anymore. Phainon wants to understand what Mydei really expects from him, instead of maintaining this awkward wall between their unspoken feelings.

It sounds easier in his head.

By the time Phainon settles into his desk, he’s still trying to figure out a good way to start the conversation.

Phainon received a few curious glances as soon as he arrived. No student asked about his involvement with the Fig Stew curse, which must be an aftereffect of his announcement during Lilgui’s livestream. Even Castorice is staring at him from behind her notebook.

Well, he’s almost used to being talked about by now. As long as nobody bothers Mydei about it, there’s no reason for him to care.

That being said, he can’t hide his disappointment when the minutes tick closer to the start of class and Mydei still hasn’t shown up.

He’s not known for being late—that’s Cyrene’s specialty—so there must be a good reason.

Could it have something to do with yesterday?

Phainon gulps as another wave of anxiety washes over him.

Phainon pulls out his phone and quickly types a message, trying not to seem too desperate.

Phainon: Hey. You coming today?

Mydei: No. I’m sick.

Phainon exhales a breath he hadn’t realized he was holding. Mydei is still clearly ignoring his last messages from yesterday, but given the circumstances, he can let it slide for now.

He also knows he shouldn’t find this funny, but it’s stronger than him.

Phainon: What happened to the Kremnoans don’t get sick discourse?

Mydei: Shut up.

Mydei: My head already hurts. I’m not dealing with you right now.

Fair enough. At least Mydei didn’t skip for a reason outside his control.

Phainon: Get well soon :)

Phainon lets out a relieved sigh.

“You alright, Phai?” Cyrene asks curiously at his side.

Phainon has been keeping her in the dark about his recent endeavors with Mydei, mostly because he knows she’s endured enough of his suffering over that crush through the years. Apparently, she’s still unaware of what happened yesterday—good. He’ll explain everything eventually.

Still, her expression clearly shows she knows exactly what he’s thinking about.

“Yeah. I just found out Mydei isn’t coming today. He’s sick.”

Cyrene’s mouth forms a little ‘o’.

“And why are you so smug about it?”

Phainon averts his gaze, scratching the back of his neck. He has no intention of telling Cyrene how Mydei actually got sick.

“Let’s just say it was his own doing,” Phainon replies vaguely. While he was an accomplice, it was Mydei who dragged them into walking under a storm.

Cyrene narrows her eyes at him.

“Why do I feel there’s much more to it?”

Phainon only answers with a half-smile. She shakes her head in resignation.

“You’ll tell me sooner or later.” She props her chin on her hand, her voice softening. “Still, at least you finally seem happy again. That’s the power of lovesickness, huh?

“Rene…” Phainon mutters in frustration, fighting back the heat crawling up his neck.

His friend lets out a delicate laugh at his doom, the bell ringing and saving him from his own embarrassment.

҉ ✼

Phainon may have developed the bad habit of expecting Mydei to always be there for lunch since last week. Even without his cooked meals, he thought they’d had a pretty fun time together.

Now that the Kremnoan is staying home, he can’t help but feel a little empty as he leans against one of the windows in the third-floor hallway. Cyrene is already on her way to meet Stelle, and he’s not in the mood to chat with Castorice and the girls.

Shit. Is he having separation anxiety?

Phainon considers sending a message to check on how Mydei is doing, but thinks better of it. If he’s sick, staring at a phone screen probably won’t help soothe an aching headache.

The only way he can think to ease his longing is to see his face—even just for a little while.

His fingers swiftly open the gallery app.

Phainon had managed to take several photos during their date. If he’d known Mydei liked keeping pictures enough to spend a small fortune on them, he would have offered earlier to snap some.

He can already feel a smile tugging at his lips as he scrolls through the images.

There was one photo he took when Mydei got an Oatmeal-themed waffle and Phainon snatched a bite without warning. He had already prepared to capture Mydei’s reaction, so the picture ended up showing him both annoyed and frustrated at the camera.

How cute.

Phainon had also tried very hard to get them to take pictures wearing the chimera-ear tiaras they handed out at the park, but Mydei was so adamantly against it that he eventually had to give up.

Sadly, they never took a proper couple photo. Phainon had felt too insecure to ask.

He lets out another sigh, resting his chin in his fist. He scrolls some more—there are a few blurry photos he snapped during the rides, some of the dromas and chimeras in the animal area, one of Mydei reading a stall’s menu out loud for him since Phainon had left his glasses at home…

The last photo of the day was taken just minutes before the storm. The sky was already darkening with heavy clouds, and Mydei stood at the center of the frame, a few lamps casting a warm glow across his face. His expression was soft, and he glanced at the camera—or was it at Phainon?—with tender golden irises.

He looked happy.

Phainon’s chest tightens. Titans, he misses him.

He stares at the photo a while longer, committing every detail to memory. It was taken after they exited the Master Cat-Thief Ghost Tower, where Mydei had kept him close the entire route after Phainon whined about being scared. The attraction is still visible in the corner of the frame.

Most guests had already retreated to the restaurants and game booths, so there were only a few people scattered in the background. Phainon isn’t sure why he’s suddenly paying so much attention to it, but something keeps tugging at his focus the longer he looks.

He adjusts his glasses, narrowing his gaze. Why does that particular figure seem so familiar?

When he finally notices the two pale-pink strands of hair peeking out from beneath a large black umbrella, it clicks.

Evernight was there.

His thoughts grind to a halt as the realization sinks in.

The girl wasn’t looking in their direction—she seemed to be heading somewhere else. As if she wasn’t bothered in the slightest that her boyfriend had been within reach all this time.

Why was she at the park?

Mydei said their plans had been cancelled. Could she be there with someone else, a friend perhaps? Phainon doesn’t recognize anyone near her.

Did she see them?

If she did, she chose to stay quiet and not approach them. Why? Phainon had been far closer to Mydei than any friend should be. There’s no way she didn’t notice that.

Does Mydei know about it?

Phainon doubts he would have agreed to their fake date if he knew she was there. He already seemed worried she might find out.

The questions keep piling up, one after another, until Phainon feels like he’s about to have a meltdown. But more importantly—

What in Kephale’s name is happening?

҉ ✼

Phainon can’t concentrate on any of his remaining classes for the rest of the day. His thoughts keep circling back to Evernight’s suspicious presence at the park yesterday.

The more he replays it in his mind, the less sense it makes.

In the end, he decides that maybe Mydei’s absence today is a blessing. Because the moment the final bell rings, Phainon heads straight to the second-year floor, beating even Cyrene to it.

Most students are already crowding the hallway on their way out. Among them is Evernight with her small group of friends: the one tall dark-haired guy he recalls as Dan Heng, the look-alike who might be her twin sister, Stelle, and her brother Caelus.

It’s Stelle who spots him first.

“Oh hey, Kevin. What brings you here?” she asks lazily as he approaches the group.

“It’s Khaslana, Stelle…” Evernight’s sister corrects with a reprimanding frown.

Phainon isn’t in the mood to play along, and his expression probably shows it.

“Hey. I was looking for Evernight.” His eyes lock onto her figure. She stares back at him with an unbothered expression, as if he were nothing more than a minor inconvenience. He adds, “Can we talk?”

The group exchanges silent glances, all eyes turning to Evernight, waiting for her reaction.

“Oh, my,” she says, feigning surprise with a palm over her mouth. “Go ahead, guys. I’ll catch up soon.” “What did you do this time?” her sister asks in a tired tone, while Dan Heng gently guides her along the group with a hand on her back.

“Eve’s been really close with the third-years lately, huh…? Think she can set me up with Castorice?” Caelus says dreamily as they leave the corridor.

“In your dreams… Castorice is already dating,” Stelle mocks, ignoring her brother’s loud “What!?” as she focuses on her phone. “Oh, I have to go meet my dear wife. Bye!”

The last thing Phainon sees is Dan Heng rubbing his temple in silent suffering.

A small chuckle from Evernight pulls Phainon’s attention back to her.

“My, my. What a scary face, Mr. Class Rep.” Her lips curve into a smile. “What did I do to deserve such hatred?”

Phainon can feel the scowl etched into his features. He flexes his fingers, trying to keep himself calm. If he messes this conversation up and actually insults Mydei’s girlfriend, he might as well say goodbye to their friendship.

Thankfully, the hallway is empty now. It’s just the two of them.

“I need to ask you something,” he begins. “Why… were you at the park yesterday?”

Evernight tilts her head slightly. She holds her signature umbrella in one hand, while the other comes to rest against her jaw.

“That sounds more like…” she muses, blood-red eyes glinting, “…you want to know whether I saw the two of you.”

She doesn’t bother hiding her amusement when Phainon visibly flinches.

Why does she seem so comfortable with this?

“Doesn’t it bother you?” he asks, his tone sharper than intended. “I roped Mydei into a pretend date.”

Evernight blinks at him, clearly confused for the first time.

“Pretend?” she echoes. “Everyone seems rather convinced it was real. Even I have to admit— it was kind of cute.”

What?

Phainon must be misunderstanding something.

“You think me going on a date with your boyfriend is cute?” he deadpans.

A long silence follows as Evernight studies him, her blood-red irises narrowing by the second.

Why is Phainon suddenly starting to feel stupid?

“…I see,” she finally says, nodding as if everything has just clicked into place. “As you may have witnessed, I’m used to stupidity. But this?”

She scoffs lightly.

“This is a whole new level.”

Phainon is certain that if he still had the same mindset he did a few moments ago, he’d be fuming. But now, he has absolutely no idea what he’s supposed to feel.

Evernight hums, tapping her chin.

“Whatever you think that big boy and I have, let’s just say our relationship is… strictly professional.”

Phainon stares at her in stunned silence, absorbing each word one by one.

“You two aren’t dating?” he repeats, voice tight, desperate for confirmation.

“No.” Evernight shakes her head slowly. “Yesterday, I was simply attending my shift.”

She pauses, and a mischievous glint flashes in her eyes.

“Can’t say the same for our big boy, though.” Her grin widens. “He dumped all his workload on us—”

“—just to go out with you.”

Phainon’s hands are trembling for an entirely different reason now. He tries to steady his voice as he continues.

“Y—you two… Work at the park?” he asks in shock, because that’s what she seems to be implying.

That means whatever he thought he understood weeks ago from her conversation with Dan Heng was completely wrong. She wasn’t talking about a secret relationship.

She was talking about work.

A job that both she and Mydei had been keeping secret.

Evernight chuckles.

“To think that poor big boy had to lose his voice just to hide his identity.” She sighs dramatically, fully aware of how her words are pulling the rug out from under Phainon’s feet. “A rather cruel fate for such a cute chimera, don’t you think?”

No.

No, no, no…

Phainon feels dizzy as the pieces finally click into place. A headache blooms behind his eyes, and he presses a hand to his forehead. Since the very beginning, he had thought Evernight’s voice sounded far too familiar—despite having never spoken to her before.

And suddenly, he’s dragged back to the park’s opening day, when Cyrene had accompanied him for a while.

The day he met Fig Stew.

The day that the black-and-red chimera, Gummy Roll—Evernight—told those kids about the curse.

So the person who had been comforting him these past weeks—who took care of his arm, who hugged him when he poured his heart out…

The friend he wanted Mydei to meet.

The one who was absent yesterday.

They were the same person.

All this time, he had been heartbroken and suffering over something that wasn’t even real. And worse—he had been venting to his own crush about losing him forever.

Evernight was being humble in calling him stupid.

“I—… just, why?” he mumbles, stunned. “Why would he hide it from me?”

Why had Mydei comforted him when they still weren’t talking? Did he know Phainon liked him and do it out of kindness? No, that was impossible. The girls would never betray his trust.

None of it adds up.

Did Mydei really have a sudden change of heart just because they met while he was dressed as Fig Stew? There’s no way. He deliberately chose to hide his identity by staying mute, even playing dumb every time Phainon brought the mascot up.

There’s more to it. There has to be.

But no matter how hard Phainon tries, he can’t grasp what that missing piece might be.

Evernight crosses her arms, a hint of pity softening her expression.

“I’m sure you will find your answer, Mr. Class Rep.” Her tone is uncharacteristically gentle, as if she were dealing with a child. “After all, chimeras have their own way of conveying their emotions—even when they can’t talk.”

When she notices Phainon's frozen state, she smiles.

“If that’s all, I’ll be taking my leave…” She walks past him, but not before adding one last remark over her shoulder. “It’s been fun… but I fear it’s about time this curse ended.”

Phainon is left speechless, alone in the hallway as the afternoon slowly bleeds into evening.

If what Evernight said is true, then Mydei isn’t just Fig Stew—he’s been keeping far more secrets than Phainon ever imagined.

He remembers how Mydei compared himself to a cat yesterday, when Phainon asked what Fig Stew’s awoo meant.

And then it hits him.

He wants to scream.

Because by Kephale—Mydei awooed at him.

Phainon buries his face in his hands. His cheeks burn so hot he thinks he might actually combust.

Is it possible to die from cuteness aggression?

Not only that—but if the metaphor really does apply to what Fig Stew was trying to convey that day… Phainon’s pulse races so fast he can hear it pounding in his ears. He might finally have an idea of the true meaning behind that small awoo.

However…

If Mydei went to such lengths to hide this from him, Phainon can’t just bring it up out of thin air. To find out what Mydei’s feelings really are, he might need to approach this the same way one would approach a feral cat—with patience and caution.

Taking a deep breath, he forces himself to calm his frantic heart as a plan slowly begins to take shape in his mind.

Well.

Two can play this game. Phainon pulls out his phone, determined to contact the other chimera experts he knows besides Mydei.

In the end, maybe he’s more inclined to play the role of Fig Stew’s crush than he had initially thought.

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei is staying home a few days to recover from his sickness. He notices Phainon is behaving oddly lately and starts wondering if their date might have anything to do with it.

Chapter Notes

No warnings for this chapter.

Being sick sucks ass. Mydei can’t remember the last time he fell ill. He had always taken good care of his health, prioritizing a balanced diet along with regular exercise. One could say that getting sick was something that should only happen to him once in a lifetime. Well, he had also never deliberately spent so much time under heavy rain and stormy winds with almost no shelter. It didn’t help that his body had burned in Phainon’s embrace as they kissed, only to cool down immediately after they parted. There was also the detail that dwelling so much on what he had done was the initial cause of his headache. If it were two years ago, Mydei would probably have buried himself in a hole and never come out. What the hell was he thinking, kissing Phainon? He knew better than anyone how this would affect their friendship, and yet he did it simply because he couldn’t bear to hear Phainon saying things that weren’t meant for his ears. Worst of all: Phainon kissed him back. It was most likely because he got lost in their pretend date. Phainon had seemed very confused until they parted ways. Who could blame him, really? It was surprising enough that he managed to keep his cool at all, still sweet enough to lend his jacket amidst everything. Mydei knew he was at fault for wishing for something unattainable; yet he couldn’t resent kissing his crush. In truth, he was glad he had been able to share his first kiss with Phainon.

Even if it never happened again, at least he had gotten a taste of what it feels like to kiss the person you like. He could only hope it hadn’t meant the same thing to Phainon; Mydei would hate to steal the guy’s first kiss over his own selfishness during a fake date. His heart stings at the thought that someone like Cyrene had everything within her reach and still chose another. The world isn’t fair. There is something Mydei does resent, though—he doesn’t want to go home. The moment he steps onto the subway is the moment everything is finally over. It’s wishful thinking to believe he could find a way to prolong their day together, since not even Oronyx answered his prayers. So, with a heavy chest, he boards, and with it, his heart shatters silently. Mydei spends the entire ride home replaying their date in his head—the day he and Phainon belonged to one another. It already almost feels like a dream. His clothes and hair are still drenched, so he refrains from taking a seat and ruining another passenger’s day later. Leaning against one of the car’s windows, he clings to the jacket draped over his shoulders. Though faint, Phainon’s scent still lingers. He can see his face in the glass reflection—a bit too flushed for his own liking, and he suspects it may not be due to the feverish state he’s feeling.

҉ ✼

After getting ready for bed, Mydei acknowledges that he’s getting sick. The insistent pulsing in his head is developing into a headache, and his throat protests at anything that goes down. His mother had been curious about his condition—her son isn’t known for being careless like that. After he insisted that the storm had caught him and his friend by surprise, she sighed and brewed some tea to soothe his raspy throat. As he sips it, Mydei stares at his phone screen. How should he approach Phainon from now on? Treating that day—and especially that kiss—as an accident induced by their roleplay doesn’t seem like a good idea. No matter how you look at it, no one would normally kiss their friend under any circumstances. Yet, Mydei doesn’t want to treat it as if it never happened either. Kremnoans are not cowards. He decides he won’t run away from it—if Phainon happens to bring it up. Mydei has no idea what he would say to justify it, but as long as he refrains from saying the real motive—that he likes Phainon far too much—there may still be hope that their friendship will last until graduation. After all, Phainon chose to kiss him back. He’s just as guilty as Mydei is. Or at least, that’s what Mydei keeps trying to convince himself of. So he fires the first shot by messaging Phainon, gauging his reaction. From the way their conversation goes, it almost feels like everything might end well, even if they never touch on the subject. But when Phainon asks if Mydei misses him, he freezes. Yes. He types it instinctively, then frowns and deletes it just as fast. I would never. It’s a blatant lie, and it shows. He doesn’t want to commit to it right now. He presses one hand to his forehead as he erases it again. His headache worsens by the minute. I miss y—… No. He can’t say it directly, but he doesn’t want to lie either. Mydei glares at his Fig Stew charm. Somehow, letting his emotions show feels easier inside a mascot suit. He sighs and rubs his temple.

When his eyes catch a glimpse of black in the corner of his room, he stops. He has already cleaned it by hand and dried it as much as he could without damaging the leather. He resents a little having washed Phainon’s scent away, but there is no way he is handing it back tomorrow in that state. It is still not fully dry and hangs from his office chair for now. Just looking at it conjures the image of Phainon in full black attire, and Mydei’s body grows hot despite the fever. He gulps, forcing his attention back to the screen. He types a message that feels far too honest, fully aware that the piece of clothing will do a very good job of keeping its owner on his mind tonight.

҉ ✼

On Monday, Mydei feels like he’s going to turn into a puddle of goo. The aching in his head grows into a full-blown headache, breathing becomes painful with such a sore throat, his nose runs endlessly, and his muscles seem purely decorative. “You’re not going to school in this state,” his mother says after taking his temperature. It’s not bad enough to truly worry her, but she still insists he stay home, rest, and eat well. Not like he can argue back, honestly. She calls the school to explain the reason for his absence. Before leaving for work, she prepares some meals early in the morning that he can heat when he feels hungry, though Mydei doubts his stomach will ask for anything in this condition. Was rain his weak spot or something? It doesn’t feel natural to be so affected by it. Phainon will probably laugh his ass off when he discovers Mydei actually got sick. Just thinking about the menace is enough—his phone vibrates almost instantly. It takes a lot of effort to send two messages informing of his condition before letting the device fall back onto the bed. There. Now he can have his fun. Mydei buries himself in his sheets, almost glad he’s being spared from seeing Phainon today. He doesn’t know how it would feel to see him back to his normal routine of crushing on Cyrene after yesterday. Luckily, the fever prevents him from thinking too much. He falls back asleep rather quickly, exhaustion winning out and pulling him into a dreamless rest.

҉ ✼

On Tuesday, Mydei feels more functional.

With only a slight fever now, his headache is manageable with some medicine, though the sore throat and runny nose remain annoyances he can’t avoid. To prevent him from spreading the flu to his classmates, he stays home again, as his mother instructed.

He can eat without feeling like his stomach is about to dissolve, and even watch some TV in the living room to pass the time.

He’s grateful for the costume, because he’s sure his face is burning the moment Vigethos steps closer and gently takes Fig Stew’s chubby paws in theirs. Mydei isn’t sure how Vigethos is supposed to mimic a kiss when their heads are so big, but he gets his answer when the white-and-gray chimera presses its plush snout against Fig Stew’s in a soft nuzzle. Mydei can’t hear the crowd’s reaction over the pounding of his own heart. It’s far from a real kiss, yet somehow it makes him feel as if he’s receiving an overwhelming amount of affection, his chest swelling with emotion. “Did it work?” he finally hears someone ask. Then that all-too-familiar chuckle carries through the air. “Of course,” Gummy Roll says, as if she’d known all along. “Any spell goes both ways. Meaning you only need one chimera to be in love for it to dispel.” Mydei doesn’t have time to dwell on her words. Because the next thing he knows, Vigethos is whispering to him—as if they weren’t standing in the middle of hundreds of people, being broadcast live, their voices echoing across the park: “That’s right. I’m sure it worked. After all—” The chimera pauses, and Mydei can hear the tremor and relief woven into its next words. “—I “awoo” you, Fig Stew.”

Chapter End Notes

I had so much fun writing this chapter!

We're almost there folks :´) Next chapter should be the last, but there are some things I want to address still so if it gets too long I may split it into two. Can't help it, I'm a yapper. Shaoji would be proud.
