chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei panics when he realizes Phainon knows about his Fig Stew persona. Unable to hide it any longer, they finally are obliged to talk about their feelings.

Chapter Notes

Hey guys, We are tipping our toes in horny teenagers territory. While this doesn't have anything explicit, keep in mind the rating of the fic. It's mostly meant for the next part.

Another important note: Yeah... it ended up getting way too long. I had to pull one or two all-nighters, but the final part is fully written. I split it mostly because I'm slow as fuck to format, and I spend an entire day per chapter proofreading with a translator open in a tab. ;')

That said, I posted this today so I could finish formatting the final part tomorrow. Hope to see you there!

Phainon knows. For fucking Titans’ sake, Phainon knows. That’s the only thought looping in Mydei’s mind as he stares in mute shock at Vigethos' oversized plush head. Under no other circumstance would that “awoo” have come up. How? How did he figure that Mydei was Fig Stew? And since when? “Is Fig Stew alright?” he hears someone ask nearby. No, he’s not. If he felt faint before, now he’s on the verge of blacking out from sheer nervousness. “Fig Stew?” Vigethos calls, stepping back just a little to give him space—like it would be possible to take a deep breath inside a mascot costume. He needs to say something. Anything. They’re in the middle of hundreds of guests, and this is supposed to be work. Even if it doesn’t feel like that anymore. “I—…” Mydei starts, but there are no words left. His mind grinds to a halt, caught on the fact that Phainon awooed at him from inside Vigethos’ costume—just like Mydei himself had done weeks ago. And just like what Mydei had wanted to convey… It feels far too much like a confession. The crowd’s murmurs grow louder, and with them, Mydei can’t bear the thundering rhythm of his heart, the heat flooding his entire body, and the tremor settling into his shoulders and legs. “I—I…” he tries again, but falters. He can sense not only Vigethos' concern—the other chimeras shift uneasily, as if worried about what is happening to him. “Did we break him?” Master Cat-Thief wonders quietly, her voice stripped of its usual playful lilt. “Wa—was it too much? Oh dear…” Butterfly Cake whispers nervously. Kremnoans are not cowards. But feeling seen like that—and having literally no room to breathe inside that costume—is not helping. He needs a break. He needs to get away somewhere quiet, even if only for a minute, to collect himself before dealing with whatever is going on. His brain then blurts out the very first thing that comes to mind. Something that can give him an excuse to retreat. “—I need to pee.” The crowd and the chimeras fall into stunned silence at the declaration. Thankfully, the costume’s narrow field of vision spares him from most of their baffled expressions, but one thing is certain. The staff restrooms are just behind one of the plaza’s buildings. And before anyone can say another word, he bolts. Mydei isn’t sure how his legs don’t give out as he reaches it in record time and slams the door behind him, locking it. There’s a faint noise from outside—the reverberation against the walls suggesting the announcer is covering for his abrupt exit. The cheerful music starts again, muffled by the restroom door. Finally alone, he rips off Fig Stew’s headpiece and lets it drop to the floor, inhaling deeply as air fills his lungs for the first time in what feels like hours. He lowers the costume to his waist, clutching his chest as he struggles to steady his heartbeat. Did Phainon and the girls set him up to be confessed to during their part-time job? Is that why they were acting so strangely? Mydei feels foolish for not realizing it sooner. And yet, he’s still trying to understand why Phainon would go so far as to awoo back at him. Had he realized it was a confession all along? If he did, then… Does that mean Phainon likes him, too? Instead of calming, his heart surges faster as his face burns. “—Mydei?” a familiar voice calls from the other side of the door, and Mydei almost jumps out of his skin. “Hey… Are you alright?” His feelings are on the verge of bursting out of his chest. What the hell is this? Shouldn’t he feel… happy? If Phainon is returning his feelings, it means they can be together. For real. However, his treacherous mind still lingers on a single thought: What about Cyrene? “Mydei—” Phainon’s voice reaches him again, strained this time. “Please. Let me in? I can explain…” Can he bear to face Phainon right now? There’s a real chance he might black out for good. He doesn’t want to—but what good would avoiding it do, when they’ll inevitably have to face each other anyway? “Mydei…” There’s a thud on the other side, as if something collided with the door. Amidst the panic and confusion, Mydei is scared. Scared that if he chooses to avoid this confrontation now, it might as well be the last chance he’ll ever have with Phainon. So, for once, he shuts out his thoughts—and listens to his heart. Slowly, he lifts his hand and unlocks the door with a soft click. It creaks open as Phainon pushes it forward almost immediately. He’s still dressed in the full costume, save for Vigethos’ headpiece, which he’s holding in one of the suit’s paws. Mydei doesn’t know what he expected, but Phainon’s expression is clouded with worry as he takes in the state the Kremnoan is in. Mydei can’t even bring himself to look at the mirror, afraid of what he might see. When Phainon finishes looking him over, he lets out a heavy exhale, his features softening slightly. He steps inside and closes the door. “Must you always run away from me?” Phainon says, a half-smile on his lips that isn’t cheerful at all.

What is he even talking about? Unable to avoid him now, Mydei struggles to find his voice, buried somewhere deep inside his own body. “…Since when did you know?” he asks in a small voice, flicking his gaze away from those impossible blue irises. “Know what?” Phainon pauses, considering. “That you were Fig Stew? Or… why you awooed at me?” Mydei wants nothing more than to crawl into a hole. He folds his arms defensively across his chest, still refusing to meet Phainon’s eyes. “Both,” he mutters. Phainon stays silent for a while, then lifts his free paw to comb his slightly damp bangs back. Mydei notices he’s without his glasses again. “Is it really important?” he asks. “We have both been hiding things from each other for a while. I thought… maybe I could come clean for once.” Mydei swallows hard, forcing down the bile rising from sheer nervousness. There’s no way out of this conversation. He tentatively lifts his gaze. “Why would you… set up such a stage for this?” “I wanted to let everyone know,” Phainon says, sweetness seeping into his tone, “but especially you, Mydei—that I like you.” A lump suddenly forms in Mydei’s throat. He wants to say it too—that he likes Phainon. Always has. But he needs to confirm that this isn’t something born from the absence of his true crush, that Phainon didn’t just get carried away by their fake date. “You like me… because of what we did at the fake date?” His voice sounds strained, even to his own ears. His chest feels unbearably heavy as he adds, “Or… because your real crush is with someone else?” Phainon’s expression shifts into one of pure confusion. “What?” Is he really going to make Mydei explain it? There’s no way he doesn’t know what he’s talking about. “Your real crush, Phainon,” Mydei snaps, annoyance bleeding into his words. “The one you keep blabbering about at every opportunity to Fig Stew—to me.” Phainon’s mouth hangs open, and Mydei takes the cue to press on.

“It’s a little too convenient that she starts dating someone else, and suddenly I’m the next option.” Bitterness seeps into his tone—he’s had enough. He refuses to think of himself as a replacement. “Since our fake date went well, maybe you thought you should give it a try? As if I—… Hmph!” Mydei’s monologue is cut short when, in the very next second, Phainon kisses him. It does a remarkably effective job of shutting him up. Phainon closes the small distance between them, pressing close and pinning him lightly against the sink with the bulk of the fluffy costume as the headpiece slips from his grip. Mydei squeezes his eyes shut on reflex, overwhelmed by the sudden intensity of it. Phainon’s insistent lips move against his, and Mydei’s mind goes blank when a tongue brushes his bottom lip in a plea for entrance. He gasps, parting his lips slightly, and Phainon swallows the sound as he licks into his mouth. The sensation sends sparks racing down Mydei’s spine, his whole body flaring with heat as he tilts his head to deepen the kiss, meeting Phainon’s tongue with his own. His legs tremble, threatening to give out—thankfully, Phainon notices and steadies him, gripping his waist before lifting him in one swift motion onto the edge of the sink. The lower half of the costume still separates them with layers of plush, but it’s enough for Phainon to settle between his legs. Oh, Titans, such a kind reminder of how strong Phainon is doing things to his already mushed brain. He can feel the smirk in their kiss as his hands slide to the back of Phainon’s head, tugging at silver strands of hair while he melts completely into the embrace. When they finally part for breath, hot puffs of air mingle between them, lips swollen and glistening. Half-lidded golden irises meet bright cerulean. “You…” Phainon breathes, his plush paws still holding Mydei firmly in place. His cheeks are flushed, chest heaving, pupils wide as he plants a quick peck on Mydei’s parted lips. It tingles. “Are the most thick-headed…” Another peck, and Mydei can’t stop the smile tugging at his lips. “…infuriating…” A third peck, and Mydei scoffs lightly, resting his arms over Phainon’s broad shoulders. “…and beautiful person in this whole world.” Last remark aside, yeah—Mydei probably deserved the rest. “What a sequence of compliments,” Mydei says, huffing out a quiet laugh, enchanted by the way Phainon gazes at him with unrestrained adoration. He absently toys with the ends of his silver hair. “Are those your pickup lines?” “They’re custom-made just for you.” Phainon grins smugly, his plush paws circling soothingly around Mydei’s waist. The sensation is oddly funny, given how soft they are. “Do you feel calmer now?” he asks quietly. Mydei nods slowly. His pulse is still racing and his whole body feels warm, but the edge of panic is finally starting to fade. “Good,” Phainon sighs softly. “I hope I got my point across. I like you, Mydei. No one else.” It almost sounds like he’s being scolded—like a stubborn child who wouldn’t listen. Yet Mydei can’t stop the way his heart skips at those words. He stays silent as Phainon continues. “I think you misunderstood something,” Phainon says, shaking his head. “But we’re not having this talk inside a toilet. Do you think you can wait until our shift ends?” That snaps Mydei out of his dazed stupor. For the Titans’ sake. They’re at their part-time job. And they were just making out in the middle of it. As embarrassment crashes down on him—holy shit, what was he thinking, bolting out of the plaza like that—he feels himself flush all the way to the tips of his ears. “Right… We should go back…” Mydei admits in a small voice, anxiety creeping in as he realizes he’ll have to slip back into Fig Stew’s character once they step outside. “Hey, relax,” Phainon says, releasing him so he can climb down from the sink and stand on his own. “I’ll be there with you.” Before Mydei can even think of a reply, Phainon adds cheerfully; “After all, we’re a couple of mascots now, too!”

҉ ✼

When the duo returns to the plaza in their full costumes, Mydei realizes that some of the guests are still lingering around. The girls had been doing some damage control, mostly keeping the more fanatical fans busy while they were gone.

“Took you two long enough!” Master Cat-Thief scolds as soon as it spots them, planting its paws on its hips. The group led by Lilgui immediately turns in their direction like a pack of hawks.

“Are you feeling better, Fig Stew?” Krenabis asks worriedly as they approach. Mydei grimaces—his panic attack must have been frightening for all of them.

“I’m fine,” he assures them. Both Krenabis’s and Butterfly Cake’s posture visibly relax.

“Fig Stew! Please, we would love an interview with you and Vigethos!” Lilgui pleads once she’s sure she can have both of their attention.

Well, there’s nowhere to run now. Mydei agrees, giving the girls some breathing room as they retreat to the staff quarters.

Once it’s just him and Phainon, Lilgui points her phone toward the duo, the crowd behind her falling into attentive silence.

“So, tell me—how did it all start? When did you two realize you liked each other?” she asks bluntly.

Mydei winces inside the suit. Are they even allowed to make shit up during a streamer’s interview?

Phainon, however, seems unfazed. He places a paw on his chin, striking a theatrical pose as if deep in thought. Since when was he so comfortable with theatrics?

“For me, ever since our first spar,” he replies smoothly, without missing a beat—surprising both Mydei and the gathered group.

“Ooh, so it was love at first sight!” someone says.

“More like love at first bite…” another adds.

They turn toward Fig Stew, who’s still recovering from the question.

Shit. He’s not being paid enough for this.

“…The same for me,” he says a bit timidly, crossing his paws over his chest.

He can hear Phainon chuckle beside him.

“I have a question too!” Lilgui’s brunette sidekick raises her hand. The duo waits for it. “If it were another chimera who lifted the curse, how would you react, Vigethos? Let’s say… Butterfly Cake, for example.”

That girl is really dead set on her ship, huh.

“Well…” Vigethos trails off, but his tone is anything but friendly. “I would never harm Butterfly Cake. But I might need some time away on a mission, just for safety.”

Mydei stares at Phainon in disbelief at how naturally that rolled off his tongue. The crowd erupts in murmurs as the brunette pales slightly.

“Uh… this reminds me of the Flame Reaver arc…” someone whispers.

“Perhaps there’s some leftover of it?” a girl wonders.

Why the fuck is he being possessive even dressed as a chimera? No, screw that. Thinking twice, it’s probably perfectly in character for Vigethos.

“Oh! Uh, such a display of loyalty to its partner!” Lilgui tries to sugarcoat it, though the threat had been crystal clear.

She goes on to ask a few more questions about how being together might affect their relationship in the cartoon, but Phainon smartly dodges them, saying they can’t reveal any upcoming plots beyond the special. Finally, Lilgui leans forward eagerly:

“Can you please say awoo to each other, then? I need it for my VOD!”

For the Titans’ sake.

He’s paying the price for running away earlier, isn’t he?

“Of course,” Vigethos says a bit too cheerfully, and Mydei can practically hear the smirk in his voice.

Turning toward him, Vigethos takes his paws again in a reprise of the play. Without a moment’s hesitation, he declares,

“Fig Stew, I awoo you.”

Mydei is grateful for the cover of the costume. His face burns as he clenches his teeth and swallows the lump in his throat. He tries to say it loudly, but it comes out as little more than a murmur.

“… I awoo you, too.”

Lilgui squeaks, and some guests echo an “aww” as they snap pictures of the moment. Great. Now, if anyone besides the mascots ever finds out about his part-time job, he’ll have an endless supply of blackmail material.

҉ ✼

Focusing on his work actually did Mydei good, pulling him out of his spiraling thoughts. Once they’re free from the fanatics, Mydei spends his time entertaining the kids, with Phainon by his side the whole time. Most just ask for pictures, though every now and then someone wants to see them holding paws or even “kissing” chimera-style for the camera. Vigethos, of course, obliges every time. Some also asked what awoo meant, and Phainon had apparently already added it to his dictionary. Each time, he answered: “It’s a word for when you like someone.” It spreads surprisingly fast, and by the end of their shift, couples and even parents are playfully saying “awoo” to each other. Mydei even finds himself wondering if it’ll reach the Kremnoan language someday. “Cinema! Simply cinema!” Mr. Reca exclaims excitedly once all the mascots are reunited at the staff headquarters. Fig Stew and Vigethos are the last to arrive. “The curse’s conclusion was a huge success with the fans!” Mydei is somewhat relieved that his panic attack didn’t affect the outcome after all. Still, he’s surprised he isn’t being scolded for it. Mr. Reca turns to Castorice. “My dear, your idea was brilliant. Getting someone to play Vigethos was the last piece we needed!” Mydei stares at her, dumbfounded. They’re all still in costume, minus the headpieces. Castorice is sitting beside Cipher, and she blushes deeply at the praise. “I—I just thought Vigethos would be a perfect fit…!” she says as if she needs to justify herself, gesturing toward the chimera in question. “A—and Phainon also offered to play it…” Mydei narrows his eyes at him. There’s definitely more to that story. Phainon lets out a soft huff of laughter. “It was fun. Thanks for having me on such short notice, Mr. Reca,” he says, wearing that charming half-smile. “Regardless! I’m sure the writers will be delighted by the outcome. We’re already trending on socials,” Mr. Reca declares, throwing both hands up as if envisioning a billboard. “I can already imagine the special ‘I Awoo You’ topping the charts later this year!” Mydei winces. Are they really going to name it like that?

“That title sounds so cute,” Hyacine giggles. “What about our payment, boss?” Cipher asks from her chair. “Credits should arrive by tomorrow. The exclusive merch will take a little longer to manufacture,” Mr. Reca clarifies. “They’ll be sent to the address you listed in the contract.” Cipher whistles. “Sounds good. Can’t wait to get my hands on it.” Castorice frowns in reproach. “You’re selling it again…” Cipher shrugs. The conversation is cut short when Mr. Reca’s phone rings. The ringtone sounds suspiciously similar to the park’s background music. Is the man really that obsessed with his job? “My, I need to take this,” he says, practically vibrating with excitement. “My dear mascots, it was a pleasure having you. The Awoo studio won’t forget your contribution!” The manager bows before hurrying out of the room, already speaking rapidly into the phone until his voice fades down the hall. Mydei still doesn’t know what to make of all this. It’s hard to believe such a silly rumor ended up adapted into his favorite show. “Well, then,” Cipher says, rising from her chair and stretching with a groan. “Work’s done. Don’t know about you guys, but I’m spent.” “Yes, and it’s getting late. We should clean up and head home,” Hyacine agrees, glancing at the clock. If Mydei remembers correctly, both she and Cipher live quite far from the park— just like Phainon. “Right…” Castorice glances guiltily at Mydei, clasping her paws together nervously. “And Mydei, I… um, sorry for overwhelming you earlier. The play was indeed my idea. Mydei sighs. He isn’t angry at her for setting it up—it wasn’t her fault she couldn’t predict how it would turn out. His retreat may not have been graceful, but it was strategic. At least he didn’t hit the ground. “It’s fine. I’m still alive.” Phainon chuckles. “Barely.” Mydei elbows him, though with the costume’s thick plush, it barely registers. Castorice visibly relaxes. The trio exchange knowing looks before saying their goodbyes and heading to the baths to change. Mydei gathers his belongings and sets the Fig Stew headpiece on the central desk. When he lifts his gaze toward the mirrors, he notices Evernight. She’s been sitting at the back the entire time, quietly scrolling on her phone. When the room falls silent, she finally looks up. “Oh. We’re already done?” Evernight asks, as if she hadn’t heard a single word since Mr. Reca’s reunion speech. Mydei has no idea why she even works as a mascot, given her immense lack of interest in the cartoon. “Yeah. We’re dismissed,” Phainon says casually. “You coming too, Evernight?” The pale pink-haired girl flicks her gaze between them before grinning. “Go ahead. I fear I’ve already meddled enough with you two,” she chuckles. “And some things certainly aren’t meant for my ears, right, Mr. Class Rep?” Phainon shifts awkwardly as he nods. Mydei squints at her. Since when have she and Phainon talked like they’ve known each other? Phainon doesn’t let him dwell on it. He wishes Evernight a good night and drags Mydei toward the staff baths. The baths are private—thank the Titans—so they take one each, and Mydei is finally relieved to be free of the stifling costume for good. He forces himself to focus on nothing but washing up, for the sake of his own heart. He doesn’t want to address their earlier talk just yet. But for Phainon, one thing seems clear: he really expects them to date. He’s confessed twice already. Meanwhile, Mydei has been so caught up in his own spiraling thoughts that he hasn’t even properly returned those feelings. Well. He will. Soon. Anxiety settles in as he changes into clean clothes and slings his bag over his shoulder. When he steps outside, he almost chokes. Phainon is already waiting for him. And he’s wearing a fucking suit. It’s deep blue and fits his form perfectly, leaving no suggestion about the defined muscles underneath it. A white dress shirt peeks out from underneath, paired with black slacks. Thankfully, there’s no tie otherwise, Mydei might think he’d stolen Mr. Reca’s wardrobe. But the black choker from their date rests snugly at his neck, like a deliberate reminder of that day. Phainon catches him staring, obviously. A smirk tugs at his lips.

“Like what you see?” Mydei wants to slap himself. Get a fucking grip, he scolds internally. Clearing his throat, he does his best to act normal about his crush looking that good. “What’s the occasion?” he asks as casually as he can manage—poorly. “Well,” Phainon begins, a mischievous glint in his eyes, “today’s a special day. There’s someone I’ve been wanting to ask out for a long time.” Mydei can already feel his insides flutter, warmth creeping up his chest. He decides to humor him, crossing his arms. “And who’s that?” Phainon rolls his eyes, though a soft laugh escapes him. “I’ll show you. Come with me?” He extends a hand. Without a second thought, Mydei takes it.

҉ ✼

“Mnestia’s Tunnel?” Mydei reads the big neon sign aloud, baffled. Phainon has guided them to one of the park’s attractions. There was nothing in the contract about mascots being allowed to ride after their shifts, since they were technically still inside the park—but Mydei had never even considered it. Usually, he was far too exhausted to think about rides once he got out of costume. “Yeah. Can we ride it?” Phainon asks in an expectant tone, eyes sparkling as if it’s the most entertaining thing ever. The attraction, as the name suggests, is aimed at couples. It’s a slow ride along a calm river through a dimly lit track themed around Cerce and Mnestia’s love—passing through a recreation of the Titan of Wisdom’s tree trunks, decorated with Mnestia’s golden nymphs to create an intimate ambience. It’s one of the few attractions that stays open until nightfall. Does Phainon want to ride it that much with him? The thought makes Mydei a little nervous, but he doesn’t see a reason to refuse. They’re… well, practically an official couple now. Mydei gives a small nod, and Phainon smiles brightly as he pulls them toward the empty queue. It’s close to park closing time, but there’s still enough room for one last ride. The employee in charge doesn’t look thrilled, yet dutifully guides them to an empty cart. They take their seats on the leather bench, a bit too small for two tall, grown teens. Mydei slides his bag under the seat as they wait for the ride to start. Their shoulders and thighs touch in the secluded cart, their hands still linked. As expected, it moves slowly. Soft ambient music plays while the track carries them up the river, golden nymphs projected along the way, their glow illuminating the dim tunnel. Mydei has to admit—it’s cozy. “Mydei,” Phainon calls, almost startling him. His thumb rubs gently over Mydei’s palm, a quiet gesture meant to keep him calm. “About earlier…” He trails off, seemingly unsure how to continue. His bright blue eyes search Mydei’s golden irises as he speaks with measured caution. “What did you mean… about my real crush?” Mydei’s jaw tightens. He expected the question, but answering it is an entirely different matter. Still, even if he wanted to run, there’s nowhere to escape unless he’s willing to dive into the river. And he already learned his lesson after going home in drenched clothes last week. Still… it shouldn’t be news to Phainon. So why does he feel so hesitant?

His gaze drops to their linked palms. Mydei remembers how he once thought his crush’s hand was meant for Cyrene’s alone. But now, looking at them together like this, fingers laced so naturally… it feels almost like a perfect fit His chest tightens at the thought. “I was talking about her,” Mydei says quietly, the words coming out small and defeated. He’d spent far too long resenting what she could have while he couldn’t. “…Cyrene.” A beat of silence. Phainon’s thumb stills, as if struck by some sudden revelation. After what feels like minutes, he finally echoes: “Cyrene?” Mydei nods slowly, the familiar bitterness resurfacing at the mere mention of her. “You thought I had a crush… on Cyrene?” Phainon repeats, incredulous. Mydei grows annoyed and turns his gaze to the glowing scenery instead. “You’re always close to her. You two seemed… happy together. Since the very first day,” Mydei vents, lost in the memory of the pink-haired girl’s arrival. “And… one day, you told Fig Stew you would never give up on your crush. That was right after she showed up dating that girl.” He can feel Phainon’s stare piercing through him. “Oh…” Phainon finally says, his brilliant reply sounding more bewildered than anything else. The surprise in his tone makes Mydei wonder why it shocks him so much. “Titans,” Phainon says slowly, his voice wrecked. “Mydei… you assumed I had a crush on Cyrene all this time?” Is it so fucking hard to understand? “Are you denying it?” Mydei snarls. It’s hard to believe otherwise, not after everything he’s seen day after day at school. “Mydei, look at me.” Phainon lifts his free hand, cupping Mydei’s chin and gently guiding his face toward him. There’s pain written all over his expression, and Mydei can’t fathom why. Phainon takes a deep breath, rolling the words out with heartfelt honesty. “Cyrene is a very dear friend to me. But that’s all. I’ve never had any romantic interest in her. All she’s done these past years is support me—encouraging me to ask you out.” What.

It doesn’t make sense. And yet… it doesn’t sound like a lie. If that’s true… “Then… who…?” Mydei trails off, as if the ground beneath him has vanished Who had Phainon been talking about all this time? If not Cyrene, then who had he been suffering over? Phainon lets go of his hand, reaching instead into his pocket and pulling out his phone. “I’m afraid you won’t believe me unless I show you,” he says, already opening his gallery. From his position, Mydei can’t help catching glimpses of the screen. He doesn’t want to pry into Phainon’s privacy—but that’s hard when it’s right there. The most recent photos are from their date. Phainon scrolls quickly, images blurring past until the timestamp at the top reads: two years ago. Mydei starts to feel faint again, but for an entirely different reason. When Phainon taps the photo and expands it to full view, Mydei stops breathing. Phainon draws the device closer to his face as he speaks, voice fraying at the edges. “This person is my real crush.” The photo shows a younger Phainon, his expression utterly radiant—cheeks faintly flushed, smile bright, as if he were the luckiest person alive. Leaning against his shoulder, fast asleep, is another boy: golden bangs dipped in red framing his face softly as Phainon holds him close at his side. Cherry petals scatter across the desk above their tutoring notes, frozen in the image like a memory of spring. Mydei’s eyes burn as he stares at the picture—at the sweet memory it summons. “It has always been you, Mydei. Only you,” Phainon mutters, his voice trembling. Mydei can’t stop the small sob that escapes him as his vision blurs. Mydei lifts his gaze to Phainon, unable to look at the picture anymore—it pierces straight through his heart. Phainon’s deep blue irises are glassy, though a small smile still clings stubbornly to his face. Shame presses down heavier than ever. Shame for assuming something that never existed, simply because he couldn’t believe that someone like Phainon—so sweet, so gentle—could ever feel the same way about him. He can’t even begin to understand what could have led someone so warm to look at him with such tenderness. In the end, the person who had everything within reach and still denied it wasn’t Cyrene. It was himself. “W—why…” he manages through the lump in his throat, the sobs refusing to stop. He lifts a hand to rub at his eyes, fully aware that the tears are already spilling freely. Drawing in a shaky breath, he forces himself to continue. “Why… why didn’t you ever say anything?” Phainon leans forward until their foreheads touch. He lets the phone rest against his thigh and cups Mydei’s cheek, carefully brushing away the tears as his brows knit together. “I thought you hated me,” he says softly—and the words cut deeper than anything else could. “You were always running from me. Like my presence bothered you.” Mydei squeezes his eyes shut, shame pressing down harder in his chest. His behavior must have hurt Phainon continuously, and for so long. He thought he was protecting his own heart, but in truth, he’d been driving Phainon away—cutting him with every retreat, every cold shoulder. His chest aches as he recalls each flicker of pain he’d seen in Phainon’s features. It had been because of him. “I didn’t hate you,” Mydei whispers at last, his voice breaking. “I was just… scared. I didn’t think I was someone you could ever choose.” Phainon exhales shakily, his thumb still warm against Mydei’s cheek. “I already did,” he says. “A long time ago.” The words sink into Mydei like a lifeline. “I’m sorry…” he sniffles. “Don’t be,” Phainon whispers, his breath warm against Mydei’s skin. “As much as you pushed me away, you—well, Fig Stew—brought us closer again. If anything, I’m grateful.” Mydei’s golden irises lift to meet cerulean blue. Phainon’s hand finds his, squeezing gently to ground him. With a soft exhale, he continues: “Fig Stew gave me the courage to do this.” His fingers trace down Mydei’s cheek, hovering just above his bottom lip, as if memorizing every detail. “So, let me ask, just this once…” Mydei’s heart soars in anticipation as Phainon leans back slightly, taking a deep breath like he’s finally releasing a weight he’s carried for years. “Mydeimos… Will you be my boyfriend?” Mydei’s vision must be playing tricks on him. Surrounded by glowing golden nymphs, the light reflecting in Phainon’s expectant blue irises is breathtaking. The dim glow gives him an almost angelic radiance. As his breath catches and his heart yearns, Mydei can’t contain what he’s held back for so long. Here, with Phainon’s feelings laid bare—just as Fig Stew had once done—Mydei finally finds the voice that had been locked away in the depths of his heart, bound by a self-inflicted curse. And like a broken spell, he whispers: “Yes,” he says shakily. If tears are still flowing down, they’re not from shame anymore. Because for once, he loses himself in the fullness of his own feelings as he says: “I like you, Phainon.” The reaction is immediate. Phainon’s mouth falls open, as if he’s been struck speechless. For a heartbeat, he can only stare, trying to process the words. And then his cheeks flush, his glassy eyes finally giving in—like Mydei’s, his tears are born of happiness. His lips curve into a smile so radiant it makes Mydei’s chest lurch with adoration. As the track nears its end, they close the small distance between them. The kiss they share is gentle and unhurried, so tender it sets their hearts fluttering like Mnestia’s nymphs themselves—a silent blessing. The warmth that had sprouted two years ago is finally allowed to bloom, unfolding into a delicate blossom.

҉ ✼

The Mnestia’s Tunnel employee looked rather curious about why the duo left the ride with visibly puffy eyes. Somewhere along the way, they managed to stop the tears, but the same can’t be said for Mydei’s racing pulse as he walks to the park’s station, hand in hand with his boyfriend. The thought alone makes him giddy. He knows he still has much to reflect on—he can’t even begin to imagine how to make up for two years lost to his own choices. But right now, he is happy. And nothing can take that away. “Say, Mydei…” Phainon says once they reach the station. He seems a bit nervous as he glances at the subway itinerary, adjusting his collar. “Would you like to have dinner at my house?” Mydei’s thoughts freeze. He stares at Phainon, dumbfounded. “We’ve been together for ten minutes, and you’re already inviting me over?” he says flatly, making Phainon wince. “It’s nothing like that,” he says quickly, frustration clear as he waves his free hand in denial. Mydei can’t resist the smirk tugging at his lips. “Really? Shame,” he teases, fully aware of the implication of his words. Phainon’s face flushes red as he frowns back at the Kremnoan. “My mom wanted me to invite you over since last week,” he explains. “She’s very eager to meet you.” Mydei blinks, studying him for a moment. Well, he supposes he will meet Phainon’s parents sooner or later. He just doesn’t expect it to be this soon. But if you take into account how much time they’ve already lost, maybe it isn’t that strange. Perhaps he can start compensating by accepting it. It certainly has nothing to do with him not wanting to leave Phainon’s side. “Sure,” he agrees with a soft sigh, pulling out his phone. “I’ll just let my mother know I’ll be arriving late.” Phainon stops him with a hand hovering over the screen, his tone decisive. “I live almost an hour away, Mydei. If you’re coming home with me, you’re staying there until tomorrow.” Oh. Now it’s Mydei’s turn to feel flustered. He swallows, trying to come to terms with the fact that this is, indeed, an invitation to sleep over. It’s fine. He can totally sleep in the same house as Phainon without being weird about it. His parents are there, too. And he surely must have a guest room or a sofa in the living room. Nothing can go wrong, right? “Okay…” he mutters, still a bit bewildered as Phainon finally lets his phone go, satisfaction radiating from him. They shift from the subway station to the bus stop. After a few minutes, they board, and Phainon insists on paying for the ride until Mydei rolls his eyes and lets him have his fun. Once the engine starts, they’re already seated at the back, with Mydei by the window. There’s still a long way to go, so he takes the opportunity to bring up a few things he’s been curious about, hoping to soothe his restlessness at the thought of spending the night. “How did you get Vigethos’ character so well?” Mydei asks. The question has been lingering at the back of his mind since Phainon appeared dressed as the chimera. If not for the initial shock of hearing his voice, he would have been impressed by the portrayal. Phainon sheepishly scratches the back of his neck. “Oh, I did a bit of research at home,” he explains. “I watched some scenes and trailers. I also read their profile on the official site…” Mydei hums. He’s impressed that Phainon managed to grasp so much from just that, but he’s not about to admit it out loud. Instead, he says, “Castorice did well choosing them for you.” Phainon flicks his gaze between the view outside and Mydei in an almost guilty manner. Mydei tilts his head in silent question. “Well, uh… It’s actually me who chose Vigethos,” he admits, and at first Mydei doesn’t understand why that would be so shocking. That’s until Phainon adds, “I asked Castorice to scout which chimera you thought Fig Stew has a crush on. I would play any chimera you chose.” Oh. So that’s why Castorice and Cipher were all over the place when they visited him. Mydei averts his gaze, feeling funny. That is… unexpectedly cute. He absent-mindedly plays with his braid to distract himself. “Then all that setup came from you?” he asks.

“Most of it. I reached out to Castorice when I decided I wanted to confess to you as Fig Stew’s crush,” Phainon replies. “She did suggest doing it through a play, though. After asking Mr. Reca about it, he seemed thrilled by the idea and included me as a mascot.” Phainon shifts in his seat a little as he continues. “I have to admit I was kind of surprised when Castorice revealed that not only she, but also Cipher and Hyacine, were mascots. I felt a bit stupid for not noticing it sooner.” “So you were off the charts this week because…” he trails off. Phainon nods, offering him a half-smile. “I was researching the character and practicing the script with the girls,” he says softly. “I also had to go to the park a few times during the week to take measurements for the costume. They got it ready almost at the last minute.” Mydei blinks a few times as he pieces it together. Then he looks back at him, a sudden realization dawning. “How did you know Evernight?” he asks, remembering how Phainon had referred to her so casually before. They must have told her about the play sometime during the week, but Mydei is certain it wasn’t at school. To his surprise, Phainon hesitates, his body tensing. “Uh—” He scratches his chin, suddenly finding the bus aisle very interesting to stare at. Mydei arches an eyebrow, waiting. “When you were sick, I sought her out… about you.” “What?” Mydei asks, not grasping what he means. Phainon hunches forward, elbows on his knees, hiding his face in his hands. “I… thought you two were dating,” he says in a tight voice. Mydei stares at him, wide-eyed, trying to process the words. “…What?” he repeats, completely lost. Phainon takes a deep breath, sliding his hands down from his face and combing his bangs back. “You were being all secretive with her at school. I thought—” His jaw tightens as he stops himself, brows creasing. Just the mention of it seems to make him uneasy. “It was easier to imagine than the two of you being park mascots, honestly.” Mydei stares at him in silence, bewildered. Phainon’s usual gentle expression is shadowed by something darker—the same flicker that had crossed his face briefly during their date. Mydei thinks back on it, on how he had kept Phainon at a distance while suddenly seeking out the pale pink-haired girl, seemingly out of the blue. The more he dwells on it, the heavier the guilt gnaws at him. So that day Phainon went to the park, heartbroken… “You were jealous of her,” he concludes aloud, his chest feeling heavy. Phainon lifts his gaze, a pained smile tugging at his lips. “I guess we’re both fools.” Mydei’s heart stings. How could he have been so blind all this time? His friends were right— he really had left his brain back at Kremnos. Is it truly all right for him to allow himself to be happy after making Phainon suffer so much? His shoulders draw inward as he chews on his bottom lip. “It’s all my fault…” he murmurs, his voice nearly drowned out by the bus’s engine. “Hey,” Phainon’s soothing tone cuts through as he inches a little closer, their shoulders brushing while he cups Mydei’s cheek. Though Mydei flinches out of reflex, the touch is warm, and he finds himself leaning into it. “It doesn’t matter anymore. We’re together, Mydei. I would slay a thousand witches and dress as a chimera every single day if it meant I could be by your side.” The image makes Mydei’s lips curve up involuntarily. Silly as it is, it makes him feel cherished. Phainon’s cerulean eyes shine again, though a tender emotion lingers in their depths. Titans, Mydei wants to kiss him. He refrains, though, afraid he won’t want to stop on just that. And there are plenty of passengers around. Instead, he scoffs lightly. “That sounds like a lot of effort…” Phainon only shrugs, a mischievous glint flashing in his eyes as he grins. “Yeah,” he says, and the way he looks at Mydei has him squirming a little in his seat. It seems Mydei isn’t the only one holding back. Phainon takes his hand and presses a kiss to the back of his knuckles. “But you’re worth the effort.” By Nikador, I’m not surviving until tomorrow. Mydei thinks as warmth rushes to his face, unsure whether being able to openly flirt like this is a blessing or a curse.

҉ ✼

Mydei is surprised by how warmly he’s welcomed at Phainon’s house. Not even a second after Phainon opens the door, his mother is already on her way to greet them, gasping when her cerulean eyes land on the Kremnoan. The woman is petite, having to crane her neck slightly to look up at them.

“Oh my Kephale, you’re gorgeous,” she says, clapping a hand over her mouth in shock, and Phainon shifts awkwardly beside him.

“Mom…” he pleads, but she only frowns at him before ushering them inside.

Mydei watches the scene unfold, amused. He’s glad to have made a good first impression, even if it’s only because of his looks. Not everyone in Okhema would refer to a Kremnoan with so many piercings and tattoos as gorgeous first and foremost.

Well, like mother, like son.

When they enter the dining room, a delicious smell hangs in the air, making Mydei’s stomach growl. The longer trip means it’s already past his usual dinner time. Phainon’s father sits at the head of the table, regarding the trio. His fluffy white hair matches his son’s. Unlike Phainon’s mother, however, he doesn’t look particularly thrilled by Mydei’s presence.

“Dad, Mom… this is my boyfriend, Mydeimos,” Phainon says, a hint of pride in his voice as he rests a hand at the small of Mydei’s back.

Nervousness surges through him, and he fights the flush creeping up his cheeks at being introduced so openly.

“Pleasure to meet you…” he says stiffly. Phainon’s father rises and extends a hand, which Mydei takes almost on autopilot.

“Strong grip,” he comments, apparently satisfied before letting go. “I’m Hieronymus. Nice to meet ya, kid.”

He pauses, then sits back with a low growl. “Thanks for putting up with my son. He can be a handful sometimes.”

“Dad!” Phainon whines, blushing in embarrassment as his father tsks. Mydei can’t hold back a chuckle.

“And I’m Audata. Welcome, dear,” Phainon’s mother says warmly, stepping forward to wrap him in a hug. The gesture catches Mydei off guard, leaving him frozen until she pulls back. “Don’t be shy, take a seat. I’ll have dinner ready in just a minute.”

He nods timidly as she heads back to the kitchen.

One thing is clear: this place is far livelier than his own home. Don’t get him wrong—Mydei loves his mother, and she’s wonderful to him. But she’s almost always at work, coming home only at night, when she isn’t away on business trips that last for days. And when he visited his father… well, it was like stepping into a museum. A mansion full of expensive furniture and almost no human warmth.

Most of Mydei’s hesitation about the dinner melts away once they sit at the table. He quickly learns that Hieronymus is rather hard-headed, rolling his eyes every time Audata gushes about how her son brought home such a beautiful young man. Audata, on the other hand, wastes no time inviting him over again, insisting that the house is always open to him.

Her food is delicious. She explains that it’s a family recipe from when they still lived in Aedes Elysae, and Mydei commits it to memory as she describes the ingredients. When Phainon brings up that Mydei is an amazing cook himself, it’s almost as if her eyes light up with glee.

“Hiero, he’s perfect,” she sighs dreamily, her eyes misting as her husband groans.

“Get a hold woman, stop drooling over your son’s boyfriend.”

Audata turns to him, her expression shifting into a smug grin.

“Aw, are you jealous?” she teases, poking his arm. “You know you’re still number one in my heart, darling.”

“Tsk,” Hieronymus snorts, taking a mouthful of food all at once. Mydei notices the faint hint of red on his face and can’t hide his smile. He imagines it must be nice to grow old with your partner and still be so clearly in love with each other.

Mydei’s gaze shifts to his side almost unconsciously. His heart skips a beat when he notices Phainon is already watching him with an unreadable expression.

“What?” he whispers, since his parents are still lost in their own little world.

Phainon’s lips curve up slightly, though he remains silent. Mydei nearly jolts when he feels Phainon’s hand settle over his thigh beneath the table, giving it a light squeeze in a gesture that says only one thing:

Mine.

For Titan’s sake, he can’t possibly be jealous of his own mother… can he? Maybe Mydei has underestimated just how possessive his boyfriend can be.

“Nothing,” Phainon finally replies, feigning innocence as he drinks in Mydei’s bewildered look. Mydei tries to ignore it and focus on his plate, but the scoundrel keeps his hand there, tracing small circles against his thigh even when his mother turns her attention back to them.

Thankfully, Mydei’s rising panic keeps things from escalating any further. He makes a mental note to scold Phainon about it later, but manages to keep his composure throughout dinner.

When he offers to wash the dishes, Audata insists on treating their guest fully tonight. Still a little flustered, Phainon seizes the chance to show him where he’ll be sleeping, while his parents wish them a good night.

And just like that, Mydei forgets he’s supposed to stay mad when Phainon leads him into his own room.

“You can take the bed. We’ve got a spare mattress,” Phainon says casually as Mydei lingers at the doorway. The room is on the first floor—small and cozy, with a large study desk neatly organized in the corner.

“… I can sleep on the couch,” Mydei suggests.

Phainon is already pulling sheets from his wardrobe. He peeks through the door, blinking at his boyfriend through his glasses—the first thing he grabbed after coming in.

“Huh? No way,” Phainon disagrees with a frown. “Besides, my dad likes watching TV in the living room until he falls asleep. Mom has to drag him to bed almost every night.”

Titans spare me.

Seeing him still hovering at the door, Phainon sets the sheets on the bed and steps closer.

“Mydei… are you uncomfortable sharing a room with me?” he asks gently, without any edge to his voice.

Mydei swallows. It feels a little silly, but he can’t help being nervous. They’ve been officially dating for less than a day; his heart can only take so much at once.

“… I’m fine,” he lies. Phainon studies him for a moment.

“We’re both tired from work. Don’t overthink it, let’s just rest,” he says with a soft sigh, rolling his shoulders.

Rich, coming from someone who had very clearly tried to stir him up during dinner. Maybe he’s decided to be considerate for once.

Regardless, now that he’s said it, Mydei realizes just how exhausted he is from their part-time job. He had pushed the fatigue to the back of his mind with everything else that had happened earlier. His eyes flick between the bed and Phainon before he finally agrees.

“Okay. But I’ll take the spare mattress,” he says firmly.

Phainon tilts his head with muted curiosity but doesn’t press. He drags the spare mattress over, and Mydei helps him set it up. Luckily, Mydei has his own hygiene items tucked in his bag, so he’s able to brush his teeth and get ready for bed without trouble.

Phainon offers him sleep clothes, but he refuses. The outfit he’s wearing is comfortable enough—and besides, there’s no way he’ll get any rest if he’s wrapped in Phainon’s sweet scent all night in those conditions. It already lingers in the room, and it’s the main reason he’s avoiding the bed.

Phainon changes a little later, now dressed in a loose blue shirt and sleeping shorts. He sits at the edge of his bed, watching Mydei from above as he pulls the sheets over himself.

“Were my parents too much?” he asks.

“They were fine,” Mydei scoffs, fluffing his pillow. “Unlike their son, they’re cute.”

Phainon pouts.

“Hey, I’m cute too…”

Mydei lets out a small laugh. It’s a ridiculous statement coming from a grown-ass teen. Even if he agrees, it’s not something he’s about to admit.

He’s just starting to relax under the covers when Phainon speaks again.

“Mydei, I was thinking…”

Mydei shuts his eyes with a sigh. It’s already hard enough to focus on sleeping under these circumstances, and his boyfriend isn’t making it any easier. He hums softly, signaling that he’s listening. “We should fulfill that promise we made two years ago…” Phainon says, his voice hesitant. “You know, about watching The Awoo Firm together.”

The words make Mydei halt mid-breath. He opens his eyes, meeting Phainon’s expectant gaze.

“Why bring that up now?” he asks quietly, brows lifting.

“Well…” Phainon scratches his chin, his tone softening. “You love that cartoon enough to dress as one of its characters. I want to learn more about it… and about you.”

While Mydei stares at him in bewilderment, Phainon adds sheepishly,

“And Vigethos seems like a cool character. That sword is dope.”

The tender comment from before is quickly derailed, and Mydei rolls his eyes.

“Seems like someone already has a favorite,” he teases.

“No way, my favorite is still Fig Stew,” Phainon replies playfully. “They’re the only chimera I would kiss.”

Mydei throws his pillow at him, but Phainon laughs, catching it effortlessly.

“Just get to sleep already, dumbass.”

“Alright, alright…” Phainon chuckles, handing the pillow back before turning off the light. “Have a good night, your highness.”

“’Night.” Mydei says, turning onto his side as his thoughts linger on the offer. He would gladly watch his favorite cartoon with his boyfriend anytime. It was what had kept him so eager for the day it would happen two years ago. He’s surprised to find the feeling still alive, thinking he had buried it deep enough never to resurface. That small flutter over something so mundane.

But sleep refuses to come. Maybe it’s because it’s been so long since he last stayed over, or maybe the floor feels too cool beneath the mattress. Even under the sheets, the chill seeps in.

He doesn’t know how much time has passed since the lights went out. Only a sliver of moonlight filters through the curtains, not enough to tell if Phainon is asleep. His breathing is steady, a sign that at least he must have been dozing off.

Mydei turns again, memories stirring. He recalls the day he fell asleep on Phainon. If only he’d had the courage not to run off afterward—would things have been different? If he had been braver to ask about his thoughts on his relationship with Cyrene… Or if he had allowed himself to think he was worthy of Phainon’s affections…

Those last two years could have unfolded in an entirely different way.

He wants to be happy and forget about everything else, but there’s still an insistent sting in his heart. One that slowly reminds him of how little time they will have to enjoy together before they have to part ways.

Only five months until graduation. And then it’s over. Phainon had told him back when they were still in tutoring that his goal was to go to Jarilo to attend the Belobog Institute’s engineering program. That’s the reason he studies so hard and maintains such high grades. But… it’s literally on the other side of the planet. Even if they try to stay in touch, the different time zones combined with the immense physical distance are bound to drift them apart. His own dream of coming back to Kremnos, studying gastronomy, and opening his own business now seems a little dull.

The sting deepens into a pulsing ache as the cold settles in. It feels like too much, like he should know better than to suffer over a fleeting relationship in his youth.

And yet, he does.

Because he knows there isn’t a single person on the planet he could ever imagine awooing to instead of Phainon.

Mydei sits up on the mattress, the sheets slipping from his shoulders. He glances toward the bed, catching only the faint silhouette in the darkness. His body moves before his mind can catch up.

He climbs onto the bed, finds the edge of Phainon’s sheets, and slips beneath them.

“Huh…? My—” Phainon’s voice is slightly raspy, a hint that he’s been fast asleep. He’s still half-unaware of what’s happening when Mydei shifts closer and buries his face against his chest.

“Not a word about this,” he mumbles, voice muffled against Phainon’s sleepshirt, his pulse quickening in a mix of embarrassment and fear of what he might say. His fists clutch the fabric of his boyfriend’s shirt tightly. There’s no plush armor to shield him, no excuse for exposing his heart so openly. It should be alright, though—they’re in a relationship now, right?

He feels Phainon stir as he becomes aware of their position. Mydei half expects teasing, but instead Phainon’s arm slides beneath his side, pulling him close.

“…You’re freezing,” he murmurs, worry edging his voice as he wakes a little more. His other hand finds Mydei’s hair, combing through the wild bangs in gentle strokes.

Mydei replies with a sound that’s half agreement, half grunt. He focuses on the steady rise and fall of Phainon’s chest, his heartbeat a steadfast rhythm against his ear. On the overwhelming, familiar scent of his skin and clothes that wraps around him like a second blanket.

Phainon’s warmth seeps into him; his embrace begins to thaw the cold dread that had settled in his bones.

I like you, he thinks. I don’t want to lose you.

Phainon remains silent as instructed, and when he kisses the top of Mydei’s head, Mydei lets out a small, surrendering breath, his muscles going slack. It feels cozy—so cozy he never wants to get up. He lifts his face only slightly, enough not to suffocate against Phainon’s sleep shirt. His cheek rests against his ribcage, and somehow it feels nicer than the pillow from before. His fists unclench, hands settling lightly over his boyfriend’s body.

Gazing at the dark wall, he sighs in quiet contentment.

“…Talk about something nerdy,” he mutters.

Phainon chuckles, his chest vibrating beneath Mydei’s cheek.

“Really?”

Mydei stays quiet. He doesn’t want to explain that he likes being lulled to sleep by his voice. He almost doesn't believe Phainon will oblige until he hears a soft, considering hum.

“Did you know a dromas scale color can change based on their diet?” he begins. Mydei can’t contain the soft hum that slips out, urging him on. Phainon’s voice trembles as if he’s smiling when he continues. "Though they prefer redsoil, they can digest almost any regular food. For instance, if you feed them enough golden apples, they might eventually develop golden scales. Mr. Anaxagoras is fascinated by it; he even offered to sponsor the dromas at the zoo to study the possibilities—"

Mydei has to admit that mentioning Mr. Anaxagoras is a brilliant strategy for inducing sleep. He feels his eyelids growing heavy as Phainon keeps talking about dromas scales pigmentation, the gentle combing through his hair never ceasing until, finally, he is freed from his own thoughts.

Chapter End Notes

Before grabbing your pitchfork, please note that I included the "Happy Ending" tag. ><

There was literally no other place I could cut this part. Sorry.

I felt like I couldn't finish this properly without addressing the future of their relationship regarding graduation. Don't worry, the ending is near and it's very sweet. Pinky promise!

See you tomorrow ❤

Chapter Summary

Have you ever wondered what 'awoo' truly means?

Chapter Notes

Hey guys :) As promised, here is the last part.

I hope you have fun!

That morning, Mydei learns that both he and Phainon are messy sleepers. When they wake, Phainon has half his body dangling off the edge of the bed, while Mydei is completely tangled in the sheets, face buried against his chest, one arm flung above Phainon’s head. He might have been more embarrassed about the little trail of drool on his boyfriend’s shirt if not for the fact that Phainon woke with strands of Mydei’s hair stuck in his mouth. Sure, the single bed being far too cramped for two didn’t help, but Mydei wonders how it would go if they ever shared beds frequently—not that he wants to, of course. It’s just a passing thought. Hm… perhaps he should start to tie his hair before sleeping, just in case. The morning sheds light on another problem: They’re about to head to school, and Mydei realizes he doesn’t have his uniform with him. With no other choice, he accepts the spare Phainon proudly insisted on offering. Though they’re about the same size, the shirt fits a bit on the tighter side around his chest. Phainon studies him with a hand on his jaw, frowning. “Actually, maybe we should ditch today…”

“HKS, shut up and get ready,” Mydei retorts. He’s not about to skip school over his boyfriend’s over-the-top possessiveness, even if he secretly enjoys the attention. They share breakfast before heading to the bus stop, and Mydei has to promise Audata he’ll visit again soon. Watching her beam, he can’t help but think he’s found the source of Phainon’s clinginess. Since Phainon usually arrives at school early, they end up with plenty of free time before classes begin. They settle into the back of their classroom, sharing Mydei’s earbuds while watching videos on his phone and swapping songs they like on the Memify app. “You like Luofu pop?” Mydei asks with arched brows when Phainon chooses the next track. Five years ago, he and Phainon moved in together to attend Kremnos University. He insisted that Mydei entrust the project to him. They moved to a bigger apartment closer to the city center and got down to planning their next steps. The Fig Stew charm is still there, but it has company now—Mydei paid a small fortune to give Phainon the same limited edition charm of Vigethos. Their threads are a little tangled, as if fate itself bound them together.
